chapters.title: Chapter 1: Betrayal and Transmigration
chapters.content:
Chapter 1: Chapter 1: Betrayal and Transmigration
Pat! Pat! Pat!
The soft rhythm of raindrops echoed across the battlefield, falling from the ash-colored sky like silent tears.
The cold touch of the rain soaked into the cracked soil, mixing with the scattered blood around it.
And there, lying motionless on the muddy ground, was Stark.
His eyes remained open, fixed on the sky above.
Dark clouds rolled across the heavens, heavy and unrelenting, yet Stark’s expression stayed still.
No tears. No screams. Just the quiet, hollow stare of someone who had lost everything.
A few glowing panels hovered above him, flickering like dying embers.
[Your health is in critical condition.]
[The "Judgment Battlefield" is an instant death zone. You cannot revive.]
The warning was brutal, direct, and final.
Stark read the text but barely reacted. His body was numb, completely severed from pain.
Not by choice. He couldn’t feel his arms or legs for a simple reason: they were gone.
His limbs had been violently cut off, left somewhere behind on the ravaged field of the [Judgment Battlefield].
And all he could do now was stare into the clouds above, waiting for the end.
Footsteps squished softly through the wet earth.
Voices followed, familiar ones, sharp against the silence.
"Hell yeah," a man laughed, his tone smug and triumphant, "That was perfect. We’re going to be rich."
Stark didn’t bother turning his head to look.
He knew the voice. He knew them both.
"I know, right~?" a woman added with a joyful, singsong tone, "We’ll never have to worry about anything again! This is it. We made it!"
Max and Seren. His best friends. Or rather, the people he thought were his best friends.
Ten years of friendship. Ten years of surviving side-by-side.
Ten years of laughter, hardship, training, and risking their lives in a world that had been torn apart by chaos.
And now, they stood behind him, laughing. Triumphant. While he bled out on the ground.
"We got the artifact," Max said, breathless with excitement, "We’re good."
"To our new lives!" Seren giggled like a schoolgirl, drunk on greed and euphoria, "Let’s go already!"
"What about him?" Max asked casually, like he was pointing at a broken piece of furniture, "Do we... finish him off?"
Stark continued to lie there, still unmoving.
He didn’t flinch, didn’t cry out, didn’t speak.
The pain in his body was distant now. Fading.
Only the weight in his chest remained.
"No need," Seren replied, a cruel smile in her voice, "Look at him. He’s already finished. It’s just a matter of time before the monsters come and clean it up for us."
And with that, they turned their backs on him.
The light of a portal opened a few feet away, shimmering gold and green, its surface rippling like water.
They stepped through it without hesitation, not sparing him another glance.
Then the portal closed. Silence returned.
Stark remained where he was, lying in the rain. Alone.
For a long moment, he said nothing. Just listened to the storm around him.
His mind wandered.
Ten years ago, the world had changed.
A game called [Eternal Soul], or the [Eternal] game in short, had descended upon Earth, merging its unnatural rules and beings with the human world.
Earth’s foundation was forever altered.
And a while after its arrival, monsters began spilling into cities, slaughtering people by the thousands.
At first, no one understood what [Eternal Soul] was.
It was like something out of a twisted video game, complete with stats, levels, and power-ups.
And yet, it was real. Too real. Eventually, it was confirmed.
[Eternal Soul] was an entirely separate dimension, and only those brave, or desperate, enough to enter it and survive could gain the power needed to fight back.
Stark had been one of them.
Like countless others, he trained, fought, and adapted.
Over time, humanity learned how to coexist with the dangerous new reality.
People could enter [Eternal Soul] to grow stronger and earn power, which they could use to make a name for themselves in this new civilization.
Stark’s journey, like so many others, began with hope and desperation.
He wanted to fight for survival, to protect what mattered.
And through it all, Max and Seren were there, his partners, his friends, his family.
He trusted them. And that trust had brought him here... to this godforsaken place.
"Heh," he let out, "I was stupid."
[Judgment Battlefield]
[Description: A hidden realm buried deep within "Eternal Soul".]
[Lives loss rate: Instant Death.]
It was said to be one of the most dangerous places in existence, but rumors whispered that a mythical artifact was buried within: the [Eyes of Oblivion].
They found it.
The journey, the bloodshed, the battles, it all led to that moment.
Stark was the first to grab it in his hands, but as soon as he inspected it, they realized the artifact came with a cruel limitation.
---
[Eyes of Oblivion]
[Rank: Unique]
[Description: The eyes of an ancient god. Can be used by up to two individuals to peer into the truths of the world.]
---
Only two. The moment they learned that, Max and Seren turned on him without hesitation.
They didn’t argue or hesitate. They didn’t even feel guilt.
And now, Stark lay broken, betrayed, and discarded.
His HP continued to tick downward, flashing red. Slowly. Inevitably.
He could barely feel the rain anymore.
His blood had soaked into the earth, and the cold had crept into his bones.
This was it. The end.
But then...
Fwish! BOOM!
A sudden gust of wind ripped across the field. Lightning cracked through the clouds above.ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ꜰʀᴏᴍ NovᴇlFirᴇ.ɴet
Stark’s vision flickered from the burst of light.
The sky... stirred.
Something massive began to form above the cloud, something with a golden glow that pierced through the gray veil.
And then he saw it. An eye.
A massive, golden eye, wide and unblinking, emerged from the sky itself.
Its pupil was vertical, otherworldly, and it looked directly at him.
Stark blinked slowly.
"Oh great," he muttered, almost amused, "Now I’m hallucinating."
The eye didn’t move. It simply watched.
And then...
Ding!
New panels appeared.
[You are about to die. What do you wish to do now?]
[Retry] [Give Up]
Stark stared at the options, mouth slightly open.
"...Seriously?"
The text looked exactly like a game prompt, but one he had never seen before.
Usually, when you died, you simply revived if you had enough lives.
But this... this was real, wasn’t it?
The giant eye above didn’t speak. It just kept watching him in silence, waiting for a choice.
Stark clenched his jaw. He didn’t know what "Retry" meant.
He didn’t know if this was real, if it was a hallucination, or if he’d already died and this was some kind of post-mortem illusion.
But what he did know was the rage burning inside him.
He had given everything for them. And they had thrown him away like trash.
"I don’t know what kind of retry this is," he said quietly, "but if it means I can make them feel even a fraction of what I felt..."
He paused, then looked straight at the panel.
"...Then so be it."
[Retry?]
"Yes."
[Very well.]
The golden eye above him closed.
The sky rippled. His vision blurred as a numbing cold washed over him.
His thoughts dissolved into darkness, pulled away from his broken body.
No pain. No fear. Just silence.
And then—
Everything went black. The world disappeared.
...

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Re-Opening of Eternal Soul, Authority of Oblivion
chapters.content:
Chapter 2: Chapter 2: Re-Opening of Eternal Soul, Authority of Oblivion
"Hah?!"
Stark’s eyes flew open as he jolted upright in bed, his breath catching in his throat as if he had just awakened from a nightmare.
For a moment, he remained frozen, his heart thundering in his chest as he scanned the room around him.
The familiar silence of a quiet apartment greeted him, one that shouldn’t have existed anymore.
His gaze darted to the walls, the furniture, the posters he hadn’t seen in years.
"...What the..."
Everything felt too real.
The creaking floorboards beneath him, the slightly open window letting in the night breeze, the dull hum of city life outside.
It all brought back memories long buried under years of war, survival, and tragedy.
And then it hit him, this was his old apartment.
The same one he’d lived in before the world fell apart, before Earth fused with [Eternal Soul], before monsters and guilds, powers and chaos became normal.
"But... when?"
He needed to know the exact date.
The logical thing to do would be to check his phone like anyone else.
But instead, some instinct told him not to.
His feet moved on their own as he crossed the room to the window and pulled back the curtain.
The city outside was... normal. Too normal.
No neon holograms lit up the sky. No flying beasts roamed overhead.
No players dashed between buildings. No colossal guild towers piercing the clouds.
It was the world before [Eternal Soul], quiet, mundane, painfully ordinary.
Stark’s breath hitched as he looked up at the night sky.
Just the ordinary, star-speckled sky he hadn’t seen in over a decade.
He slowly turned around and grabbed the phone from his desk.
The screen lit up, still using an outdated interface. He swiped up and opened the lock screen.
[August 17th, 2025 – 23:58:49]
His heart skipped a beat.
"...Oh, shit."
Only a minute remained. Exactly sixty seconds before it would all begin.
The first announcement from [Eternal Soul] would descend like a divine prophecy, and humanity’s fate would twist irreversibly.
Stark collapsed back onto his bed, still gripping the phone tightly in his hand.
His eyes stared blankly at the ceiling.
So he really had gone back.
He remembered dying. There was no mistaking that part.
His final moments had been agonizingly vivid.
Yet here he was, alive again, and somehow transported ten years into the past.
"...It must’ve been the [Retry] option," he whispered.
It was the only explanation that made sense.
Right before his death, he’d seen it, a floating golden eye, vast and ancient, offering him one last chance.
Stark hadn’t hesitated. He chose it without knowing what it meant.
Now, it all made sense. That eye... whatever it was, it had actually done it.
It had thrown him back to the beginning.
Back to the very night everything started.
But just then... a mechanical voice sounded in Stark’s mind, and a panel appeared before him.
’Huh, but there’s not supposed to be any panels before the game begins...’
Ding!
[The "Eyes of Oblivion" have chosen their host, and have activated.]
[You have obtained the "Authority of Oblivion"]
"Wait a minute..."
It didn’t take Stark more than five seconds to understand what had happened.
And once he did... he laughed.
"THESE IDIOTS!"
Stark had been the first to touch the [Eyes of Oblivion].
And though they could be used by up to two people, it seemed like the very moment he touched them, they had been bound to him.
Meaning that even if he had been killed, the other two... wouldn’t have been able to use them at all.
Stark closed his eyes, and in the darkness of his mind, he felt a strange presence.
Ding!
---
[Eyes of Oblivion]
[Rank: Unique]
[Unique Power: Authority of Oblivion]
[Authority of Oblivion: A power sealed by the gods as they feared that its wielder, the "God of Oblivion", was too strong, its power surpasses anything in the universe, though you are not capable of wielding it yet.]
[Passive: When entering "Eternal Soul", will grant the user the strongest class and talent.]
---
"Authority of Oblivion..." Stark muttered, "I guess I can’t use it yet?"
Though Stark took notice of the passive, which was active.
’I’ll... get the strongest class and talent when I enter the game?’
He was about to wonder just strong that could be, but his thoughts were abruptly interrupted as a sound echoed through his mind.
It was an ethereal chime, as if a system had booted up.
A faint green glow bathed his vision.
["Eternal Soul" has connected with Earth.]
A bitter smile curled Stark’s lips.
"As expected," he murmured, his voice filled with a strange mixture of relief and dread, "Just like before..."
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have established a connection with "Eternal Soul".]
[The next time you fall asleep, you will be transported to this realm. Be wary of its dangers.]
The panel disappeared just as quickly as it had come, and silence fell over the room once again.
Stark exhaled deeply, his mind racing.
Once [Eternal Soul] connected with Earth, every teenager and adult that went to sleep would immediately be transported to this new world.
It was impossible to escape it, no matter how hard you tried.
Soon enough, it would be a global phenomenon.
But Stark knew he couldn’t waste even a single second, from there on, he needed to make use of everything he had.
He opened his phone again, entering the old password without missing a beat.
Notifications buzzed to life.
The group chat from his past, his old friends, had already reacted.
---
[Seren: Did you also get that weird panel, Max?!]
[Max: Yeah, this is crazy, something big’s coming! Let’s go to sleep!]
---
Stark stared at their messages with cold eyes.
There was no spark of nostalgia, no warmth in his chest. Only a bitter chill.
It was almost funny, it was only upon betrayal that Stark remembered all the small moments where he could sense that they didn’t truly consider him as a "friend".
One of them being that Seren only called out to Max instead of the both of them.
Also, the moments where their presence in the game had held him back came to mind.
Where their fears, hesitation, and lack of strength had cost them all dearly.
He wasn’t going to repeat that mistake.
---
[Stark: Don’t contact me again.]
[Stark has left the group chat.]
[Max: The hell’s wrong with him? Dude got issues.]
[Seren: Whatever, maybe he figured out we don’t like him. Let’s just focus on this "Eternal" thing.]
[Max: Yeah, agreed.]
---
Stark didn’t want to stay with them any longer.
He wouldn’t waste his energy. Their Chapter in his story was over.
Without another word, he set the phone aside, walked to his bed, and lay down.
The time had come. His eyes slowly closed, mind focused on what awaited him.
And soon, he felt it, that strange sensation of falling without movement.
A light pull, like gravity turning sideways.
A heartbeat later, he opened his eyes and landed softly on something unseen.
A void stretched in every direction, a formless realm of darkness and silence.
Ding!
[You have officially entered "Eternal Soul" for the first time— never mind.]
Usually, when first entering the game, you were asked to choose a class, then you would receive a talent.
In his past life, Stark chose warrior and received the A-Rank Berserker Talent, allowing him to become incredibly strong.
Talents ranged from F-Rank all the way to SSS-Rank, with F being the lowest, and SSS being the strongest.
They were spread out around several categories: F, E, D, C, B, A, S, SS, SSS.
As for classes, there were several at disposition: warrior, assassin, mage, summoner, archer and more that you could select.
You could also get lucky and receive a [Hidden Class], making you much stronger.
Stark would have surely hesitated like hell to choose a class, especially in this new life.
But...
Ding!
[The "Eyes of Oblivion" passive has activated.]
[You will be granted the strongest class possible.]

chapters.title: Chapter 3: Mage of Oblivion, SSS-Level Infinite Evolution Talent
chapters.content:
Chapter 3: Chapter 3: Mage of Oblivion, SSS-Level Infinite Evolution Talent
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have obtained the Unique Class: Mage of Oblivion!]
[Mage of Oblivion (Unique Hidden Class): Your spells and will are ultimate, none of those standing in your way will survive your power, show them what is oblivion.]
[Class Passive #1: All your magic damage is multipled by 10.]
[Class Passive #2: Your MP recovery is multiplied by 10.]
[Class Passive #3: All your spells’ cooldowns are reduced by half.]
[All of these passives may evolve along with the user.]
---
Seeing that, Stark was overjoyed.
Mages weren’t considered that strong in his previous life, not only because often, getting into a big fight would mean having to strategize and manage way too much.
And if a mage’s mana fell too low, or if their skills had cooldowns, they basically couldn’t win.
Of course, there were several powerful mages, after all, all initial classes are equal, but even then, the majority of players assumed them to be bad.
And yet, seeing that new class in front of him, Stark couldn’t help but grin.
"This class is incredibly strong, no wonder it’s the strongest."
Not only was his magic damage and MP recovery increased, but his cooldowns were also cut.
This pretty much solved all of the mage’s class’ problems, essentially making Stark a god.
Plus, these passives could still evolve as Stark did in the game.
It was absolutely perfect!
With these passives, his chances of dying were low, and he could quickly grow to be the strongest as long as he managed everything right.
Stark was satisfied, it was definitely stronger his warrior class in his previous life.
After that, Stark decided to check the skills he received along with his new class, and there were two of them.
---
[Fireball (Common): Conjure a small fireball that deals 100% of Spirit. 30 (15)-seconds cooldown.]
[Magic Shield (Common): Summon a small shield that can endure a few attacks, if damage is too strong, it will break, 60 (30)-seconds cooldown.]
---
The first skill was one that he could use to deal damage to monsters and players.
It had a 30 seconds cooldown, but the parenthesis right afterward showed Stark that the third passive of his class was already in effect.
Reducing a cooldown by half was godly, no matter how much he looked at it.
On the other hand, his second skill was a defensive one, that allowed him to defend himself.
He was already off to a good start, and as he acquired more equipment and skills, he would evolve to become the strongest.
But after that... Stark knew it was finally time, and he took a deep breath.
Because...
Ding!
[The "Eyes of Oblivion" passive has activated.]
[You will be granted the strongest talent possible.]
After your class came your talent, and though Stark received an A-Rank one in his past life as a warrior, he was eager what he would get now.
Ding!
---
[Congratulations, you have obtained the SSS-Talent: Infinite Evolution!]
[Infinite Evolution: Upon killing strong monsters, there is a chance to obtain "Evolution Points", allowing you evolve your skills.]
[Passive: You gain 5 Evolution Points every 24 hours, it may increase with time.]
[Current Evolution Points: 5.]
---
’SSS-Talent?!’ Stark’s eyes widened in shock, ’Holy shit...!’
In his previous life, he had only heard a very few amount of individuals having an SS-Rank talent, but now, his was SSS, a whole level higher.
"This is insane!"
He understood how it worked on his first read, but he still wanted to try it out if he could.
He opened up the skill panel containing his initials skills, and clicked on [Fireball].
When he did that, a small prompt appeared.
[Do you wish to consume 1 Evolution Point to evolve "Fireball"?]
"Yes!"
He didn’t hesitate for a single second, and instantly allowed it.
Aura began to surround him and the skill panel before he felt a burst of power go through him.
Ding!
[You have evolved "Fireball" (Common) to "Big Fireball" (Uncommon)]
[4 Evolution Points remaining.]
He immediately went to check the new panel as well.
[Big Fireball (Uncommon): Conjure a big fireball that deals 100% → 200% of Spirit. 30 → 25 (12.5)-seconds cooldown.]
Stark grinned, "Perfect!"
Not only had the damage of his fireball doubled, since it now dealt 200% of his spirit attribute, but its cooldown went down by a full five second.
But seeing that, Stark couldn’t help but wonder... what if he did it once more?
He checked the skill’s panel, and as expected, he could do it again.
[Do you wish to consume 3 Evolution Point to evolve "Big Fireball"?]
It now needed 3 Evolution Points since he had evolved it, but Stark didn’t even hesitate.
"Yes!"
Ding!
[You have evolved "Big Fireball" (Uncommon) to "Great Fireball" (Rare)]
[1 Evolution Point remaining.]
[Great Fireball (Rare): Conjure a great fireball that deals 200% → 300% of Spirit. 25 → 20 (10)-seconds cooldown.]
"Even better," Stark laughed to himself.
His damage with the skill had again increased, while his cooldown decreased, making it already incredibly strong before he even entered.
The monsters of [Eternal Soul] were immensely strong and dangerous, so having this from the start would allow him to overwhelm them.The most update n0vels are published on
Since Stark only had one evolution point remaining, he decided to evolve his [Magic Shield] this time.
[Do you wish to consume 1 Evolution Point to evolve "Magic Shield"?]
He confirmed it.
Ding!
[You have evolved "Magic Shield" (Common) to "Magic Shield" (Uncommon)]
Of course, Stark already knew that not all skills changed names every time they ranked up, so it didn’t bother him.
[Magic Shield (Uncommon): Summon a shield that can endure a few attacks, if damage is too strong, it will break, 60 → 50 (25)-seconds cooldown.]
He noticed that the "small" before shield disappeared, as well as the fact his cooldown was reduced.
Now that he had evolved his two skills though, Stark had no more evolution points.
He would need to wait to regain them by waiting, or, as the talent said, kill strong monsters to gain some.
Either way, he was extremely satisfied.
His two common-rank skills had evolved to rare-rank and uncommon-rank respectively.
Items, skills and even monster ranks were spread across several categories, more precisely twelve of them: Common, Uncommon, Rare, Elite, Epic, Legendary, Mythical, Ancient, Ascendant, Divine, Immortal, Eternal.
It was quite a lot, but Stark knew that it would become useful in the future.
He was done with everything that needed to be done related to his first entry in [Eternal Soul] now.
Or so he thought, because...
Ding!
[Player "Stark Darksouls" identified.]
[Please enter your game ID.]
In [Eternal Soul], every player needed to choose an ID, which would be their nickname from there.
This process was permanent, with no way of changing it, so people who chose names like "EpicGamer69" or "DogHater" probably regreted it.
But for Stark, his name in his past life had been "Berserker", only taking it because of his class.
And in this life...
"I’ll call myself Oblivion."
It was extremely unoriginal, since it was simply his class’ name, but Stark didn’t mind.
Ding!
[You have selected "Oblivion" as your ID.]
[You have finished the process of initiation to "Eternal Soul", you will be transported inside of this new realm now.]
Ding!
[Entering "Novice Continent" of "Eternal Soul"...]
The darkness surrounding Stark rippled and twisted before gradually dissolving.
A strange weightless sensation swept over him, as if reality itself was shifting.
Moments later, he met solid ground.
The black void peeled away, replaced by the world before him.
"Here we go again," Stark muttered, a faint grin tugging at his lips.
He stood in the heart of a small town.
Above, a clear blue sky stretched endlessly, the sun casting its warm glow, yet the air still carried a feeling of desolation.
It was the same central square he had materialized in during his previous life.
He noticed several players around him, looking around them in confusion.
"What the fuck is this place?"
"I’m sure I went to sleep, and now I’m here?"
"I went to sleep after that weird panel, looks like it’s the real deal..."
"Yahoo! Time to be the main character of one of those mangas!"
Some were confused, others excited.
But as Stark and the other players appeared, so did a new panel right in front of them.
---
[Welcome to "Eternal Soul".]
[This is a dangerous realm, where countless monsters and dangers await.]
[Be careful, or you may just lose all of your lives and be forgotten forever.]
[Leave this town and explore this realm to gain "Lives", but every time you die, you will lose some of them depending on the loss rate of your location.]
---
Stark already knew about all of this, so it wasn’t new, but the players around him were surprised.
"What do they mean by lives? Don’t we just respawn?"
"We’ll see soon anyway."
---
[You have entered "Novice Town #783"]
[It is a peaceful zone with no monsters allowed in the area, as well as player protection, meaning you cannot attack each other.]
[Lives loss rate: 1]

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Entering Eternal Soul, Status Panel
chapters.content:
Chapter 4: Chapter 4: Entering Eternal Soul, Status Panel
Lives were one of the most important systems in [Eternal Soul].
Every single player started the game with 10 of them.
Upon dying, you would lose a certain number depending on the loss rate of the location you were in.
The [Novice Towns] had a lives loss rate of one, meaning that for now, players only lost one life if they died.
But of course, as one might expect, the deeper you went, the more dangerous it became, and some locations could take thousands of lives with every death.
In addition to that, after a while, lives became the main currency worldwide, as they could be exchanged.
Players could gain lives by killing monsters in [Eternal Soul].
If you ever reached zero lives, you would die instantly.
Furthermore, these lives allowed players to transfer their in-game strength to the real world.
Meaning, as said before, lives were one of the most important mechanics in [Eternal Soul].
Stark needed to gain a large number of them if he wanted an advantage.
But of course, the monsters in this game were extremely dangerous.
In fact, many people stayed in the [Novice Towns] as they were scared.
But it was pointless as you couldn’t leave [Eternal Soul] before meeting a certain level requirement.
[To leave "Eternal Soul", you need to reach level 3.]
Many others pushed their luck and died, losing all their lives.
Stark, in his previous life, had many lives, that was true, but the reason he was able to die instantly was simple:
[Judgment Battlefield]
[Lives loss rate: Instant Death.]
As stated, this realm would kill you instantly if you died in it.
In exchange, the reward for completion was the [Eyes of Oblivion], which were helping Stark at this moment.
After that, Stark decided to directly check his own status panel.
---
[ID: Oblivion]
[Class: Mage of Oblivion]
[Talent: Infinite Evolution (SSS)]
[Level: 1]
[Lives: 10]
[Constitution: 10]
[Strength: 10]
[Agility: 10]
[Spirit: 10]
---
[Eternal Soul] was extremely fair from the start, meaning that every player began with the same points in each of the four core attributes.
But that wasn’t all, because Stark also had combat attributes, which were used in battle.
These combat attributes were determined by your core attributes:
---
[Health Points: 100] (Constitution x 10)
[Mana Points: 100] (Spirit x 10)
[Magic Damage: 10 (+3)] (Spirit x 1)
[Physical Damage: 10] (Strength x 1)
[Magical Resistance: 10] (Spirit x 1)
[Physical Resistance: 10] (Constitution x 1)
---
His current combat attributes were average, but it didn’t bother Stark at all, since he had started with the same stats in his past life.
In addition to those attributes, he also noticed the staff he held in his hand.
Every class would start with a weapon related to their role, and since Stark was a mage, he had a low-level weapon.
[Low-Level Mage Staff (Common): The most basic staff of them all. +3 Spirit to spells when wielded.]
That was the reason why his [Magic Damage] had a +3 next to the number: the staff increased his spell damage.
However, it only applied to spells, which was why none of the other attributes tied to [Spirit] had increased.
But just as he was about to head to the town’s boundary to begin his journey...
Fwish! Ding!
He heard a soft sound, and saw white particles gather before forming the figures of three people.
One of them was slightly chubby, the other wore glasses, and the last was rather muscular.
"D-Did we just die?"
"Holy shit... and now our lives dropped from 10 to 9... I guess this is the real deal..."
"What were we even supposed to do? That level 1 shadow wolf was way too strong. Even the three of us together couldn’t take half of its life..."
"Don’t worry, if we can find a better group and team up, I’m sure we can do better!"
"Yeah, we have experience now!"
Hearing that, Stark couldn’t help but let out a small laugh.
’You have experience in dying, maybe.’
It was normal for new players to get overwhelmed and die in their first few moments.
But Stark didn’t care any more than he already did, so he walked toward the outskirts of the town.
After a few minutes, he reached the boundary of the [Novice Town], marked by a small fence.
Beyond that, he would no longer be in a safe zone.
This meant monsters could attack, and other players could kill each other.
But Stark didn’t need to worry too much about that, so he left the town.
Ding!
[You have left the "Novice Town #783" (Safe Zone)]
Stark didn’t mind. With his staff in hand and years of experience, he was confident in his abilities.
Stark walked for a few minutes through the open plains before eventually arriving at a forest.
[Shadow Forest]
[A beginner zone to help new players get used to the mechanics of "Eternal Soul", though still dangerous the deeper you go.]
Stark was in the game’s first zone.
In his previous life, he had been here with his two "best friends," Max and Seren, and even then, they had struggled to kill some of the monsters.
But strangely, now that he was alone, he had never felt safer.
He stepped into the forest without hesitation.
[You have entered the "Shadow Forest"]
There was one more thing players would eventually learn in [Eternal Soul], aside from the fact that strength was absolute and lives were the most important mechanic.
They would discover that monsters were also extremely strange in their own ways.
Not only were they unusually strong, even at the lowest levels, but... they could evolve.
Just like players, monsters could grow stronger by killing players and absorbing their lives.
A few minutes after entering the forest, Stark sensed something and took his stance.
Through the shadowy outlines of the trees, he saw a monster resting.
---
[Shadow Wolf (Level 1)]
[Rank: Common (Evolving...)]
[HP: 250]
---
’Evolving,’ Stark noted.
This was exactly the kind of evolution he had mentioned earlier.
This monster had probably killed the three players from before, and likely others as well.
Once a monster advanced, its rank would increase by one, making it much stronger.
In this case, the [Shadow Wolf] would go from [Common] to [Uncommon].
But Stark wasn’t going to let that happen.
’Give me those lives you took,’ he thought with a grin.
He had never been a mage in his past life, in fact, he had never cast a single spell, but even so, Stark felt strangely calm as he approached the monster.
The shadow wolf was, as its name suggested, a dark-furred wolf with purple eyes, large enough to intimidate most people.
As soon as he was close enough, the wolf noticed Stark’s presence, baring its teeth and preparing to strike.
If it absorbed any more lives, it could evolve and become far more dangerous.
But Stark didn’t hesitate.
Great Fireball!
He conjured the spell, a blazing sphere of fire quickly forming at the tip of his staff before hurtling toward the wolf.
’The speed is incredible... is it because of my class? Though it’s not a passive.’
Fwish! Boom!
The fireball struck the shadow wolf directly, and in an instant—
-390!1
The wolf’s body was engulfed in flames, its life snuffed out in a single blow.
"Hah..." Stark looked at the corpse in astonishment. "Incredible..."
As the first passive of his [Oblivion] class stated, he indeed dealt ten times more damage than normal.
But it also helped that [Great Fireball] had been upgraded to rare rank.
Ding!
[You have killed "Shadow Wolf (Level 1)"]
[You have gained 10 experience points.]
But aside from that, Stark noticed small orbs of light floating beside the corpse.
He reached out, and the moment he touched one of them—
Ding!
[You have gained 2 Lives.]
’Bingo,’ he grinned.
10 Spirit from attributes + 3 Spirit from staff = 13 x 300% of spirit from great fireball = 39 x 10 = 390.

chapters.title: Chapter 5: Mother Shadow Wolf Boss, Reaching Level 2
chapters.content:
Chapter 5: Chapter 5: Mother Shadow Wolf Boss, Reaching Level 2
[Lives: 10 → 12]
Stark had obtained 2 lives from killing the shadow wolf, and thus gained them.
’Two lives isn’t much at all, but that’s a start,’ he thought, narrowing his eyes slightly. ’I’ll need to keep searching for more monsters.’
After dealing with the first white orb, Stark stepped toward the other two that had appeared.
Without hesitation, he reached out and touched them one by one, feeling a faint pulse of energy pass through his fingertips as each was absorbed.
One was a piece of equipment.The other was a skill book.
[Shadow Fur Boots (Common): Physical Resistance +2, Movement Speed +3%. Requirement: Level 1]
[Skill Book: Shadow Slash (Common): Assassin-type skill book. Requirement: Level 1.]
The shadow wolf he had killed was only a level 1, common-rank monster. It was no surprise that the loot wasn’t anything exceptional.
Still, Stark was satisfied.
Without wasting time, he equipped the [Shadow Fur Boots], feeling the slight improvement in his movement.
’Seems like weak monsters like these really don’t give me [Evolution Points], or maybe its a low chance,’ he mused, glancing back at the wolf’s fading corpse. ’I’ll have to see what happens with a boss.’
After making sure there was nothing else left behind, Stark turned away from the clearing and headed deeper into the forest.
The air here felt thicker, shadows stretching across the ground like claws reaching for prey.
Somewhere in the distance, faint shouts and clashes echoed through the trees.
Meanwhile, in the novice town, many players who had already died once or twice were beginning to form small teams.
Some were cautious, others desperate, but all of them were aware of one thing: they couldn’t afford to lose all their lives.
Slowly, they ventured out to explore, their movements hesitant but determined.
As Stark advanced, the forest grew darker, the sunlight breaking only in thin streaks through the canopy.
His footsteps were quiet, measured... until a sudden scream tore through the silence.
"HOLY SHIT, WHAT IS THAT THING!"
Another voice followed, trembling. "W-We killed one of those shadow wolves, but what the hell is that?!"
Stark’s eyes flickered in the direction of the sound.
Through the gaps between the trees, he spotted the source: a young couple, one dressed as a priest, the other an assassin.
They stood frozen, faces pale, as an enormous shadow loomed over them.
It was a massive wolf, its dark fur rippling with every movement, and its eyes glowed an ominous purple that seemed to pierce straight through the soul.
---
[Mother Shadow Wolf (Level 1)]
[Rank: Uncommon (Boss)]
[HP: 1,500]
---
Not a normal monster, but an uncommon-rank boss.
Its health points alone were far higher than any common creature at this stage, and the oppressive aura it gave off was suffocating.
When Stark reached the edge of the clearing, a slow smile spread across his face.
’A boss would guarantee evolution points, wouldn’t it?’
The truth was obvious: no ordinary player could handle this creature.
Even a group of ten would be torn apart before they could chip away a quarter of its health.
The [Mother Shadow Wolf] was the leader of the [Shadow Wolves], and true to its title, several of its smaller kin lurked nearby, their eyes glinting from the shadows, waiting to pounce.
Stark stood silently, his gaze cold, as the boss raised a massive claw toward the couple.
He had no intention of saving them.
He didn’t know them after all, and he would prioritize the people close to him.
The air shifted, and from the brush around them, several shadow wolves suddenly emerged, closing in.
"Take this!" the assassin shouted, darting forward with his dagger.
But the attack barely grazed the boss’s fur. In seconds, the two players were surrounded.
Teeth and claws flashed. The couple’s attacks were too weak, their health too low, their resistance pitiful.
They could do nothing but watch as the wolves closed in and tore into them.
"Ah—!"
A flurry of red damage numbers burst above their heads.
Within moments, their bodies collapsed, fading into motes of light.
Each of them had lost one life, the essence of which transformed into small glowing spheres.
The nearby wolves eagerly absorbed them, their bodies twitching faintly as if savoring the stolen vitality.
That was the moment Stark had been waiting for.
The wolves, including the boss, were all grouped together, the perfect target.
Great Fireball!
Mana surged to the tip of Stark’s staff, forming a blazing sphere that pulsed with heat.
He let it fly.
BOOM!
-390! -390! -390!
The explosion engulfed the cluster of wolves.
Most of the smaller ones were instantly incinerated, leaving behind only scorched patches on the grass.
The [Mother Shadow Wolf] staggered back, snarling, its purple eyes blazing with fury.
ROOOOARRR!
The sound shook the clearing as the boss locked onto Stark and charged.
’I only have 100 HP... any hit will kill me,’ Stark thought, his lips curling into the faintest smirk. ’But even then...’
Fwish!
He sidestepped with precision far beyond what most players at his level could manage, narrowly avoiding the boss’s swipe.
Mages weren’t meant for close combat, one hit was usually a death sentence.
But Stark wasn’t like other mages.
Ten seconds passed. His [Great Fireball] cooldown ended.
Fwish! BOOM!
-390!
He repeated the process twice more, his movements sharp and deliberate, the fireballs crashing into the boss and steadily burning away its health bar.
Now the creature was barely clinging to life. It knew it too.Thɪs No(ᴠ)ᴇlFire.nᴇt
With a sudden surge of speed, the [Mother Shadow Wolf] lunged, its fangs bared, determined to take him down before the end.
This time, Stark couldn’t dodge.
Magic Shield!
A shimmering blue barrier erupted in front of him, the impact shaking his arms as the boss slammed into it.
Cracks spiderwebbed across the shield, but it held long enough.
By the time it shattered, Stark was already raising his staff again.
Great Fireball!
Fwish! BOOM!
-390!
The blast engulfed the wolf’s head, and with a final, echoing roar, the uncommon-rank boss collapsed.
Ding!
[You have killed "Mother Shadow Wolf (Level 1 Uncommon-Rank Boss)"]
[You have gained 250 experience points.]
The rush of experience hit immediately.
Ding!
---
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 2!]
[You have gained 5 points in all of your attributes, and 5 free points to distribute.]
But then, another notification appeared right beneath it.
[You have gained 2 Evolution Points!]
---
"Amazing," Stark muttered, his eyes brightening. "So killing bosses really does give evolution points."
And with that level up, another system message appeared.
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have unlocked the "Novice Town #783’s" Level Leaderboard!]
[You have gained 1 Prestige Point!]
At that same moment, a system-wide announcement rang in the minds of every player in Novice Town #783.
[Player "Oblivion" has killed "Mother Shadow Wolf (Uncommon-Rank Boss)" and was the first to reach Level 2!]
[The "Novice Town #783’s" Level Leaderboard is now open!]
By now, hundreds of players were gathered in the town.
Most were teenagers or adults, though a few elderly individuals had also appeared.
The reaction was immediate.
"What the hell, he already killed a boss?"
"I couldn’t even kill a single monster, this game is rigged!"
"How could anyone reach level 2 so fast?"
Meanwhile, the young couple Stark had ignored revived in the central square, the system informing them that they now had only 9 lives left.
"Hey... do you think that lives thing is real?" the priest girl asked, her voice low. "If we lose them all... do we die?"
"Impossible. There’s no way that’s true," the assassin replied automatically, though there was doubt in his tone.
"But think about it... we woke up here, in this strange world, and everything is too realistic..."
Before he could answer, the system notification of Stark’s kill reached their ears.
"What? Wasn’t the [Mother Shadow Wolf] the thing that killed us? And someone killed it?!"
"How? Who the hell is this ’Oblivion’ guy?"
"Didn’t it have a bunch of shadow wolves with it too?"
The more they thought about it, the more their confidence crumbled.
"Maybe he had a full team of professionals with top-tier talents?"
"No. Look at the leaderboard, his is the only name on it."
They checked.
---
[Level Leaderboard:]
[1. Oblivion: Level 2]
---
No one else had even reached level 2 yet.
The realization hit them, this person might not just be first in their town, but possibly first in the entire world.
That thought was terrifying.
But for others, it was motivating.
"Better safe than sorry. Let’s just assume this game is the real deal."
"Agreed."
In Novice Town #783, as more people gathered, the urgency in the air grew.
Groups began forming with more care, players seeking out those with different classes and useful skills/talents.
"The max team size right now is ten. We’re missing three more people!"
"I’m a [Holy Warrior], I have a skill that allows me to protect my comrades. Let’s go together!"
Determination and hope sparked across the town.

chapters.title: Chapter 6: Evolution Points Drops, Hand of Avarice
chapters.content:
Chapter 6: Chapter 6: Evolution Points Drops, Hand of Avarice
Thanks to the fact that he had reached level 2 so quickly, Stark gained one point of prestige.
In the future, the more of these points he had, the better.
Later on, he could use them to buy high-level items from NPCs, items that normal players wouldn’t even get to see, let alone touch.
It wasn’t something he could use right now, but Stark knew the value of preparing early.
In addition to the prestige, leveling up to level 2 increased each of his four core attributes by 5, and also gave him another 5 points to allocate however he wanted.
He didn’t hesitate for even a second. All 5 went straight into [Spirit].
---
[Constitution: 15]
[Strength: 15]
[Agility: 15]
[Spirit: 15 → 20]
---
Stark grinned with satisfaction. His damage output was going to skyrocket.
But there was still loot on the ground.
He turned his attention back to the boss’s corpse and the bodies of the other monsters he had slain.
Several small glowing orbs lay scattered around them, pulsing faintly.
Without wasting time, he crouched down and swept them into his inventory.
Ding!
[You have gained 21 Lives.]
The boss had given him the most Lives by far compared to the regular monsters.
If this had been a normal team fight with several players, each person would have only gotten one or two Lives at most since the rewards would be split evenly.
But Stark was alone, which meant he got it all.
[You have gained 1 Evolution Point.]
"Huh?" Stark blinked at the notification. "But I already got the ones from the boss..."
And then it clicked.
Every monster had a chance to drop evolution points.
That meant that the drop rate for regular monsters was abysmally low, but bosses were almost guaranteed to drop at least one.
’Incredible,’ Stark thought, eyes narrowing in excitement. ’No wonder this is an SSS-Rank Talent.’
He turned to the rest of the loot.
’Most of this is junk... except for two things.’
The first made him grin.
[Shadow Staff (Uncommon): +10 Spirit. Requirement: Level 1.]
’Perfect.’
This staff alone would add +10 Spirit to every attack he cast.
With his build, that meant an extra 100 points of damage per spell.
For a player who had just reached level 2, this was absurd.
He equipped it immediately.
The weapon felt light in his hands, yet radiated a cold, shadowy energy that seemed to hum with power.
The second notable drop was even more intriguing, a skill book.
And not just any skill book, but one he could actually learn.
[Skill Book: Hand of Avarice (Uncommon): Can be used on corpses, has a 25% chance to obtain another loot reward. Requirement: Level 2.]
’Holy shit.’
The skill wasn’t tied to any specific class, meaning anyone could learn it. That alone made it extremely valuable.
The effect itself was simple, but terrifyingly useful.
A 25% chance to get extra loot from corpses? Even if the rate was low, the sheer number of monsters Stark planned to kill made this potentially game-breaking.
And the best part? He could evolve it.
He pressed his hand to the book and poured mana into it.
The pages dissolved into black smoke, which wrapped around his arm before seeping into his body.
Ding!
[You have learned the skill "Hand of Avarice"!]
Another prompt appeared almost immediately.
[Do you wish to consume 3 Evolution Points to evolve "Hand of Avarice"?]
"Hell yes."
Ding!
[You have evolved "Hand of Avarice" (Uncommon) to "Hand of Avarice" (Rare)]
[Current Evolution Points: 0]
[Hand of Avarice (Rare): Can be used on corpses, has a 25% → 50% chance to obtain another loot reward.]
The percentage had doubled. For Stark, this was a jackpot.
"Time to test it."
He pointed his staff at the pile of bodies.
Hand of Avarice!
A dark, spectral hand burst forth from the staff, coiling through the corpses before sinking into them.
Ding!
[You have obtained 7 Lives.]
[You have gained 1 Evolution Point!]
His eyes widened.
That was only from a single use. And he’d just earned back one of the evolution points he had spent.
’Yeah... this skill is insane.’
After clearing up the area, Stark decided it was time to move deeper into the hunting grounds.
The stronger the monsters, the more valuable the loot, and the higher the chance of gaining evolution points.
The only way to leave [Eternal Soul] the first time was to reach level 3.
Twenty minutes had passed since he had unlocked the [Level Leaderboard] of his novice town. Only now did other players start catching up.
The first to reach level 2 after Stark was a team of six led by a [Holy Warrior] named BraveCop, real name David.
His group took up the 2nd to 7th spots on the board.
While they were celebrating, Stark had already spent those same twenty minutes killing dozens of monsters, gaining a handful of Lives and another precious evolution point.
His current damage was nothing short of terrifying.
Great Fireball!
BOOM!
-900!1 Tʜe sourcᴇ of thɪs content ɪs novᴇl(ꜰ)ire.ɴet
Almost 1,000 damage in a single hit.
In his past life, reaching this level of power so early would have been unthinkable.
’To extract equipment and skills into reality, I’ll need far more Lives. I have 51 now, but I’ll also need to reach level 10 before it’s even possible.’
That goal would have to wait. For now, strength came first.
As Stark ventured further, the monsters began to change.
And then, he saw it.
---
[Shadow Bear King (Level 2)]
[Rank: Uncommon (Boss)]
[HP: 3,000]
---
Its massive frame moved with surprising speed, crashing through the forest as if the trees were twigs.
But it wasn’t charging at him, it was chasing something else.
Stark paused, lowering his staff. Instead of attacking right away, he decided to follow.
The Shadow Bear King’s claws slashed with lethal precision, striking faster than most players could dodge.
For new players, this boss was a nightmare.
After a few seconds, Stark saw its target, a team of six.
At the front, a burly man held a heavy shield, parrying blow after blow while steadily retreating.
It was David, the second-place player in the novice town.
Behind him, the rest of the team unleashed a flurry of arrows, spells, and strikes.
Their expressions were tense, their movements stiff.
Hitting the boss was proving harder than they expected.
’People don’t adapt instantly to their powers,’ Stark thought, watching closely. ’It takes time to adjust.’
The bear king kept darting in and out, its shadowy claws hammering David’s shield until his health dropped to half.
David’s [Holy Warrior] class let him absorb damage for his allies, but against a boss of this rank, it wasn’t enough.
Worse, the boss had barely lost any HP, still sitting at over 95%.
"J-Just keep attacking!" David shouted, trying to stay calm. "Even if we can’t kill it, we can chip it down!"
They couldn’t have been more wrong.
Because from the shadows, other monsters began to appear.
---
[Poison Snake (Level 2)]
[Rank: Common]
[HP: 600]
---
Slithering forward, the snakes reared back and spat venom at the group.
"Ahhh—!"
A female mage was struck.
-48! -2! -2!
Not only was she hit, but the poison effect began eating away at her health.
"I-I can’t hold on for long!" she gasped.
The team’s formation crumbled. The bear king still loomed over them, and now poisonous projectiles rained from every side.
Health bars plummeted.
Watching from a distance, Stark remained still, eyes narrowing.
’I guess I should deal with that boss,’ he thought. ’I’m sure it’ll drop evolution points.’
20 Spirit + 10 Spirit from the staff = 30 x 300% = 90 x 10 = 900.

chapters.title: Chapter 7: Venom Crystal, Killing the Shadow Bear King
chapters.content:
Chapter 7: Chapter 7: Venom Crystal, Killing the Shadow Bear King
Great Fireball!
–900!
A blazing orb of fire exploded from Stark’s staff and smashed straight into one of the poison snakes coiling near the party.
The creature had been hissing and spitting venom toward David’s group, too focused on its own attack to notice the incoming spell.
The moment the fireball connected, the snake’s body ignited in a burst of flame.
Its scales charred black, skin peeled away, and in less than a heartbeat, it crumbled into a pile of ash on the burnt earth.
---
[You have killed "Venom Snake (Level 2)"]
[You have gained 25 experience points.]
[You have gained 2 Lives.]
---
The sudden flash of fire stunned the monsters nearby.
They froze for a brief second, unable to understand what had just happened.
A predator from the shadows had struck, and they didn’t even know where it was.
While they were still confused, Stark acted.
He quickly extended his staff, activating [Hand of Avarice] in an attempt to grab more loot from the snake’s remains.
Beep!
[Hand of Avarice has failed.]
’Figures. Can’t expect it to hit every time,’ Stark thought.
The skill only had a fifty-percent success rate, and luck wasn’t always on his side.
At the moment, it was still stuck at rare-rank.
He would need five evolution points to push it to the next tier.
Meanwhile, David and his party had stopped mid-battle, still processing what they’d just witnessed.
The corpse of the snake was gone, reduced to dust, and the number floating in the air from Stark’s attack was absurd.
"What the hell was that damage?" one of them blurted out.
"Did I see that right? Nine hundred? That’s not... that’s not normal."
"A level 1 shadow wolf takes around five seconds for us to bring down, and you’re telling me a level 2 monster just evaporated?"
David snapped them back to focus. "Don’t lose concentration! Hold your ground!"
Great Fireball!
A second blazing sphere erupted from Stark’s staff, streaking through the air before slamming into another poison snake.
The impact lit the area in a fiery glow.
Another snake fell instantly, this time leaving nothing behind.
But the pressure on David’s team lessened dramatically.
Two of the snakes were gone, and that meant fewer threats to juggle.
"Hold out!" David shouted. "My skill cooldown is over!"
His eyes sharpened as he activated the signature ability of his [Holy Warrior] class: [Holy Barrier].
A golden light wrapped around his towering figure, forming a radiant shield that glimmered with divine energy.
For the next five seconds, nothing could touch him.
The massive shadow bear king slammed its claws into the barrier again and again, but each blow simply rebounded, sparks flying from the magical protection.
Great Fireball!
Boom!
–900!
A third snake burst apart under Stark’s magic, its corpse dissolving into ash.
This time, however, something caught Stark’s attention. A book.
A faint glow shimmered around it, and Stark’s eyes lit up.
He dashed forward, snatched it from the ground, and quickly retreated behind a tree before examining it.
[Skill Book: Poison Crystal (Common), Mage-type skill book. Requirement: Level 2.]
Skill books worked in a fair way in this world.
Most of the time, the book would match the user’s class.
That made sense, what was the point of giving a warrior a spell only mages could use?
But luck had failed him once before.
His first drop had been for assassins, completely useless to him.
This time, though, it was perfect. He didn’t hesitate.
Ding!
[You have learned the skill "Poison Crystal".]
---
[Poison Crystal (Common): Summon a small poisonous crystal that deals exactly 50 damage and applies the "Poison" status effect. 15 (7.5)-seconds cooldown.]
[Poison: Deals 10% of damage received per second for 5 seconds.]
---
He activated [Hand of Avarice] again.
Ding!
[You have gained 1 Evolution Point.]
’Perfect,’ Stark grinned, ’Even small fry can drop these.’
The system message appeared again:
[Do you wish to consume 1 Evolution Point to evolve "Poison Crystal"?]
"Yes."
Ding!
[You have evolved "Poison Crystal" (Common) → "Venom Crystal" (Uncommon).]
[Current Evolution Points: 1.]
---
[Venom Crystal (Uncommon): Summon a poisonous crystal that deals exactly 50 → 100 damage and applies the "Poison" status effect. 15 → 12 (6)-seconds cooldown.]
[Poison: Deals 10% → 15% of damage received per second for 5 seconds.]
---
’Now we’re talking.’
He immediately prepared to test it.
More skills meant more ways to keep attacking while other abilities cooled down.
At the moment, none of his abilities truly consummed high mana, which is why it wasn’t even shown, but he knew that wouldn’t last forever.
Higher-tier spells would demand heavy mana costs, he’d need to manage that carefully in the future.
And that also meant trying to increase his mana as much as he could.
After all, the second passive of his [Mage of Oblivion] class was to grant him 10 times the MP recovery.
One last Great Fireball took care of the remaining poison snake.
Then, the shadow bear king had already broken through David’s holy barrier, ready to again and kill, but Stark stepped forward.
Venom Crystal!
A green crystal formed at the tip of his staff, pulsing with toxic light.
With a sharp flick, Stark hurled it toward the bear king.
Fwish! Slash!
The crystal pierced deep into the monster’s side.
The bear king roared, staggering.
–1,000!
Stark’s grin widened.
His passive skill, tenfold damage to all magic, worked even on fixed-damage attacks.
The crystal’s base damage might have been 100, which would still be very useful to a new player, but here, it hit like a cannon.
And then came the poison.
–150! –150! –150!
Each tick drained 15% of the crystal’s original damage for five seconds.
The numbers kept stacking.
All told, that one cast had dealt 1,750 damage.
David’s team froze mid-fight, eyes wide.
They’d been grinding at the bear king for half an hour, barely scraping 5% off its health bar.
Stark had halved it in one attack.
The boss turned its fury toward Stark.
Its eyes glowed red, muscles tensed, and it charged.
"Heh," Stark smirked. "Come on, then."
Great Fireball!
Boom!
–900!
The bear didn’t even flinch at the blast, swinging a massive claw down toward him.
But Stark sidestepped effortlessly, spinning his staff.
Venom Crystal! Slash!
–1,000!
The crystal struck the bear’s head, punching through its skull.
The beast collapsed with a heavy thud, unmoving. The fight was over.nᴇt
"This... this isn’t normal," one of David’s teammates muttered, "Is he even the same level as us? Could he be cheating?"
"Idiot. How would you even cheat here? We don’t even know if this place is... real."
Suspicion lingered, but relief was stronger. The danger was gone.
The boss’s corpse dropped piles of loot, shimmering with rarity.
But in [Eternal Soul], loot belonged to whoever dealt the most damage.
Stark had done more than ninety-five percent of the work. Everything was his.
---
[You have killed "Shadow Bear King (Level 2 Uncommon-Rank Boss)".]
[You have gained 500 experience points.]
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 3!]
[You have gained 5 points in all of your attributes, and 5 free points to distribute.]
[You have gained 3 Evolution Points.]
[You have gained 7 Lives.]
---
Three evolution points from a single boss confirmed Stark’s theory, bosses guaranteed them, and in large amounts.
With four points now in total, it meant he only needed one more to upgrade one of his rare-rank skills.
For now, though, he decided to hold onto them.
He knelt beside the shadow bear king’s body, gathering every last piece of loot.
David and his party stayed silent, watching him with a mixture of awe and disbelief.
"Thank you, friend," David expressed his gratitude, "We wouldn’t have made it without—"
But Stark cut him off, "Don’t thank me, in this forsaken place, you shouldn’t trust others so easily."

chapters.title: Chapter 8: Elite-Rank Skill, Full Backpack
chapters.content:
Chapter 8: Chapter 8: Elite-Rank Skill, Full Backpack
"I understand, thank you for the reminder," David nodded after Stark’s warning.
In [Eternal Soul], the only truly safe zones were the towns, since players couldn’t attack each other inside them.
But outside the towns, Stark knew, player-killing would become rampant.
Especially in the future, where taking lives from other players was easier and more rewarding.
When someone killed another player, they would gain lives corresponding to the number that player would have lost in that specific zone.
For example, Stark could easily kill David and his team, taking one life for every player eliminated.
But... it was pointless. They were already too weak and broke to matter.
Stark also remembered David from his past life.
Building a connection could be beneficial in the future.
But for now, Stark didn’t want to be friends, and preferred to leave only a strong impression in their minds.
"Then we’ll leave and not disturb you any further," David said, bowing slightly. "If you need any help in the future, feel free to ask me!"
Stark nodded, though he knew he wouldn’t need it.
David and the rest of the group began to leave, except for one.
It was the mage girl who had been struck by the poison snake’s venom earlier and had taken some damage.
"My ID is Starfall, can I add you as a friend?" she asked, her eyes bright with curiosity.
Stark let out an amused sigh as he heard that, but he still had a neutral expression on his face.
He knew her from his past life too; she had the [Star Prophet] class, a type of mage stronger than the average one.
But, just like many others in the future, she had died.
Stark studied her for a few seconds, anticipating her next move.
And then...
"No."
"Aww..."
She looked ready to argue, but one of her teammates tugged her away, shaking their head.
Stark observed David’s team. They were solid, each member with a decent class. Even so, it wasn’t enough in this game.
"My attacks deal a lot of damage," he thought, "but I leave myself vulnerable because of the cooldowns."
Even with his cooldowns halved, Stark still had to dodge incoming attacks, something most mages shouldn’t have to worry about.
"I guess I’ll just be a battle mage," he muttered to himself.
Left alone in front of the corpse of the shadow bear king, Stark immediately used [Hand of Avarice].
The dark hand reached out and extracted something from the massive body.
[You have gained 1 Evolution Point!]
[You have gained 4 Lives.]
’Perfect!’ Stark thought, smiling slightly.
Aside from that, there were three loot drops from the boss, but only one was usable for him.
[Bear Mage Robe (Uncommon): Mage-type equipment. Physical Resistance +7. Magical Resistance +12. Requirement: Level 2.]
It wasn’t much, especially since he generally avoided being hit, but he equipped it anyway. Just in case.
Now that he had 5 evolution points, Stark had to decide what to evolve.
’Honestly... the answer is obvious,’ he thought.
His attacks were already strong enough to easily handle level 2 monsters easily and possibly level 3 too.
His [Magic Shield] wasn’t used much, except in situations where he was truly outmatched.
The only real choice that made sense was [Hand of Avarice]. Its effect of constantly giving him extra loot would compound as it evolved.
[Do you wish to consume 5 Evolution Points to evolve "Hand of Avarice"?]
Ding!
[You have evolved "Hand of Avarice" (Rare) → "Hand of Avarice" (Elite)]
[Current Evolution Points: 0]
---
[Hand of Avarice (Elite): Can be used on corpses, has a 50% → 75% chance to obtain another loot reward.]
---
’Perfect.’
It was his very first elite-rank skill in this new life, and Stark felt a rare sense of pride.
Usually, evolving a skill required repeated use or special items to deepen one’s understanding of it.
But Stark had [Infinite Evolution], meaning none of that was necessary.
He also noted that to evolve it further, to epic-rank, he would need 7 evolution points.
With that done, Stark gathered all the loot from the shadow bear king and prepared to head deeper into the shadow forest.
His current lives had reached 65, giving him confidence.
His growth was already a hundred times faster and stronger than in his previous life.
He continued killing monsters in the forest, gaining experience and evolution points steadily.
Eventually, however...
[Backpack is full: 10/10]
Every player started [Eternal Soul] with a backpack to store items directly.
Now that Stark’s backpack was full, he had to return to town to manage his inventory.
Most of his collected items were equipments not aligned with his own class, but they were still valuable.
Lives were a unique currency. They could be traded for items, but they were also actual lives in the game.
In essence, trading for items meant putting your life on the line.
It was a risk, but one that was unavoidable.
For the people of [Novice Town #783], these items could significantly improve their strength.
For example, the [Shadow Slash] skill book would likely be highly sought after by assassins.
On the way back, Stark noticed several people being chased by shadow wolves.
It was a completely normal sight early in the game.
New players would need time to adjust to this environment.
Until then, he could only push forward and grow stronger.
’There were several extremely strong players in my previous life,’ he thought, ’I wonder if they can do the same thing I do.’
Stark wasn’t stupid, if he could find players that weren’t evil and be friends with, it would only be better.
Especially when he knew what would come later.
While walking, Stark decided to assign all 5 free attribute points to [Agility].
Dodging would be his main challenge, so higher speed would be crucial.
Just before leaving the shadow forest, he paused to use another feature.
[Do you wish to enable the "Hide Face" feature?]
In [Eternal Soul], players’ appearances matched their real-life look and couldn’t be altered.
Since Stark hadn’t yet extracted his powers to the real world, revealing himself was risky.
Inside the game, he was nearly invincible. Outside? Not yet.
"Oblivion" was the highest-ranked player, not just in this town, but across the entire world. Once word spread, he could be in danger.
He had seen this kind of situation many times in his past life.
Activating [Hide Face] caused a glitchy, pixelated veil to cover his face.
He still wore all the same equipment and carried the same staff; only his face was concealed.
Beyond that, only his cold, calculating eyes were visible.
Ding!
[You have entered "Novice Town #783"]
[You are now in a safe zone.]
Inside the town, many players paused, unsure what to do next.
To leave the game, they needed to reach level 3. Many couldn’t defeat even a single monster on their own.
Monsters often appeared in groups, making the challenge greater.
Stark moved confidently through the town. Many began to whisper and point.Thɪs ɴo(v)elFɪre.ɴet
"Holy shit, is this guy aura farming or what?"
"I can’t even see his face, huh?"
Stark heard the murmurs and allowed himself a faint, small smile.
But he quickly returned to his usual composed attitude and found a quiet spot to sit.
He took out all his items from the backpack and arranged them neatly in front of him.
Without hesitation, he activated the [Shop] function.
[Equipments and skill books for sale only for 15 minutes, pretty cheap.]

chapters.title: Chapter 9: Selling Items, Evolving Monster
chapters.content:
Chapter 9: Chapter 9: Selling Items, Evolving Monster
Stark assumed that fifteen minutes would be more than enough to sell everything.
Any more time than that wouldn’t be worth it to him.
What he wanted most right now was to level up and get more items.
Of course, he could have just dropped the items in the forest and gone after better ones.
But to Stark, that was a waste of resources.
And obviously, he wasn’t about to give things away for free, especially not to strangers.
He remembered clearly how many people and opportunities he had missed out on in his past life.
Most of them were lost because of his so-called best friends.
Max and Seren were strong, with powerful classes and talents, that was true, but their personalities were the problem.
This time, things would be different.
He wouldn’t make the same mistakes twice. He would form bonds only with strong and reliable people.
As soon as his shop appeared, it immediately attracted everyone nearby.
"Holy shit, isn’t that Oblivion guy?"
"That’s amazing. I wish I could get strong like him..."
"Look at that loot. It’s actually really good!"
The crowd grew quickly, whispers spreading as they examined the items Stark had placed for sale.
Before long, a man stepped forward and pointed at one of the skill books, [Shadow Slash].
"How much for this? It could be useful to me."
The man, like Stark, had the [Hide Face] feature activated.
His ID was shown as "PrinceLucas," and he wore a clean, small uniform that suggested he wasn’t a casual player.
Stark glanced at him, then answered plainly. "Ten Lives."
PrinceLucas frowned slightly. "Ten Lives? That’s basically what you start with at the beginning. You can’t be serious."
Stark shrugged. To him, it was a fair price.
A skill like [Shadow Slash] didn’t just allow the user to slash an extra time.
It also increased the damage output and had a chance to cause bleeding.
That kind of ability was far too valuable to let go cheaply.
In fact, Stark was making them an incredible offer.
"Can I use cash instead?" PrinceLucas asked.
"If you’ve got cash, you can buy Lives from others," Stark replied calmly. "Then come back and trade."
The man scratched his chin for a moment, then gave a small nod. "Very well."
He turned away, walking back toward his teammates. The group huddled together and exchanged a few words.
Not even thirty seconds later, PrinceLucas returned.
"Here."
Ding!
[You have sold the "Shadow Slash" skill book and gained 10 Lives]
[Lives: 65 → 75]
In [Eternal Soul], players could trade lives at any time, this was what made them the universal currency.
Seeing the notification, Stark grinned.
His number of Lives was already starting to rise at a good pace.
After that, several more people approached his shop.
Some tried talking to him casually. Others asked if he would accept real money instead of Lives.
But Stark refused all of them.
"Move along if you’re not buying. Don’t interfere with my business."
To him, money was already on its way to becoming worthless.
Soon enough, people would realize that Lives had far more value.
They could be used not only in the game but also to extract things from [Eternal Soul] into reality.
And that was only the beginning.
The players around him had no idea what awaited them in the future, both inside the game and in the real world once the rest of the system fully opened.
Later on, only strength would matter. Everything else would be irrelevant.
And Stark would make sure he was among the strongest.
All the friends and close people he had lost in his previous life because of his mistakes, this time, he would not fail them.
This time, he would fix everything.
Only a few minutes after his first sale, he managed to sell every last item.
No one really knew the market price yet, but Stark had made sure to sell at a rate slightly smaller than the normal one, allowing him to sell and also make the buyer satisfied.
When he was done, he had earned an additional thirty-six Lives.
Once his last item was gone, Stark packed up.
"Time to head back," he thought. "I need to go deeper into the forest and find stronger monsters."
Upon reaching Level 5, he would unlock the [Teleportation Array], allowing him to move between towns.
And his main goal was Level 10.
At that stage, he would be able to extract power from the game into reality to be ready for the disasters that would come.
Other parts of [Eternal Soul] would also open.
That was where the real game would begin.
With his mind set, Stark left the town and returned to the [Shadow Forest].
...
About twenty minutes later, he was already rushing through the forest.
This time he went deeper than before, not slowing down.
He soon reached a large clearing.
The air felt heavy, and his instincts told him something was about to happen.
Sure enough, on the ground ahead, he noticed large footprints scorched into the earth.
"Flame monster," Stark muttered, eyes narrowing.
He pushed forward. And soon enough, he found it.
A massive [Flame Fox] boss was feasting on the fallen remains of players.
Their Lives had already been consumed.
---
[Flame Fox (Level 3)]
[Rank: Uncommon Boss (Evolving...)]
[HP: 5,000]
---
Stark tightened his grip on his staff.
This monster would give him solid experience if he could bring it down.
He prepared to cast [Venom Crystal].
But right as he aimed at the fox...
Fwish! BOOM!
The ground erupted with a violent explosion. Fire scorched the entire area around the boss.
Stark’s eyes widened as he instinctively stepped back.
The fox lifted its head, flames dancing violently around its body.
Its aura grew heavier, more powerful. Its form stretched, looking sharper and more majestic as the fire consumed it.
"It evolved," Stark thought, his eyes narrowing further. "Not sure if this is good or bad timing."
In [Eternal Soul], monsters that killed players could absorb their Lives.
If they gathered enough, they could evolve.
This was the same thing that had nearly happened to the very first shadow wolf Stark had encountered.
He had killed it just in time. But this time, the [Flame Fox] had succeeded.
Its new form radiated dangerous power.
---
[Inferno Fox (Level 3)]
[Rank: Rare (Boss)]
[HP: 7,500]
---
When a monster evolved, its rank increased, its stats jumped, and its HP rose significantly.
Thankfully, this was still early in the game.
Evolutions weren’t too terrifying yet. But soon enough, things would become much harder.
Stark took a steady breath. He pointed his staff forward.
"Venom Crystal!"
Fwish!
A jagged crystal formed instantly, then shot toward the towering three-meter-tall Inferno Fox.
Bam!ʀᴇᴀᴅ ʟᴀᴛᴇsᴛ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀᴛ
-1000! -150! -150!
The crystal slammed into the boss, making it stumble.
The poison seeped into its body, lowering its HP over time.
The fox’s flaming ears twitched. It snapped its head toward Stark’s position, its burning eyes locking onto him.
The ground trembled as it unleashed a surge of flames in his direction.
Flame Surge!
The attack spread wide, covering the entire area with fire.
Magic Shield!
Stark summoned the shield just in time.
The wall of energy held for a moment against the flames but shattered quickly under the pressure.
The fire still grazed him, and he felt the heat bite at his skin even through the protection.
-10! -10! -10!
Using [Great Fireball] against this boss was pointless. Fire skills simply wouldn’t work.
That was why having [Venom Crystal] was such a blessing.
Even better, his class’s passive ability cut cooldowns in half.
The skill was ready again in just six seconds.
"Here we go," Stark muttered, his eyes sharp and focused.
He aimed his staff again.
The Inferno Fox stepped forward, flames burning hotter, its mouth opening wide as it prepared another deadly attack.

chapters.title: Chapter 10: Cursed Tree, Vine Swing Skill
chapters.content:
Chapter 10: Chapter 10: Cursed Tree, Vine Swing Skill
Venom Crystal!
-1000! -150! -150!
Each of Stark’s attacks landed cleanly, the numbers popping above the boss’s head.
In total, every single strike dealt 1,750 damage.
The best part was the cooldown, Stark could fire one every six seconds.
That meant in the early stages of the game, he was a walking powerhouse of damage.
Of course, there was still danger.
The [Inferno Fox] wasn’t just going to stand there.
Its flames were brutal, and even a single hit could probably kill Stark.
Even at level 3, a rare-ranked boss could deal around 200 damage in one strike.
That just so happened to be Stark’s current HP.
In other words, one mistake and he was dead.
But Stark was focused.
It only took four venom crystals to bring the boss down to the brink of death.
And just when its health was almost gone, the [Inferno Fox] turned tail and tried to escape.
The monsters in this game weren’t mindless.
They had some level of intelligence. And when close to death, some tried to run.
"Oh, you don’t," Stark’s eyes narrowed as he dashed forward, staff aimed right at the fox.
Venom Crystal!
Fwish! Boom!
The crystal shot out and struck the fox squarely.
The impact echoed across the scorched clearing, and the boss’s body froze mid-stride.
Its health bar dropped to zero.
The creature let out a final screech before collapsing, its burning body hitting the ground with a dull thud.
Ding!
---
[You have killed "Inferno Fox (Level 3 Rare-Rank Boss)"]
[You have gained 1,500 experience points.]
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 4!]
[You have gained 5 points in all of your attributes, and 5 free points to distribute.]
[You have gained 4 Evolution Points!]
[You have gained 9 Lives.]
---
Obviously, higher-ranked monsters and bosses gave more experience, which is why Stark got so much from this one.
But Stark wasn’t done yet.
Hand of Avarice!
A dark, shadowy hand extended from his staff and gripped the fox’s corpse.
Ding!
---
[You have gained 4 Evolution Points!]
[You have gained 4 Lives.]
---
Stark blinked in shock.
"Eight Evolution Points instantly?" He grinned wide. "Incredible."
With eight EP in hand, he could evolve at least one or two skills.
He didn’t waste a second and pulled up his skill list.
[Skills: Great Fireball (Rare), Magic Shield (Uncommon), Hand of Avarice (Elite), Venom Crystal (Uncommon)]
He thought carefully.
"It costs 3 EP to go from Uncommon to Rare, and 5 EP to go from Rare to Elite... If I pushed [Hand of Avarice] to Epic, it would take 7 EP.’
It was tempting, but not the smartest right now.
Instead, he decided to boost his offense.
[Do you wish to consume 5 Evolution Points to evolve "Great Fireball"?]
Ding!
[You have evolved "Great Fireball" (Rare) to "Scorching Fireball" (Elite)]
[Current Evolution Points: 3]
---
[Scorching Fireball (Elite): Conjure a scorching fireball that deals 300% → 400% of Spirit. 20 → 15 (7.5)-seconds cooldown.]
---
"Not bad at all."
With his remaining EP, he evolved another skill.
[Do you wish to consume 3 Evolution Points to evolve "Venom Crystal"?]
Ding!
[You have evolved "Venom Crystal" (Uncommon) to "Toxic Crystal" (Rare)]
[Current Evolution Points: 0]
---
[Toxic Crystal (Rare): Summon a poisonous crystal that deals exactly 100 → 150 damage, it also applies the "Poison" status effect. 12 → 10 (5)-seconds cooldown.]
[Poison: deals 15% → 20% of damage received for 5 seconds.]
---
With two evolved attack skills, his damage output had skyrocketed. He felt unstoppable.
And then he noticed the loot on the ground.
---
[Flame Ring (Rare): +6 Spirit, +15 Fire Element Resistance. Requirement: Level 3.]
[Storage Backpack (Uncommon): Adds 5 slots to your backpack, allowing you to hold more items.]
---
"Perfect!" Stark slipped the ring onto his hand.
A small ember flickered along its edge, glowing faintly.
Specialized items like this were good in the early game.
With the added fire resistance, Stark could tank fire attacks much more easily.
He also equipped the [Storage Backpack], increasing his holding capacity.
He clenched his fist and smirked. "I’ll be level 5 in no time."
Without hesitation, he pushed deeper into the Shadow Forest.ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ꜰʀᴏᴍ ɴovel(ꜰ)ɪre.nᴇt
Along the way, he unleashed his new skills on every monster he saw.
At level 4, most enemies had around 1,500 HP.
A single strike from Stark, whether [Toxic Crystal] or [Scorching Fireball], was enough to wipe them out.
The only problem was the Evolution Points.
Normal monsters almost never dropped them.
Stark racked up kills, but not a single EP fell.
Still, it wasn’t a waste. His EXP bar climbed steadily.
And soon, he found something much better than common mobs.
---
[Cursed Tree (Level 4)]
[Rank: Uncommon (Boss)]
[HP: 7,500]
---
This proved just how much rank mattered.
After all, the flame fox had one level lower than the cursed tree, but because of its higher rank after evolving, it had the same HP, and almost the same strength.
Regardless, Stark lifted his staff and launched a [Scorching Fireball].
Some monsters could have elemental weaknesses to specific skills, and for the cursed tree, it was obviously weak to fire.
When you dealt an attack to a monster that had a weakness against it, it deals 1.5x more damage.
Fwshhh! BOOM!
-2,760!
A massive hit. Nearly a third of the tree’s health gone in one shot.
It tried to retaliate, swinging its massive branches at him.
Stark dodged, weaving around its sluggish strikes, before hurling another fireball.
Then another.
BOOM! BOOM!
The cursed tree roared as flames engulfed it, its bark blackening and cracking until it finally collapsed.
Ding!
---
[You have killed "Cursed Tree (Level 4 Uncommon-Rank Boss)"]
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 5!]
[You have gained 5 points in all of your attributes, and 5 free points to distribute.]
[You have gained 2 Evolution Points!]
[You have gained 3 Lives.]
---
Stark frowned slightly.
"I gained less EP than with the fox, even though this thing was higher level."
He thought for a moment.
Maybe it wasn’t level that determined EP drops. Maybe it was rank.
He crouched beside the corpse and activated [Hand of Avarice].
The shadowy hand reached out, but this time it fizzled out.
["Hand of Avarice" has failed.]
’It currently has a 75% of success,’ he thought, ’But if I evolve it one more time... will it become 100%?’
But at that moment, a skill book dropped from the cursed tree and made Stark’s light up with surprise.
[Skill Book: Vine Swing (Uncommon). Mage-type skill book. Requirement: Level 4.]
"New skill book for my class!" Stark’s grin widened.
Ding!
[You have learned the skill "Vine Swing."]
---
[Vine Swing (Uncommon): Summons a small vine from the ground that will swing with immense force at a target. Deals 100 damage + 100% Spirit. 40 (20)-seconds cooldown.]
---
"Three attack skills now." Stark clenched his fist.
Better yet, he could evolve the vine skill to rare-rajo later once he collected more EP.
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have unlocked the "Novice Town #783’s" Teleportation Array!]
Level 2 had unlocked the level leaderboards.
Level 5 unlocked the teleportation array.
And level 10 would be the next milestone.
[Go back to the town to activate it!]
"Maybe later," he muttered. "For now, I need levels and items to sell."
With his new skill and his boosted firepower, Stark marched deeper into the Shadow Forest, eyes gleaming.

chapters.title: Chapter 11: The Eternal Game is Real, Oblivion’s Reputation
chapters.content:
Chapter 11: Chapter 11: The Eternal Game is Real, Oblivion’s Reputation
Stark had already pushed himself to level 5.
