His movements through the shadow forest were calm, efficient, and merciless.
While he farmed alone, news began spreading across the world: the very first batch of players had finally reached level 3.
And that single milestone changed everything.
Ding!
[You can return to reality.]
For the first time, people realized the first part of the "tutorial" had an endpoint.
Those who managed to reach level 3 could leave [Eternal Soul].
They could return to their real bodies, then come back whenever they wanted.
Whenever someone was dragged into [Eternal Soul], their bodies in the real world would disappear as they were transported to this other realm.
Family members and friends who witnessed it were thrown into panic.
Some people outright refused to sleep, terrified that they would vanish forever.
And then, those level 3 players finally returned.
Their words only made the confusion worse.
"After falling asleep, we were... transported somewhere. It’s called [Eternal Soul]."
"We had to fight monsters. And there were systems, stats, levels, all of that."
"Basically like a game? How does that even make sense?"
"And it can make you stronger, what?"
"That system of lives is pretty weird, not gonna lie, but I don’t wanna find out what happens if your lives reach zero."
...
The [Teleportation Array] in novice towns worked in a two-way manner.
Meaning that even if Stark lit up the array in his town, it was useless as the others towns needed someone to reach level 5 and activate it.
That was why he wasn’t in much of a rush.
Moreover, Stark wanted to reach level 10 as quickly as possible.
That would allow him to leave this small novice town behind and enter the next stage, where the true beginning of [Eternal Soul] awaited.
He resumed his hunting in the shadow forest, cutting down wave after wave of monsters with precise blasts of magic.
Though while doing so, his thoughts drifted to Max and Seren.
’We spawned in the same town in my past life, but I’m pretty sure this one is different.’
They were at the top of his kill list after all, so finding their town and teleporting there to kill them would be the best thing he could do.
Finding that town would be difficult though.
A flicker of cold killing intent sharpened his eyes.
’But I’ll find it, no matter what, and if I can’t... then I’ll do it in the real world.’
Half an hour passed, and Stark had finally reached level 6.
He was aware that he had points to allocate.
[Free Points to Allocate: 15]
He paused for a moment, glancing at the glowing notification.
As a mage, he didn’t need strength.
His constitution was still low, yes, but survivable.
What he needed most was sharper magic and faster reflexes.
"Seven into Agility. Eight into Spirit," he muttered.
Power flowed into him immediately.
His body felt lighter, his mind clearer, his spells sharper.
One by one, the ferocious monsters in the eyes of most players were instantly killed by Stark.
...
Meanwhile, in the real world, official reports were already being made.
"Be careful of [Eternal Soul]."
That was the main message in the report.
But people couldn’t avoid sleeping forever.
Plus, they couldn’t resist the pull of the game.
Speculation began spreading online.
In addition to that, the top players across the world were making the news.
"I’m telling you, that Oblivion guy is a transmigrator."
"What the fuck are you even talking about?"
"Think about it, he reached level 3 and didn’t leave immediately, he definitely knows something!"
"Man... stop reading so many novels and get your act straight."
Several instances of people losing all their lives and dying were recorded.
The number was rather low as this was only the start of the game, but people already began to take it seriously.
But of course, they didn’t know that the real chaos was yet to come.
...
Far away, Max and Seren spawned together in [Novice Town #637].
Unlike most unlucky beginners, both of them hit the jackpot.
They both got [Hidden Classes], after all!
Seren awakened as a [Life Priest], wielding the [Healing of Divinity] talent, an S-Rank ability that amplified her healing magic to absurd levels.
Max became a [Blood Warrior], with the SS-Rank talent [Blood is Fuel].
The more blood he shed, the stronger he became.
Every cut, every drop, only fueled his rage and power.
Together, they were terrifying.
Seren’s radiant healing kept Max alive through impossible fights, while Max’s raw ferocity shredded anything in his path.
They could already handle level 3 monsters without help.
And Stark knew all too well how dangerous they would become.
In his past life, he had fought alongside them.
Seren’s timely heals had saved them countless times.
Being a [Life Priest] also didn’t mean she couldn’t do damage by the way.
Later in the game, priests could actually deal a lot of damage with their attacks.
As for Max, his strength carried them through battles they should never have survived.
But their flaws... those were burned into Stark’s memory as well.
Max was arrogant. Overconfident.
His ego pushed them into reckless battles, and more often than not, Stark had been the one forced to clean up the mess.
Seren, though competent, sometimes indulged him too much.
Petty arguments, wasted time, near-death experiences, all because of them.Tʜe source of this ᴄontent ɪs NoᴠᴇFɪre.nᴇt
This time, Stark had no intention of enduring it again.
He would grow stronger than either of them, then crush them when the time was right.
...
Back in [Novice Town #783], Stark returned from another long hunt with his backpack stuffed full of loot.
Thanks to his [Storage Backpack], he had brought back fifteen valuable items.
He did a quick calculation.
If he sold everything, he’d earn at least 120 Lives.
Considering that all his monster farming had only netted him nineteen extra Lives, these lives would be substantial!
Still, before opening shop, Stark made his way to the town square.
There it was, the [Teleportation Array].
A swirling formation of runes etched into the stone, glowing with faint blue light.
He placed his hand against it.
---
[Congratulations, you have activated the Teleportation Array of Novice Town #783.]
[Novice Town #783 is now connected to other towns. You may teleport once per day for free.]
[You have gained 1 Prestige Point!]
---
After doing that, many eyes fell on Stark, and he quickly turned around, a small smile on his face.
He set up his stall, laying out the fifteen rare items one by one under the envious gazes of others.
After all, now that [Eternal Soul] was confirmed to be real and something supernatural, who wouldn’t be jealous?
"Holy crap, it’s Oblivion!"
"Hell yeah, I prepared lives just for this moment..."
"Did you hear about that [PrinceLucas] guy? He bought [Shadow Slash] from Oblivion and shot to second place on the leaderboard!"
"Yeah, he’s been praising Oblivion non-stop!"
A crowd formed almost instantly.
Everyone knew that Oblivion’s loot came from bosses, monsters far too difficult for most players at this stage.
His gear was rare, affordable, and always worth the price.
Within three minutes, everything was sold.
Players left satisfied, holding their new treasures like priceless artifacts.
Stark glanced at his balance.
[Lives: 149 → 284]
His lips curved upward.
’More than expected!’
But before leaving, he stood and raised his voice, letting it carry across the square.
"If any of you have better backpacks or storage rings," he said slowly, "I’m willing to buy them."

chapters.title: Chapter 12: Small Space Ring, Player Killers are Here
chapters.content:
Chapter 12: Chapter 12: Small Space Ring, Player Killers are Here
Right after shouting about wanting items with more storage, a beautiful girl in a robe walked toward Stark, her staff in hand.
He recognized her instantly.
It was Starfall, the same girl from David’s group he had seen when saving them from the Shadow Bear King.
She wasn’t just any mage either. She carried a hidden class called [Star Prophet], which made her far stronger than a normal spellcaster.
Her hair had a soft orange tint, and her golden eyes sparkled like the stars in her class name.
If Stark remembered correctly, her real name was Grace Stargazer.
"I think I found something related to what you need..." she said with a calm smile, extending her hand toward him.
Stark’s eyes immediately shifted to what she was holding. A small silver ring glimmered on her palm.
---
[Small Space Ring (Rare): +12 storage slots, does not occupy a backpack slot.]
---
Seeing the item, Stark’s eyes widened in shock.
This was huge.
Every player could carry a maximum of three backpacks at once.
For example, Stark right now had his normal backpack and his storage backpack, which gave him five extra slots.
That meant he had two backpacks equipped already.
Later in the game, there would be some incredible items, massive bags, enchanted vaults, dimensional gear, that could hold hundreds of items at once.
But the [Small Space Ring] was extremely special for the simple reason it didn’t occupy a backpack slot.
It was pure bonus storage. An extra 12 slots, on top of everything else.
Stark clenched his fist as he thought about how rare it was.
Sure, maybe it could drop from monsters, but if it did, the chances had to be abysmally low.
And since this was the "lowest" variant of it, the higher ones had to be even harder to come by.
He raised his head and asked seriously, "How much do you want for that?"
Such an item wasn’t just about convenience.
It meant more loot carried on long runs, more items sold later, and more profit overall.
Grace shook her head lightly. "I don’t want your lives."
Then she smiled a little wider. "But... I do want your help killing a special boss that appeared."
Stark’s eyes twitched.
’Special boss?’
He knew exactly what that meant.
Special bosses only appeared for short periods of time, and they were always dangerous.
But they also dropped some incredible loot. A win-win situation.
"Alright," Stark nodded without hesitation.
He couldn’t afford to let an opportunity like this pass by.
But he needed to get there first, since these bosses disappeared if not killed by the end of the time.
Without another word, he tapped his panel and sent her a friend request.
Ding!
[Player "Starfall" has accepted your friend request!]
Almost immediately afterward...
[Player "Starfall" has sent you a private message!]
[Starfall: I’m so happy you can help us out! (ﾉ◕ヮ◕)ﾉ]
Stark stared at the message blankly, then let out a quiet sigh.
Another message popped up.
[Starfall: I didn’t want to say it out loud, but it was a level 7 elite-rank boss... so I know nobody but you could beat it! (っ◞‸◟c)]
[Stark: What about its name?]
[Starfall: No idea, I ran as fast as I could the moment I saw it. But it was some weird creature on a small ship.]
A small ship? That didn’t ring any bells for him.
Even in his past life, his encounters with special bosses had been rare.
He couldn’t recall anything like what she described.
"I can kill it," Stark said firmly. "If the boss drops equipment or skill books your team can use, I’ll give those to you. Everything else belongs to me."
Grace thought about it for a moment, then nodded.
It was fair. And honestly, for a level 7 elite-rank boss, she doubted anyone else in this entire novice town could even scratch it.
Stark wasn’t completely confident either.
But that made it even more tempting to test himself.
"Okay then," Grace said cheerfully. "Let’s wait for the others to come back first~"
"There’s no need," Stark replied flatly. "Take me there now. I’ll fight it alone."
Grace blinked at him in disbelief.
She knew he was strong, the strongest player in the whole town.New ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄhapters are published on No(ᴠ)ᴇlFire.nᴇt
But still... taking on an elite boss by himself?
She bit her lip. He was insane.
But Stark’s thoughts were different.
’Special bosses in the starting zones are the easiest ones. Can’t waste this chance.’
...
A few minutes later, Stark and Grace left [Novice Town #783] and headed back toward the Shadow Forest.
Grace walked beside him, her robe fluttering with each step.
She glanced at him hesitantly.
"So you’re really going to... fight it alone? Even though you’re a mage?"
Grace herself was a mage, and she knew her limits.
Their class had high damage, but weak defenses and combat capabilities.
One solid hit from an elite boss could wipe them out instantly.
Stark didn’t get a chance to answer.
His sharp senses suddenly picked up something behind them.
His eyes narrowed.
"Someone’s following us."
"Hah?" Grace tightened her grip on her staff.
Her voice trembled slightly, but Stark was already certain.
’Player killers... they’re already here.’
As one might assume, once news spread that [Eternal Soul] was real, people would do anything for lives.
Monsters were one way. But killing other players worked too.
When killing a player, you would get the number of lives corresponding to loss rate of the zone.
It was less rewarding, but a much safer method to get lives.
After all, other players weren’t as wild or unpredictable as monsters.
Stark had run into these scum plenty of times in his past life, and he hadn’t liked them then either.
He stopped walking and turned around.
Five figures stepped out from behind the trees.
"Oh, looks like he noticed us."
"They must be strong. Stay sharp."
"Doesn’t matter. It’s five against two. And they’re mages—"
Vine Swing!
Before the last one could even finish, Stark moved.
A vine burst from the ground and whipped through the air like a serpent.
It slammed into all five players in an instant.
Boom!
Damage numbers exploded above their heads.
-1,640! -1,640! -1,640!1
The five didn’t even have time to react before their bodies shattered into particles.
Ding!
[You have gained 5 Lives!]
’Heh.’
Stark smirked faintly.
But he didn’t waste time.
He turned back around, grabbed Grace by the waist, and hoisted her up onto his shoulder.
"H-Hah?!"
She squeaked in surprise, but Stark was already dashing forward at incredible speed.
His agility was sitting at 47 now.
Carrying her barely slowed him down at all.
In fact, it was much faster this way.
The special boss wouldn’t wait forever.
Grace held onto him tightly, her eyes wide. ’Is a mage supposed to be this fast? This is insane...’
Meanwhile, Stark calmly raised his staff while running.
Without missing a step, he fired precise spells at monsters that tried to block their way.
Ding!
[You have gained 7 Lives!]
[You have gained 1 Evolution Point.]
’Nice,’ Stark thought with satisfaction.
Ten minutes later, they arrived.
Stark slowed down and gently set Grace back on her feet.
She looked a little reluctant, but said nothing.
They were standing on top of a cliff now.
From here, the view stretched wide.
Stark’s eyes immediately locked on the swamp below.
Floating across its dark waters was a strange, creaking ship.
And on that ship... something was waiting.
The special boss of the Shadow Forest.
100 damage + 48 spirit + 10 from staff and + 6 from flame ring = 164 x 10

chapters.title: Chapter 13: Special Boss, The Swamp Revenant
chapters.content:
Chapter 13: Chapter 13: Special Boss, The Swamp Revenant
From where he stood on the cliff, Stark could see the status panel of the special boss below.
---
[Swamp Revenant (Level 7)]
[Rank: Elite (Special Boss)]
[HP: 25,000]
[Countdown: 18 minutes 47 seconds]
---
"Less than twenty minutes..." Stark muttered, narrowing his eyes. "That should be enough, as long as I don’t die."
He took a slow, steady breath, forcing himself to stay calm.
His heart was already pounding in excitement.
Facing an elite boss this early was dangerous, maybe even stupid, but if he won... the rewards would be great.
Next to him, Grace, better known as Starfall, looked pale.
She clutched her staff tightly as her gaze stayed fixed on the monster below.
On the swamp, an old half-sunken ship drifted aimlessly.
Standing at its center was a skeleton wrapped in rotting robes, holding a staff of blackened wood.
Blue-green fire flickered in its hollow skull, and the entire swamp seemed to shudder under its presence.
"Wait here," Stark said firmly, turning to Grace. "Be careful of anything that comes near. I’ll deal with the boss."
Grace hesitated for only a moment before nodding.
"Alright... I’ll hold back monsters if they approach. Good luck."
Stark gave her a small nod, then found a narrow path leading down the cliffside.
His boots crunched against rocks and damp soil as he descended.
But just as his foot stepped into the muddy ground, a system message appeared before his eyes.
---
[Due to the influence of the "Swamp Revenant," this area has become more dangerous.]
[Lives loss rate: 50]
---
"Tch." Stark clicked his tongue. "Figures."
The swamp itself had been corrupted by the revenant.
Anyone who died here would lose fifty lives on the spot.
That meant even if someone had exactly fifty lives left, they’d be erased instantly, gone forever.
That was the cruelty of [Eternal Soul]. No mercy, no second chances.
Stark had a good stockpile of lives, but it wasn’t something he could waste carelessly.
If he died now, not only would he lose them, but the special boss would vanish before he could even try again.
He gripped his staff tightly. "Alright... let’s do this."
The ship creaked in the distance.
The revenant raised its flaming skull as if it could already sense Stark’s presence.
Before giving it the chance to attack first, Stark pointed his staff.
Scorching Fireball!
Fwish! BOOM!
A blazing orb shot through the air and slammed into the revenant.
Flames engulfed its skeletal body, and damage numbers floated above its head.
-2,560!
Stark’s eyes widened. "Insane!"
That was just his base damage of his fireball, boosted by the 400% Spirit amplification from his build and the advantage of being Level 6.
"Let’s keep it up."
He swung his staff again.
Toxic Crystal!
A shard of poisonous energy shot forward, slamming into the revenant’s ribcage.
Green mist seeped into its bones, and the poison effect took hold.
-1,500! -300! -300!
In just two spells, he had shaved off nearly 6,000 HP.
The swamp water rippled violently as the revenant raised its staff in response.
Flames burned brighter in its hollow sockets.
"Here it comes," Stark muttered, already moving back.
The revenant slammed its staff into the deck of its ship.
Water Surge!
Fwoooosh!
The swamp exploded as thick columns of water shot upward like geysers.
Dozens of them burst in rapid succession, surrounding Stark in a deadly cage.
One wrong step and he’d be obliterated instantly.
He sprinted sideways, mud splashing beneath his boots as he weaved between the surging water.
His eyes tracked the timing, his instincts calculating each movement a second before it happened.
He had dodged attacks like these thousands of times in his past life.
To him, this was nothing new.
But to a normal player, this would have been instant death.
Stark rolled to the side as another column exploded, droplets raining down around him.
His breathing was steady, his focus absolute.
"Too predictable." He smirked, landing lightly on his feet.
The revenant hissed, tapping its staff again.
This time, a shockwave rippled outward across the ship and into the swamp.
Revenant’s Call!
The swamp began to bubble.
Thick, wooden arms emerged from it, followed by twisted humanoid bodies made entirely of roots and bark.
Ten [Tree Revenants] dragged themselves onto the shore, their glowing green eyes fixed on Stark.
---
[Tree Revenant (Level 5)]
[Rank: Rare]
[HP: 5,000]
---
"Figures..." Stark muttered, raising his staff.
Vine Swing!
CRACK!
A massive vine erupted from the ground in front of him, sweeping across the swamp in a wide arc.
It smashed into multiple Tree Revenants at once, knocking them back with tremendous force.
-1,640! -1,640!
The damage wasn’t as high as his other skills, but the range made up for it.
The Tree Revenants stumbled but quickly regained their footing, rushing him all at once.
It took a few minutes, but Stark managed to get rid of every [Tree Revenant].
By the time the last one fell, the Swamp Revenant had already lost most of its health. Its bar was below 5,000.
But then... the special boss raised its staff high into the air.
The flames in its skull grew to an almost blinding intensity.
"Oh no," Stark muttered, his expression hardening.
A massive wave of spectral energy burst outward from the swamp, covering the entire area.
Soul Wave!
The air turned icy cold as the wave surged forward.
Anything it touched would be paralyzed and burned away.
And there was no dodging it as it covered the entire battlefield.
"Damn it," Stark hissed. "Looks like I don’t have a choice."
A system prompt appeared before him.
[Do you wish to consume 3 Evolution Points to evolve "Magic Shield"?]
"Yes!"
He had just enough.
[You have evolved "Magic Shield" (Uncommon) to "Magic Barrier" (Rare)]
---
[Magic Barrier (Rare): Summon a barrier around the user that can endure a few attacks, if damage is too strong, it will break, 50 → 40 (20)-seconds cooldown.]
---
"The name changed..." Stark smirked. "Good."
He spun his staff in his hand and used the ability.
Magic Barrier!
A translucent dome of shimmering energy wrapped around him just as the Soul Wave slammed into his position.
BOOOOM!
The force rattled his bones, cracks spreading across the surface of the barrier.
For a moment, he thought it might break.
But then... the wave passed. The barrier held.
"Perfect." Stark grinned.
The revenant staggered on its ship, its flames flickering weaker than before.
It was running out of strength.
"Time to finish this."
Meanwhile, up on the cliff, Grace swung her staff.
Lightning Strike! Crack!
A bolt of lightning fell from the sky, frying a group of two monsters that had been moving toward Stark’s location.
Damage numbers popped up.
-128! -137! -127!
She grit her teeth and kept casting.
Even if she couldn’t help against the boss, she could at least make sure no stray monsters interrupted him.
Stark noticed her support from afar and gave a faint smile. "Not bad."
Then he turned back to the revenant and raised his staff for the final blow.
Scorching Fireball!
Fwoooosh! BOOM!
The blazing orb exploded against the revenant’s chest.
Its HP dropped to zero.
The skeleton shrieked, the fire in its skull sputtering out before the bones collapsed into a heap.
Its staff clattered against the deck of the ship.
Ding!
---
[You have killed "Swamp Revenant" (Level 7 Elite-Rank Special Boss).]
[You have gained 4,000 experience points.]
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 7 → Level 8!]
[You have gained 10 points in all of your attributes, and 10 free points to distribute.]
[You have gained 7 Evolution Points.]
[You have gained 39 Lives.]
---
Stark lowered his staff, then he looked at the glowing panels hovering in front of him and let out a low laugh.
"Two levels, seven evolution points, and almost forty lives..." His grin widened. "That was worth it."
The Swamp Revenant had been completely subjugated.

chapters.title: Chapter 14: First Elite-Rank Kill Announcement, Revenant Bell
chapters.content:
Chapter 14: Chapter 14: First Elite-Rank Kill Announcement, Revenant Bell
Right as he killed the Swamp Revenant, a global announcement echoed in the mind of all [Eternal Soul] players.
---
[Player "Oblivion (Novice Town #783)" is the first to kill an elite-rank special boss.]
[You have gained 3 Prestige Point!]
---
The announcement played three times in a row, ringing clear in the minds of all.
For a moment, the entire player base was stunned.
"Holy shit, an elite-rank boss?"
"Who the hell is that Oblivion guy?"
"Don’t you see? It even tells us which novice town he’s from!"
"That means we can go there as soon as we’re level 5!"
...
Both in reality and inside [Eternal Soul], the announcement shook the world.
Announcements of this scale were extremely rare.
They only appeared when a player accomplished something absurd.
And to Stark... this was the very first time his name had ever been announced to the entire world.
Since he was the only one who had dealt damage to the revenant, Grace’s name wasn’t mentioned, of course.
The boss was gone.
Its body had completely disintegrated, leaving behind scattered loot glowing faintly on the deck of the ship.
Stark was just about to step forward to claim his rewards when—
"There he is!"
"We found him! With this many players, there’s no way he can survive!"
"He’s a mage, don’t let him escape!"
Dozens of players rushed out of the swamp and surrounded him in a loose circle.
One of them lifted his hand and summoned a [Ghost Eagle].
The spectral bird screeched before flying high above, locking onto Stark’s location so he couldn’t run.
"If we kill him, we get all the loot, right?"
"Doesn’t matter, let’s just get rid of him first!"
Stark stopped in place, glancing between them and the loot on the ship.
He wasn’t worried.
The system protected his drops, since he had done all the damage, no one else could take them until the five-minute [Protection Period] ended.
The [Ghost Eagle] circled above, its eyes glowing as it kept track of his every move.
Stark arched an eyebrow.
"Are they stupid? I’m level 8. They should know that by now."
Still, if they wanted to throw themselves at him, he wouldn’t mind.
He calmly raised his staff.
"Get ready!" one of the players barked. "Everyone activate your shield skills at the same time! If we stack defenses, we can tank his spells!"
"Once his cooldowns are down, a mage is basically useless!"
It was actually a decent strategy.
For a brief moment, Stark was almost impressed.
But they didn’t know he wasn’t just a normal mage.
VINE SWING!
A massive vine burst out of the swampy ground, snapping forward with terrifying force.
The tanks at the front braced themselves, shields raised high, activating their defense skills in perfect unison.
But...
Fwish! Slam!
-870! -870! -870!
Even with their defenses halving the damage, it wasn’t nearly enough.
The impact crushed them instantly, their visions fading to black as they collapsed one by one.
Their confident expressions vanished in an instant, replaced by stunned disbelief as death claimed them.
The [Protection Period] for items was only five minutes.
In the future, situations like this would happen more and more often, players ambushing others for loot, lives, or revenge.
Ding!
[You have gained 17 Lives!]
They were lucky the death penalty in this zone had reset to 1 life after the revenant’s death.
If it had stayed at the higher rate, most of them would have died.
Stark glanced up toward the cliff.
Grace was still busy, firing spells at the monsters she was fighting.
’I’ll help her later. First, the loot.’
He turned back to the ship but paused mid-step.
[Do you wish to consume 7 Evolution Point to evolve "Hand of Avarice"?]
"Perfect timing." He confirmed.
Ding!
[You have evolved "Hand of Avarice" (Elite) to "Hand of Avarice" (Epic)]
[Current Evolution Points: 0]
---
[Hand of Avarice (Epic): Can be used on corpses, has a 75% → 100% chance to obtain another loot reward.]
---
"Haha!" Stark grinned wide. "I knew it!"
Now the success rate had jumped from seventy-five percent to one hundred, guaranteed extra loot every single time.
That said, it made him curious.
What could the higher ranks possibly look like?
Going from Epic to Legendary required ten points, though.
Evolution was getting more and more expensive.
Stark made a mental note to stockpile points for the future.
For now, he raised his staff, pointing it toward the ship at the swamp’s center.
"Hand of Avarice!"
A dark spectral hand shot from his staff, descending upon the ship.
Ding!
---
[You have gained 4 Evolution Points!]
[You have gained 27 Lives.]
---
"Not bad." Stark nodded with satisfaction.
[Lives: 379]
His stockpile was finally becoming respectable.
At this pace, he’d break past 500 soon.
He leapt onto the ship, boots splashing against the damp deck.
Loot shimmered faintly in piles across the wooden boards.
One by one, he checked each drop, scanning for anything of value.
Most of it wasn’t particularly impressive.
Until—
A faint golden glow caught his eye.
"A special item?" Stark’s heartbeat quickened as he picked it up.
---
[Revenant Bell (Special Item): When carried, death will not result in any lives loss. 6-hours cooldown.]
[Soul Shockwave (Active Skill): Shake the revenant bell to cause a 3-second stun effect to all enemies within a 100-meter radius. 10-minutes cooldown.]
---
"Incredible..." Stark whispered, eyes shining.
Special items were unique drops tied only to specific monster types.
They were extremely rare.
As the game progressed, such items would become unbelievably rare, worth tens of thousands of lives on the trading markets.
And this one even had a powerful active ability tied to it.
The cooldowns weren’t halved, of course, his class passive only affected spells.
[Class Passive #3: All your spells’ cooldowns are reduced by half.]
Still, the effects were absurd.
Not losing lives once every six hours could easily save him once in dangerous zones.
In regions where players could lose thousands of lives per death, this item would be priceless.
Admittedly, it wouldn’t work in places like the [Judgment Battlefield] or similat zones to it though.
Instant death didn’t take lives after all, it just killed you.
But even with that limitation, it was one of the best early-game items he could have asked for.
Normally, this would have been the end of his loot.
But thanks to [Hand of Avarice], one extra reward appeared.
And this one was perfectly suited to his class.ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ ɴo(v)elFɪre.ɴet
---
[Revenant Staff (Elite): Mage-type weapon. Spirit +38, Agility +17, Casting Speed +25%. Requirement: Level 7]
---
Stark’s eyes widened again.
His old staff had only been uncommon rank.
This was two entire tiers higher.
He swapped it immediately, gripping the new weapon and feeling its power surge through him.
Casting would be faster, smoother, deadlier.
The rest of the loot wasn’t meant for his class except for a necklace.
Whatever other item Grace could use, he’d let her have it.
After all, the [Small Space Ring] still outweighed everything else combined, except for the special item.
That was his true prize today.
Tucking the Revenant Bell safely away, Stark turned, ready to head back.

chapters.title: Chapter 15: Vine Smash, Exchanging Items with Grace
chapters.content:
Chapter 15: Chapter 15: Vine Smash, Exchanging Items with Grace
The majority of the loot dropped by the [Swamp Revenant] were rare and elite-rank items.
The rare ones were fine, but the elite-rank pieces were useless to sell for now.
Not because they weren’t valuable, just the opposite.
Nobody at this stage could actually afford them.
Still, Stark wasn’t disappointed.
[Do you wish to consume 3 Evolution Point to evolve "Vine Swing"?]
"Yes!"
Ding!
[You have evolved "Vine Swing" (Uncommon) to "Vine Smash" (Rare)]
---
[Vine Smash (Rare): Summons a vine from the ground that will smash with immense force at a target, it will deal 100 → 200 damage + 100% → 150% of spirit. 40 → 35 (17.5)-seconds cooldown.]
---
’Nice,’ Stark nodded, satisfied, ’The damage can rival those of the others now.’
With that done, he gathered up the items, storing everything between his backpack and storage backpack, then left the swamp behind.
Ding!
[You have sent a message to "Starfall"]
[Oblivion: I’m done, I’ll come back up and then I can give you some of the items!]
[Starfall: Thanks... I struggled against those monsters (ಥ﹏ಥ)]
[Oblivion: The fact you actually killed them is good enough.]
She had been fighting two level 3 monsters earlier.
It wasn’t easy, but her [Star Prophet] class gave her the tools to survive and take them down on her own.
Climbing back up the cliff, Stark soon found her sitting on a rock, catching her breath.
...
At the same time...
Slash!
Max’s sword cut through a level 4 uncommon-rank monster.
-473!
Thanks to his class and his talent, every blood he shed raised his damage.
With each swing, he hit harder than before, allowing him to tear through enemies even at his level.Follow current ɴᴏᴠᴇʟs on novᴇl(ꜰ)ire.ɴet
And when he did take hits...
Divine Healing!
Seren raised her scepter, her light wrapping around Max and restoring him to full health in an instant.
"Did you see that Oblivion guy?" Seren asked while keeping her eyes on Max’s fight. "He’s in another town, judging from the announcements."
"What of it?" Max grunted, hacking into another monster. "Eventually, we’ll catch up."
"Hm..." Seren nodded slowly. "I just hope it doesn’t take too long."
"We only need to be level 5 to use the teleportation array," Max reminded her, cleaving into another beast. "Let’s focus on that, then see what happens after."
"Agreed!" Seren replied brightly.
The two of them kept grinding, eager and full of excitement for what awaited in this new world.
Their classes and talents gave them confidence that they could achieve greatness.
"Do you think Stark actually entered the game?" Seren asked suddenly.
Max barked out a laugh. "That guy? He’s probably already dead or running scared. No way he changed overnight like that."
"If he ever shows up again," Seren grinned, "we’ll make him beg to join us. Maybe we’ll even let him be our dog."
"Haha, sure."
But what they didn’t know... was that Oblivion, the most talked-about player in the world, and Stark were the same person.
...
Stark moved quickly through the [Shadow Forest], the [Revenant Bell] hanging around his neck.
Grace was in his arms as he carried her toward town.
"I’ve got all the items," he told her calmly. "We’ll head back and exchange there."
Grace nodded lightly, relieved.
Before long, they reached [Novice Town #783].
Stark put her down outside, not wanting her to feel embarrassed by being carried the whole way.
"As agreed, I’ll give your team most of the stuff," he said, "but I’m keeping some of the mage gear."
Grace nodded again.
He handed over a fair portion of the items, keeping the other half for himself.
Then, seeing her weapon, he also gave her the [Shadow Staff] he had been using earlier.
"W-Wow!" Grace’s eyes lit up as she held it. "Thank you!"
He wasn’t finished.
Alongside it, he gave her a rare-rank necklace that added +15 spirit and boosted mana recovery by +3 every second.
Grace blinked in surprise.
Honestly, she had expected him to scam her somehow, or at least hold back more.
Instead, he trusted her with the rest of the gear for David and their teammates.
"Thank you," she said, bowing slightly. "With this, my spells will be way stronger."
Stark only shook his head and smiled faintly. "It’s fine. We had a deal. Now, can I have the [Small Space Ring]?"
"Right!" Grace fumbled in her inventory and brought it out, placing it carefully in his hand.
"It’s not like I’ll be filling it anytime soon," she admitted with a smile.
Stark slid it onto his left hand.
[Small Space Ring (Rare): +12 storage slots, does not occupy a backpack slot.]
’That makes 27 storage slots total,’ Stark thought, ’Much easier.’
"Look, it’s Oblivion!"
"Holy crap, maybe he’s selling again! If he lists new gear, I want in..."
The people of the novice town were buzzing, and Stark couldn’t help but notice the shift.
In this life, his reputation was completely different.
He was not only the strongest in his town, possibly in the entire world, but he had also helped others by selling items they desperately needed.
He had earned respect.
’It doesn’t matter now, but later... it could be useful,’ Stark thought.
For now, his focus was simple: reaching level 10.
At that point, he could perform his [Class Advancement] and leave the [Novice Continent] behind to head to the true beginning of [Eternal Soul].
But he still needed two more levels.
He had already explored most of the [Shadow Forest], even fighting its hidden boss.
Normally, other players would grind experience by farming monsters.
But Stark remembered something.
From his past life... a memory resurfaced.
There was an entrance to a level 10 zone deep within this very forest.
The hardest zone in the entire [Novice Continent].
Back then, Seren and Max had refused to go.
It was too dangerous, and Stark had backed off with them.
But not this time. This time, he would enter alone.
If he could clear it, there was no doubt he would hit level 10.
...
Leaving town once more, Stark cut down every monster in his path, but their experience wasn’t enough to matter.
He rushed deeper, straight toward his destination.
He searched through the thick shadows until he found himself at the forest’s edge.
’It should be here... I’m sure of it.’
Minutes passed as he scanned the area.
Then, finally, he saw it.
A grin spread across his face. "Heh. Just like before. Still here. I doubt anyone else has even thought of trying."
In truth, even he hesitated for a moment.
But he was stronger now.
With his class, his gear, and his skills, Stark had confidence.
A narrow cave entrance yawned before him.
The moment he stepped close...
Ding!
[You are about to enter a dangerous level 10 zone: "Abandoned Temple of Fate"]
[Once you enter, you cannot leave unless you die.]
This warning had stopped countless players before.
Even Seren and Max had turned away at this point.
But Stark? He didn’t slow.
The pressure rolling out of the cave only made his heart beat faster.
Without hesitation, he stepped inside.
Ding!
[You have entered the "Abandoned Temple of Fate"]
[Lives loss rate: 100]

chapters.title: Chapter 16: Secret Zone, Abandoned Temple of Fate
chapters.content:
Chapter 16: Chapter 16: Secret Zone, Abandoned Temple of Fate
[You have entered the "Abandoned Temple of Fate"]
[Lives loss rate: 100]
[Description: An abandoned temple previously dedicated to the "God of Fate", some believers still remain inside, corrupted and turned into monsters.]
---
’God of Fate,’ Stark’s eyes narrowed, a glint flashing in them. ’I remember the [Authority of Oblivion] mentioned that the [God of Oblivion] was feared by the others...’
If that was true, then the God of Fate had to be one of those beings.
And this temple, though abandoned, still carried that lingering presence.
This place was the hardest zone on the entire [Novice Continent].
That continent alone contained tens of thousands of novice towns players were in.
And this was the most dangerous zone in all of them.
Backing away wasn’t an option. He was already inside.
And here, death meant losing one hundred lives.
Almost nobody could afford that right now.
But Stark wasn’t worried.
He still had the [Revenant Bell], which would prevent him from losing any lives.
To him, the threat was far less terrifying than it would be for anyone else.
The entrance was a tight cave, damp and oppressive.
Stark walked through the dark passage for a long stretch, the silence only broken by his own footsteps.
Eventually, ahead in the distance, a faint light flickered.
The rough cave walls gradually transformed into carefully carved stone.
Strange symbols and faded murals decorated them, etched deep into the surface.
Stark slowed, brushing his hand across one of the carvings.
He had never seen anything like it before.
But without any knowledge of their meaning, he dismissed it and pressed forward.
Finally, he reached a small, narrow gate.
Passing through it, he stepped into a massive chamber.
The chamber was well constructed, ancient but still solid.
In the center stood a stone altar, tall and imposing, while multiple passageways branched out into deeper sections of the temple.
But what drew Stark’s focus were the two figures kneeling before the altar.
---
[Corrupted Fate Believer (Level 10)]
[Rank: Rare]
[HP: 15,000]
---
Two monsters, each with a massive health pool.
Just one of them was enough to overwhelm the average player.
Both were kneeling, their hands raised toward the altar, muttering in low voices that echoed eerily through the chamber.
Their bodies were ragged, clothes in tatters, and their eyes, completely black, with glowing purple pupils, radiated a sense of madness.
"..." Stark watched silently for a few seconds.
Then, without hesitation, he made his move.
Vine Smash!
The ground cracked as a thick vine shot upward, slamming into the two corrupted believers.
-3,530! -3,530!
The attack tore chunks of their health away, nearly a fifth in one strike.
Both believers stumbled, snapping their heads toward him.
Their twisted eyes locked onto Stark, and in that instant, their bodies trembled violently.
["Corrupted Fate Believers" have entered a "Berserk" state.]
"What?" Stark muttered, quickly pulling back just as one believer lunged at him with razor-sharp claws.
Normally, monsters only went berserk when enraged or at the brink of death.
But these two had gone berserk the very moment they looked at him.
’Is it because of the [Authority of Oblivion]?’ he thought grimly.ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ꜰʀᴏᴍ Novᴇ(l)Fɪre .ɴᴇt
A fireball formed in his hand, blazing with heat.
Scorching Fireball!
Boom!
-4,080! -4,080!
The explosion rocked the chamber, flames bursting across the believers’ bodies.
Their health plummeted again, but instead of slowing, their madness only grew.
If it were any other player, just one of these berserk believers would have been enough to end them instantly.
But Stark had the stats, the gear, and the experience to survive.
’I can’t afford to waste time.’
One believer leapt high, claws gleaming as it dove toward him.
Magic Barrier!
The barrier flared into existence just in time.
CRASH!
The impact cracked, but it bought Stark the split-second he needed to hurl a [Toxic Crystal] forward.
Poison mist spread instantly, eating away at the believer’s health.
But before he could follow up, the second believer was already upon him, claws swinging.
’Not today...’
Fwish! Clang!
Stark braced his staff, deflecting the strike.
The impact jolted through his arms, but the [Revenant Staff] was sturdy enough to handle it.
’A mage isn’t supposed to block attacks like this. But if I’m aiming to fight as a battle-mage, then I’d better start acting like one.’
Being a mage usually meant launching spells from afar.
But Stark knew very well there were some powerful spells that allowed for close-range battles.
Mages were extremely versatile, but as one might expect, these spells cost a lot of MP, and had huge cooldowns.
He shoved the believer back, then unleashed a chain of spells in rapid succession.
Toxic Crystal! Vine Smash! Scorching Fireball!
The combined assault tore through their weakened forms.
With a final shriek, both believers collapsed, their corrupted bodies disintegrating into motes of black mist.
Ding!
---
[You have killed "Corrupted Fate Believers (Level 10)"]
[You have gained 3,600 experience points.]
[You have gained 1 Evolution Point.]
[You have gained 18 Lives]
---
"Good," Stark grinned, "I should be able to get to level 10 soon."
Hand of Avarice!
A dark spectral hand emerged from his staff, wrapping around the believers’ remains.
Ding!
[You have obtained 13 Lives.]
[You have gained 1 Evolution Point!]
"Oh?" Stark’s eyes widened. "That’s better than I expected."
The monsters hadn’t dropped items, but he still came away with two evolution points.
That was worth more than loot to him.
Still, his mind returned to their strange behavior.
The way they had gone berserk just from looking at him...
"God of Oblivion," Stark muttered under his breath, ’Oh well.’
The temple wasn’t going to give him time to dwell on it.
Without hesitation, he advanced deeper.
Zones like this were built as labyrinths.
Long corridors twisted endlessly, forcing players to explore until they stumbled upon the exit.
At the very end would be a boss.
And the more dangerous the zone, the greater the rewards that boss would drop.
In his past life, Stark didn’t remember anyone clearing the [Abandoned Temple of Fate] in his novice town.
The risk of losing one hundred lives had been far too high.
Almost nobody had dared to try.
But this time, he would.
He turned a corner, the shadows pressing close around him.
And almost immediately—
"Ah, shit."
A group of corrupted believers was already charging his way, their bodies trembling as they entered berserk the moment they sensed his presence.
’So it really is the [Authority of Oblivion]... these things are reacting to me on sight.’
Stark sighed, raising his staff as his mana flared.
Scorching Fireball!
The blazing sphere hurtled forward, exploding in the narrow hallway and engulfing the believers in flames.
"This god really must’ve pissed off the others," Stark muttered as his grip tightened.
The thought drifted back to the panel he had seen when first obtaining the [Authority of Oblivion].
---
[Authority of Oblivion: A power sealed by the gods as they feared that its wielder, the "God of Oblivion", was too strong, its power surpasses anything in the universe, though you are not capable of wielding it yet.]
---
He still couldn’t use it, but it seemed like its influence was already showing in his new life.

chapters.title: Chapter 17: More Players in the Novice Town, Abandoned Fate Guardian
chapters.content:
Chapter 17: Chapter 17: More Players in the Novice Town, Abandoned Fate Guardian
While Stark was exploring the [Abandoned Temple of Fate], at the same time...
Fwish! Ding!
Many players finally began to cross the level 5 threshold, activating the [Teleportation Arrays] of their respective towns.
Of course, the so-called "strongest" players, the ones already at level 7 and even pushing into level 8, didn’t care.
They didn’t stop.
They were too busy grinding, too focused on leveling, fighting, and chasing power.
Their leveling speed and strength still couldn’t compare to Stark’s, but they were strong in their own right.
As for everyone else...
"Is this the town?"
"It is! Look, the number matches!"
"Holy shit... then where’s Oblivion?"
The moment players hit level 5, the very first thing they did was head to [Novice Town #783].
When a player reached level 5 and unlocked the teleportation array, all they needed to do was touch the circle of light, and a system panel would appear before their eyes:
---
[Where do you wish to teleport?]
[Novice Town #783]
[Novice Town #637]
[Novice Town #369]
---
And so on... dozens of towns, all nearly identical in structure, design, and layout.
But despite all being the same, one stood above the rest.
As expected, [Novice Town #783] was quickly becoming the most crowded town in the entire game.
The reason? Oblivion!
The legend that was starting to spread like wildfire.
Players from across different towns, hundreds at a time, chose to teleport straight there just to see the place where Oblivion was rumored to play.
"Why the hell are there so many people here?" David muttered as he logged in, his team standing behind him.
His brow furrowed. "Huh..."
He had taken a small break from [Eternal Soul].
Real life had pulled him away briefly, but he knew the truth: the optimal path was staying logged in, grinding, leveling.
Missing even a day meant falling behind.
And so here he was again, pulled back into the game.
Before he could say much else, Grace hurried over.
She didn’t waste time, rushing to his side and pressing several items into his hands.
"Here!" Grace beamed, grinning ear to ear. "Oblivion beat that special boss and told me to give you these."
The entire group froze, stunned as they examined the loot in their inventories.
The quality... the rarity... There were no words.
David and his team exchanged wide-eyed glances.
None of them had met Oblivion in person except for when he saved them, but at that moment, they didn’t need to.
They silently gave thanks in their hearts.
And while they were still reeling...
"Holy shit, look at those two!" someone in the crowd suddenly shouted.
"Yeah... they look crazy strong..."
Dozens of eyes turned, and murmurs spread like wildfire.
Two new players had just appeared inside the square.
Max and Seren.
The two stood tall, their presence dominating the plaza without effort.
Their levels glowed clearly above their heads, both at level 8, already brushing against level 9.
Their in-game IDs were just as flashy as their strength:
[GodOfViolence] for Max.
[DivineGoddess] for Seren.
"Alright..." Max cracked a grin, scanning the crowd. "Where’s Oblivion now?"
...
Back in the temple, Stark was in motion.
Ding!
---
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 9!]
[You have gained 5 points in all of your attributes, and 5 free points to distribute.]
---
After wiping out the last cluster of monsters in the temple, Stark had officially reached level 9.
Level 10 was already within sight.
He checked his progress bar.
He needed 10,000 experience to hit the next milestone, and he was already a little under halfway there.
Fifteen free points sat unused in his panel.
Stark left them unallocated for now.
It was better to wait, better to hold them for the perfect moment.
And then...
Ding!
[You have entered the "Final Chamber"]
The chamber opened before him like the maw of some forgotten god.
Massive marble pillars rose in the four corners, supporting a roof carved with murals and ancient lines of text.
On the walls, a strange giant symbol was engraved, the same one Stark had seen in fragments throughout the temple.
It was some sort of crimson eye that seemed to follow you.
The symbol of the [God of Fate].
But his focus locked on the center.
There, a three-meter tall stone statue stood motionless, carved into the shape of a warrior.
Behind it loomed a massive sealed door by the same symbol he saw everywhere in this zone, impossible to open without clearing what came before it.
The system panel confirmed his suspicion.
---
[Abandoned Fate Guardian (Level 10)]
[Rank: Elite (Boss)]
[HP: 50,000]
[A guardian that protects this temple even though it has been abandoned long ago.]
---
The true boss of the zone was here.
Stark narrowed his eyes. This was it.
No room for mistakes.
Without hesitation, he unleashed everything he had the moment the fight began.
Scorching Fireball! Toxic Crystal! Vine Swing!
Fwish! Boom! Crack!
-4,280! -1,500! -3,605!
Nearly a fifth of the boss’s health evaporated instantly under the onslaught.
But as expected, the poison effect of [Toxic Crystal] didn’t trigger since this was a statue.
The moment the attacks landed, the giant stirred.
Its head slowly tilted.
From the single hollow cavity carved where its eyes should’ve been, a pitch-black flame ignited.
One step.
BOOM!
Another.
BOOM!
Its fists, massive stone slabs, radiated raw destructive aura.
And then—
Rock Smash!
The guardian raised both arms high before slamming them into the ground.
The chamber shook. A shockwave tore through the floor.
But Stark was faster.
Fwish!
He leapt over the quake, landing smoothly before counterattacking with another spell.
Boom!
-4,280! -1,500!
’Vine Swing’s cooldown is twice as long as the others,’ Stark thought, eyes sharp. ’I’ll evolve it next chance I get.’
Even so, his rhythm didn’t falter.
The guardian pressed forward, swinging fists heavy enough to pulverize stone walls.
But Stark never got hit.
Slow. Predictable. That was the monster’s weakness.
Its strength was absurd HP and raw power. Its weakness was speed.
Even the strongest of teams would’ve struggled to chip it down.
Yet here Stark was, dodging every swing, weaving through every slam, and chipping its health away solo.
Fwish! Boom! Crack!
Minutes passed like this, the duel escalating.
Whenever the guardian managed to close in—
Magic Barrier!
BAM!
The giant fist collided with Stark’s shimmering shield, shattering it instantly but buying him just enough space to retreat and retaliate.
And eventually...
[HP: 9,890/50,000]
The boss was down to its final health.
But that’s when it changed.
ROOOOARRRR!
From the hollow mouth in its head, a shockwave of sound and darkness erupted.
The air rippled.
And suddenly, ten robed believers materialized around Stark, emerging from the shadows of the chamber.
The exact same enemies he had fought earlier, except now, they were here in numbers, and alongside the boss.
A deadly combination.
’If I focus on them, I’ll get pinned by the guardian... no, I need to finish the boss first.’
His mind was set.
He launched another barrage of spells, carving chunks off the guardian’s remaining health.
But just as his cooldowns stacked up, the believers swarmed, cutting off every escape route.
For a mage, this was death. But Stark wasn’t just any mage.
He had the perfect trump card.
His hand instinctively brushed against the bell hanging from his neck.
The [Revenant Bell]. He hadn’t used its active ability yet.
But he had been saving it precisely for this kind of moment.
---
[Soul Shockwave (Active Skill): Shake the revenant bell to cause a 3-second stun effect to all enemies within a 100-meter radius. 10-minute cooldown.]
---
It wasn’t much, but it didn’t need to be.
The instant the believers lunged—
Soul Shockwave!
A pulse of deep blue energy burst outward from the bell, washing over the entire chamber.
The believers froze mid-step.
The guardian staggered, its flame eye dimming briefly.
’Bingo.’
Stark raised his staff, locking onto the boss.
Toxic Crystal!
Fwish! Bam!
-1,500!
[HP: 0/50,000]
The guardian froze.Thᴇ link to the origɪn of this information rᴇsts ɪn NovᴇlFɪre.nᴇt
Cracks spiderwebbed across its massive stone body before it collapsed entirely, crashing into rubble.
Only the stunned believers remained.
Stark smirked, raising his staff toward them.
"Here we go..." he muttered. "Survive this, then."

chapters.title: Chapter 18: All Offensive Skills to Elite-Rank, The Weird Woman
chapters.content:
Chapter 18: Chapter 18: All Offensive Skills to Elite-Rank, The Weird Woman
Ding!
[You have killed "Abandoned Fate Guardian (Level 10 Elite-Rank Boss)"]
[You have gained 10,000 experience points.]
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 10!]
[You have gained 5 points in all of your attributes, and 5 free points to distribute.]
[You have gained 8 Evolution Points!]
[You have gained 58 Lives!]
---
Stark exhaled sharply, lowering his staff.
Stark managed to easily overpower the [Corrupted Fate Believers].
The [Revenant Bell] helped a lot, as even those small seconds of stun allowed him to throw spells that damaged the majority of them.
It also allowed him to re-position himself and not be surrounded.
Eventually, after two minutes only, all of the believers were dead, killed by him.
Still, if he had to credit one skill above all... it was [Magic Barrier].
The translucent shield shimmered as it absorbed blow after blow, allowing him to fight with far more freedom than expected.
’I might’ve underestimated this skill,’ Stark admitted to himself, ’Based on how much it endured, I’d say it can block at least a thousand damage before breaking.’
The thought made him grin faintly.
Ding!
A new panel flickered into view in front of him.
[You have reached Level 10.]
Stark glanced at it for a moment but dismissed it just as quickly.
He still had to finish clearing the zone and claim its final rewards.
After all, reaching level 10 was the next big milestone.
And so a lot of panels appeared around him to inform him of the next steps, even though Stark knew about them all.
He extended his hand, activating [Hand of Avarice].
The massive hand of darkness grabbed the corpses.
Ding!
---
[You have gained 6 Evolution Points!]
[You have gained 76 Lives.]
---
"Not bad," Stark muttered, grinning.
In total, he had gained over a hundred lives just from this fight alone.
But more importantly, he’d earned a massive 14 Evolution Points in one go.
[Current Evolution Points: 17.]
The number glowed brightly on his panel, and Stark felt his pulse quicken.
With that much, he could evolve multiple skills.
But first came the basics.
"Ten points into Spirit, ten into Agility," Stark decided aloud, distributing the twenty attribute points he’d saved up from leveling up.
Ding!
---
[Constitution: 55]
[Strength: 55]
[Agility: 77 (+17)]1
[Spirit: 78 (+44)]
---
"Perfect," Stark muttered with a satisfied grin.
His Spirit and Agility had skyrocketed, leaving his Strength and Constitution lagging a little behind.
That was fine.
His build wasn’t about brute force or tanking damage, it was about speed, control, and overwhelming magical power.
A faint grinding sound broke his focus.
Fwish! Click!
The massive stone door at the end of the chamber rumbled as the glowing fate-symbol on its surface cracked and shattered.
Slowly, the seal faded away, leaving the door free to open.
Stark’s eyes lit up.
That was the way forward, the zone’s final reward awaited him inside.
But before moving on, there was still one last matter to take care of.
The guardian had dropped something.
He crouched down.
But what he found instead made him groan in frustration.
---
[Guardian Armor (Elite): Warrior-type Armor, +50 Constitution, +28 Strength, +15 Physical Resistance, +8 Magical Resistance. Requirement: Level 10]
---
"Of course..." Stark muttered, shaking his head, "An incredible piece of gear... and I can’t even wear it."
The armor’s stats were monstrous, far beyond anything most players could even dream of at this stage.
For a warrior-type Awakener, it would be priceless.
For him, though? Completely useless.
Still, useless didn’t mean worthless.
He stored it in his inventory, one day, he could maybe sell it for a good amount.
With that settled, only the Evolution Points remained.
Stark’s gaze drifted to his skill panel.
[Skills: Scorching Fireball (Elite), Magic Barrier (Rare), Hand of Avarice (Epic), Toxic Crystal (Rare), Vine Smash (Rare)]
’It takes ten EP to push a skill from Epic to Legendary,’ Stark recalled, ’But I’ll prioritize the attack skills for now.’
His eyes lingered on [Vine Smash].
A good skill, versatile and strong, but limited by its long cooldown.
Alongside [Toxic Crystal], it was still stuck at rare rank.
That made the decision easy.
[Do you wish to consume 5 + 7 Evolution Points to evolve "Vine Smash" twice?]
"Yes."
Ding!
[You have evolved "Vine Smash" (Rare) to "Vine Surge" (Elite) to "Vine Cataclysm" (Epic).]
[5 Evolution Points remaining.]
"Now we’re talking."
---
[Vine Cataclysm (Epic): Summons several vines from the ground that will strike with immense force at multiple targets. Deals 200 → 300 → 500 base damage + 150% → 200% → 300% Spirit. Cooldown: 35 → 30 → 25 (12.5) seconds.]
---
Stark’s eyes widened as he read through the description.
"Holy shit... this thing will deal over eight thousand damage at least!"
The sheer destructive potential made his blood race.
And he still had points left.
He turned next to [Toxic Crystal].
[Do you wish to consume 5 Evolution Points to evolve "Toxic Crystal"?]
"Yes."
Ding!
[You have evolved "Toxic Crystal" (Rare) to "Corrosive Crystal" (Elite).]
---
[Corrosive Crystal (Elite): Summons a corrosive crystal that deals exactly 150 → 300 damage. Applies the "Poison" status effect. Cooldown: 10 → 9 (4.5) seconds.]
[Poison: Deals 20% → 25% of received damage for 5 seconds.]
---
"Perfect."
Now all three of his offensive skills were at least Elite-rank.
Only [Magic Barrier] remained behind at Rare, but for the moment that was fine.
A defensive skill could wait, his offensive power had just skyrocketed.
Closing his panel, Stark turned his attention back to the massive stone door.
Beyond that door lay the true reward of the zone.
Now that he was level 10, he would be able to go through his [Class Advancement].
And also head to the [Eternal Continent], where the game would actually begin.
He placed his hand on the stone and pushed.
The heavy door rumbled, grinding open inch by inch.
Stark immediately stepped back, prepared in case some hidden monster was waiting to ambush him.
But no monster appeared.
Instead, the chamber beyond was vast and silent, bathed in a soft starlit glow.
At its center stood a raised altar, faintly radiating golden light.
And beside it... a figure.
"Huh?" Stark’s eyes narrowed, "What the..."
A woman stood beside the altar, dressed in a flowing white robe.
A translucent hood draped over her head, obscuring her features.
Even so, her presence was impossible to ignore.
---
[??? (???)]
[Rank: ???]
[HP: ???]
[Skills: ???]
---
Stark’s expression hardened.
He couldn’t read her stats, but the fact that she had a "Skills" section meant she was an NPC.
As her head lifted, her aura exploded outward.
It pressed down on Stark like a crushing wave, forcing him to take an instinctive step back.
’Too strong,’ he thought immediately, ’If she attacks, I won’t stand a chance.’
Through the veil of her hood, he caught a glimpse of her eyes.
Dark, with eerie purple pupils, the same as the [Corrupted Fate Believers].
His heart tightened.
She raised her hand, aura gathering like a storm around it.
For a moment, Stark tensed, ready to throw everything he had at her...
But then, just as suddenly, her body dissolved into glowing particles.
Within seconds, she had completely disappeared.
"She’s gone..." Stark muttered, frowning, "Weird. What the hell was that about?"
The silence stretched, but there was no further sign of her.
Shaking his head, Stark turned his gaze back to the altar.
And then his breath caught.
Right in front of it stood a glowing chest, its surface golden, its presence radiating unmistakable power.
[Legendary Chest]
Stark’s eyes widened in pure excitement.Follow current novels on
He hadn’t expected the zone’s reward to be this valuable.

chapters.title: Chapter 19: Legendary Chest, Curse Flower Skill
chapters.content:
Chapter 19: Chapter 19: Legendary Chest, Curse Flower Skill
[Legendary Chest]
The chest shimmered before Stark, glowing with a golden radiance that screamed of its rank.
His reward for clearing the dungeon and defeating the boss now sat right in front of him.
He didn’t hesitate.
Pouring mana into the chest, he heard a soft—
Click!
That was the sound.
The chest had recognized him and was ready to be unlocked.
Most chests only contained a single item, but that wasn’t what mattered.
The quality of the loot always depended on the rank of the chest itself.
Which meant, no matter what came out, it would be legendary.
Stark reached forward and threw the lid open.
Ding!
[You have opened the "Legendary Chest" and obtained the "Curse Flower" skill book.]
The system announcement rang in his ears.
Stark immediately shoved his hand inside the chest and pulled out his reward.
[Skill Book: Curse Flower (Legendary). Requirement: Level 10]
A grin spread across his face.
His very first legendary skill, and it was a universal skill since every class could learn it!
Without a second thought, Stark chose to learn it.
Ding!
[You have learned the skill "Curse Flower"]
---
[Curse Flower (Legendary): Use on a player or NPC’s corpse within five seconds of death to curse them with the "Curse Flower".]
[The flower will grow on their bodies and absorb their lives for 30 seconds at a rate of 1 life per second.]1
[The flower has 100 HP, and if it is destroyed, the user gets nothing as it will not bloom.]
---
"What the fuck..."
Stark blinked at the description, then read it again. And again.
Each time, the shock didn’t lessen.
So far, he hadn’t seen a single NPC in this life besides the strange woman he encountered inside this very dungeon.
The [Novice Continent] didn’t contain NPCs at all.
They only began appearing once you set foot in the [Eternal Continent].
Which meant...
Right now, this skill was basically only usable against players.
And if the description was right, he could squeeze thirty more lives from someone after they died.
"Wait... if they don’t even have thirty lives left..." he muttered under his breath. "Would that mean... I could permanently kill them?"
The thought was insane.
’I wonder...’
As for the flower’s 100 HP? Stark wasn’t worried.
After all, how could the flower be destroyed if he made sure there was nobody left to do that?
The more he thought about it, the more terrifying this skill seemed.
This was his first legendary skill in his new life too, and he could definitely see why.
And the best part? Like everything else he obtained, this skill wasn’t stuck in place.
It could evolve. Curious, Stark checked the panel.
[Do you wish to consume 50 Evolution Point to evolve "Curse Flower"?]
His jaw dropped.
"God damn... that’s... way too much."
The jump was absurd.
From [Epic] to [Legendary], it only cost 10 EP.
But now, a single step further demanded 50 EP?
That was five times the cost!
He couldn’t even imagine what came after that.
100? 200? More?
Shaking his head, Stark closed the panel.
He would worry about that later.
Right now, something else appeared in front of him.
A glowing portal shimmered into existence nearby. His exit.
Once he stepped through, he’d be sent back to the start of the zone.
But before leaving, Stark wanted to deal with something else.
He wanted to check the panels that appeared around him when he reached level 10.
Ding!
[Congratulations to player "Oblivion" for being the first player to reach level 10 in Novice Town #783!]
[You have gained 5 Prestige Points!]
The announcement boomed across the minds of everyone in his novice town.
And then, before he even had time to smile—
Ding!
[Congratulations to player "Oblivion" for being the first player to reach level 10 in the world!]
[You have gained 10 Prestige Points!]Nᴇw novel chapters are publɪshed on
This one rang across the world.
"Nice," Stark grinned.
Fifteen prestige points. Just like that.
He knew that some players were already at levels 8 and 9.
People with ridiculous talents and overpowered classes.
But still, he had beaten them all.
Right now, nobody stood above him.
Of course, the rest of the world had their own thoughts.
"God fucking Oblivion again! Can’t that guy take a break?"
"Bro, just admit you’re jealous."
Speculation about his identity ran rampant, but it didn’t matter.
Nobody would figure out who he was.
’Soon enough, it won’t even matter,’ Stark thought. ’Once everyone moves to the [Eternal Continent], the real game begins. That’s when everything will connect.’
The world announcements weren’t the only panels that appeared.
Ding!
[Since you have reached level 10, you are able to leave the "Novice Content" and head to the "Eternal Continent" to finally start your journey!]
And right beside it—
[Congratulations, you may now undergo your first class advancement.]
Class advancements were usually a nightmare.
Tasks designed to push players to their limits.
But they were necessary, because each advancement strengthened your class beyond recognition.
But the very first one...
[To advance your class, you simply need to head to the "Eternal Continent"!]
[Your experience will be locked until then.]
"Of course," Stark muttered, grinning.
They made the first one easy to "help" players, but Stark knew the truth.
It was nothing but a leash.
A way to force every single person toward the [Eternal Continent].
Because in itself, agreeing to go there would be the real nightmare.
Once you left, there was no going back.
The real challenge would begin there.
And besides, nobody could surpass level 10 while staying here.
Ding!
[Do you wish to go to the "Eternal Continent"?]
[Yes] [No]
Stark immediately pressed [No].
’I still have things to do here. Besides, I can leave whenever I want.’
Another reminder flashed:
[You will only be able to extract your abilities to the real world by reaching the "Eternal Continent"!]
"I know that already," Stark groaned.
The system was pushing people toward that continent as much as it could.
Even he had no choice but to accept it eventually. But not yet.
Turning away, Stark stepped into the glowing exit portal and reappeared at the start of the [Abandoned Temple of Fate].
He left the cave behind and stepped back into the forest.
Without wasting a second, he sprinted toward town.
Sure, he could’ve killed himself to teleport instantly, he’d only lose a single life since he could unequip the [Revenant Bell]—
But why ruin his no-death streak now?
At full speed, it still took him twenty minutes to reach [Novice Town #783].
As soon as he crossed into the safe zone, Stark slowed, his eyes widening.
"What the hell..."
The streets were packed.
He had never, not once, seen a novice town this crowded.
Weaving through the mass of players, he made his way toward the central square.
And when he arrived, it all made sense.
Every gaze turned toward him.
"Wait, holy shit, it’s Oblivion!"
"He must be a strong warrior like me, right?"
"Nah, trust me, he’s an assassin. Nobody else levels that fast."
Then their eyes actually fell on him.
"Oh... he’s a mage."
"-_-," Stark could only sigh.
If you’re a fear and hunger fan, you might get the reference of this skill

chapters.title: Chapter 20: Meeting Max and Seren, Its Time for Payback
chapters.content:
Chapter 20: Chapter 20: Meeting Max and Seren, Its Time for Payback
"Could mage be the best class?" one of the players around Stark asked, his tone filled with doubt.
"Hell no," another scoffed. "I’ve got a mage in my party. Sure, he can deal good damage, but the cooldowns are ridiculous!"
"Then maybe he’s got a [Hidden Class]?"
"Definitely. No other way!"
The chatter around Stark kept going, players debating loudly as if their guesses mattered.
But Stark ignored every word.
He wasn’t here to listen to speculation.
There were people he needed to find from his past life.
In that life, humanity had been brought to its knees.
The majority died within the first month, leaving only the strongest to claw their way forward.
And in the middle of it all, Stark had made mistakes, mistakes that led to the pointless deaths of friends he should have protected.
That guilt had followed him into this new beginning.
This time, he swore he wouldn’t let it happen again.
Still, there was a reason he wasn’t rushing out to search for them immediately.
Two reasons, actually.
First, he needed to become stronger on his own.
Without power, he’d only repeat the same failures.
Second, he knew they would all end up at the [Eternal Continent].
Every player would eventually be pulled there, it was the center of everything.
So even if he didn’t search now, he’d meet them sooner or later.
The only exceptions were two people. Max and Seren.
If possible, he wanted to find them before stepping foot on the [Eternal Continent].
Or at the very least, he wanted to test the limits of his new [Curse Flower] skill against them.
’But finding them in all this chaos... it’s almost impossible,’ Stark thought grimly, ’Tens of thousands of novice towns scattered everywhere...’
The task felt hopeless
Until—
"Make way!"
The loud voice cut through the crowd, familiar enough to freeze Stark in his tracks.
He turned his head. And there they were, Max and Seren.
His lips curled into the faintest, coldest smile.
Of course, Stark had already activated his [Hide Face] feature before coming here.
No one could recognize him, not even people who might see him outside of the game.
He wouldn’t risk his identity, not even for a second.
---
[ID: GodOfViolence]
[Class: ???]
[Talent: ??? (??-Rank)]
[Skills: ???]
---
[ID: DivineGoddess]
[Class: ???]
[Talent: ??? (??-Rank)]
[Skills: ???]
---
Max and Seren had activated [Hide Face] as well.
But unfortunately for them, they had made one critical mistake: they used the same IDs as in Stark’s past life.
That was all Stark needed to recognize them.
His expression darkened.
His heart beat steadily, but his blood ran cold.
"Hello, Oblivion," Max greeted with a confident grin. "I’m a warrior, and my companion here’s a priest." He motioned to Seren, who gave a cheerful wave.
"We wanted to know if you’d join us," Seren said brightly. "With your strength and ours combined, nothing could stand in our way. Together, the three of us could conquer everything!"
Stark’s gaze stayed locked on them, his expression utterly neutral.
In this life, there would be no fake smiles.
They weren’t his friends. Not anymore.
He couldn’t forgive them for what they had done in the past. And he never would.
The only reason he hadn’t already cut them down was simple: killing them here and now was pointless.
Inside the safe zone, they were untouchable.
Even outside, they had plenty of lives to burn.
But with the [Curse Flower]... things could change.
’Maybe this will be my ticket to finally killing all my enemies.’
Max, oblivious to the storm behind Stark’s eyes, extended his hand.
"My talent lets me stack blood to increase my damage," he said proudly, as if bragging would win trust. "I can already deal hundreds of damage with every strike. Seren and I even killed a level 8 rare-rank boss monster on our own."
"And I can heal over a thousand HP already," Seren added, smiling sweetly. "Which means if we stick together, we basically can’t die."
They weren’t lying.
Stark knew better than anyone how strong the two of them were.
But strength wasn’t the issue.
"No," Stark said flatly. "I fight alone."
And with that, he turned his back and walked away.
The two stood frozen, shocked by the rejection.
Them? Rejected?
Hundreds of players were begging to join their party, throwing offers of gold and equipment at their feet.
And yet Oblivion? the level 10 mage at the top of the world, turned them down without a second thought?
Max’s grin twisted into a sneer.
"Hah. What an idiot. He’ll regret that soon enough."
Seren crossed her arms, her smile turning sharp.
"We’ll surpass him. Then he’ll realize he made a mistake."
They didn’t linger.
With only one free teleport per day, and the next costing ten lives, they weren’t about to waste it.
Instead, they decided to head deeper into the [Shadow Forest], grinding until they hit level 10.
Meanwhile, Stark ignored the crowd and lifted his eyes upward.
---
[Level Leaderboard:]
[1. Oblivion: Level 10]
[2. PrinceLucas: Level 8]
[3. FateBreaker: Level 8]
[4. GodOfViolence: Level 8]
[5. DivineGoddess: Level 8]
[6. Starfall: Level 7]
[7. BraveCop: Level 7]
...
---
The leaderboard stretched on, filled with names both familiar and unknown.
Stark studied it calmly.
The board included every player connected to this novice town, even those who had teleported here from somewhere else.
On average, most players hovered around level 5.
But the climb was picking up pace, hidden talents, rare classes, and lucky encounters pushed many forward quickly.
For now, Stark held the number one spot.
He knew the rest of the world was catching up.
Within a few hours, plenty of players would break through to level 10 and cross into the [Eternal Continent].
That didn’t worry him.
Instead, he stood silently in the central square, waiting.
And when Max and Seren finally left the safety of the town, Stark moved.
He didn’t care if it would take a small amount of lives.
Revenge wasn’t about efficiency, it was about sending a message.
A grin tugged at the corner of his mouth.
’This is just the beginning,’ Stark thought, ’A small taste of what’s coming for you.’
They had called themselves his "friends" once.
But he could see clearly now, that had been nothing but a lie.
With his staff in hand and his [Bear Mage Robe] draped over him, Stark followed.
A sudden message popped up.
[Starfall: Hellooo (◕ᗜ◕), I just wanted to thank you for the staff and necklace, it’s really helping! The team also wanted to say thanks for the items!]
Stark’s heart softened.
A faint smile touched his lips. Starfall.
In his past life, she had died during the [First Cataclysm].
Her lives had run out, and she’d vanished forever.
Seeing her alive now, carefree enough to send messages like this, only strengthened Stark’s determination.
’Everything that’s coming... the Eternal Continent, the real world... I’ll handle it. I won’t let history repeat itself.’
He pressed forward.
Max and Seren were just ahead, leaving the safety of the town behind as they headed toward the [Shadow Forest].
Stark shadowed them, quiet and patient.
The forest loomed ahead, its twisted branches stretching upward like claws, its shadows deep and heavy.
And the moment they were about to step inside the forest, Stark raised his staff.
He didn’t hesitate.
Vine Cataclysm!

chapters.title: Chapter 21: Using Curse Flower, Absorbing Lives
chapters.content:
Chapter 21: Chapter 21: Using Curse Flower, Absorbing Lives
Vine Cataclysm!
The moment Stark activated the spell, the ground trembled.
Several thick vines shot upward like serpents breaking free from the earth.
They lashed out instantly, striking toward Max and Seren with brutal force.
BOOM!
-8,660! -8,660!
The numbers exploded above their heads.
Even with Max’s absurd defense and raw power, and Seren’s continuous healing spells wrapping around him, there was no way they could withstand that much damage in an instant.
Their bodies staggered. Their vision blurred.
And then, darkness.
Ding!
[You have been killed by Oblivion.]
In [Eternal Soul], death wasn’t just a vague blur of defeat.
If the killer didn’t hide their identity with a special ability, their name was displayed for all to see.
It was one of the reasons wars in this world escalated so quickly.
The moment a player saw who killed them, grudges were born, and blood would follow.
Just like that, Max and Seren’s avatars flickered, their bodies on the verge of disintegration.
But before they fully vanished, Stark moved.
He tried to cast [Curse Flower] from where he stood, but a cold message appeared before his eyes.
[You are too far from the target.]
"Tch."
Without hesitation, Stark burst forward.
His boots hammered against the dirt, closing the gap between him and the collapsing corpses.
Five seconds.
That was all the time a body lingered before disappearing in [Eternal Soul].
And it was the exact same five-second window that [Curse Flower] required.
Finally, Stark skidded to a stop right beside them, thrusting his palm out.
Curse Flower!
Ding!
[The "Curse Flower" has been planted on the corpses of the players you killed.]
’Got it.’
Relief flickered across Stark’s face.
A thin vine sprouted from Max’s chest, followed by another from Seren’s.
Each carried a small bud at the end, tightly closed, like a crimson flower yet to bloom.
[Curse Flower: 100 HP]
The mechanic was simple.
If anyone struck those buds, even with the weakest attack, they would instantly shatter.
But here, no one would come to save them.
Stark crouched low, watching as faint energy bled out of the corpses.
The buds pulsed faintly, glowing as they began to absorb.
It was slow, steady, and unsettling.
’Beautiful,’ Stark thought, his eyes narrowing as the buds slowly grew, ’And terrifying. A flower that steals lives.’
At a rate of one life per second, the flowers drank greedily.
Ten seconds. Fifteen. Twenty.
At the thirty-second mark, both buds unfurled at the same time, their petals opening wide.
They revealed beautiful crimson flowers that shimmered like crystals.The source of this content ɪs No(ᴠ)ᴇlFire.nᴇt
Ding!
[Your "Curse Flower" has taken 30 Lives from GodOfViolence]
[Your "Curse Flower" has taken 30 Lives from DivineGoddess]
Stark let out a low whistle.
Sixty-two lives. From just two kills.
It was absolutely game-breaking, and it was only the start!
But his smile faded almost as quickly as it appeared.
He couldn’t use this ability recklessly against just anyone.
Only against tthose he knew would be a problem later on.
It wasn’t something to be wasted on random fodder.
Plus, no one should know the existence of this.
If they knew, it would spread, and people do anything they could to hit the flower.
With the test complete, Stark straightened.
He had no reason to linger in the [Novice Continent] any longer.
Max and Seren now knew his name. His identity.
The seed of fear had been planted.
And more importantly, he had confirmed the power of his new skill.
Across the leaderboards, the second-place player in his town was already level 8.
In the world, several players should be already at level 9 and pushing.
Stark knew that in under a few hours, many would enter the [Eternal Continent].
And once you crossed over... there was no going back.
He opened his interface.
---
[Oblivion: I’m going ahead, make sure to level up and immediately proceed afterward.]
[Starfall: Okay
---
Grace’s odd way of typing always caught him off guard.
