Excitement, nerves, ambition, everyone was still riding the wave of discovery.
Stark ignored most of it.
He had his own goals.
He moved to the center of the square and tilted his head up at the giant projection above, the leaderboard.
---
[Level Leaderboard:]
[1. Oblivion: Level 13][2. Ghost: Level 12][3. PrinceLucas: Level 12][4. EvilDemon: Level 12][5. GodOfViolence: Level 11][6. DivineGoddess: Level 11][7. BraveCop: Level 11]
...
---
Still at the top.
’Others should all have a few hundred lives saved up by now,’ Stark thought.
He himself had more thanks to [Hand of Avarice], but assuming everyone else was far behind would be a mistake.
Especially when there were talents out there that multiplied life gains outright.
He didn’t know who had them, but he was sure someone did.
Still, it didn’t bother him too much.
He had his own advantage, and that was enough.
Stark moved to the edge of the square, sat cross-legged on the ground, and dumped his inventory in front of him.
A pile of gear spilled out, mostly weapons and armor.
He kept the [Undead Soul Mage Robe] and [Soul Staff], but everything else was fair game.
He opened the [Stall] function and typed out a single blunt message.
[I can’t hold these items anymore, they’re cheap, come and buy them.]
He set the prices low enough that people would bite, but still enough to profit.
And, as expected, players swarmed.
Some hesitated at first, but once the first sales went through, the rest followed like sharks that smelled blood.
His gear sold piece by piece, most going for twenty lives.
The square around him buzzed louder, more players drawn over by the word "cheap."
It was going smoothly.
Until—
Fwish! Fwoom!
An assassin burst forward, shadow blurring as their [Speed Boost] ignited.
Their hand darted to the ground, snatching up the [Guardian Armor (Elite)] from Stark’s display.
Stark’s smile twitched.
’Of course.’
Since there were no rules and protection, anyone greedy or reckless enough could just try to steal.
The assassin bolted, feet barely touching the ground.
For a moment, it looked like he might actually get away.
But Stark’s hand was already raised.
"You’re not getting away," he whispered.
The staff in his grip pulsed, and he cast one of his newer skills.
Lightning Strike!
Fwish! ZAP!
A crack of light snapped through the air, hitting the assassin square in the back.
-10,275!
The thief froze mid-step, body convulsing, then dropped to the ground in a smoking heap.
The crowd went silent.
Dozens of wide eyes turned toward Stark.
"Ten... ten thousand damage?!"
"Impossible, how the hell—"
"I told you, mages are busted!"
"Shut up, idiot. Oblivion’s busted, not mages."
Their whispers didn’t matter.
Stark bent down, picked the armor off the ground, and set it back on display like nothing happened.
He didn’t bother using [Curse Flower].
He wanted to, but he didn’t want to reveal something like that yet.
The majority might be confused, but if even one figures it out, it wouldn’t be good.
He would rather keep it a secret than acquire the 30 lives from it.
By the time most of his items were gone, the crowd had thinned again.
Only one man lingered close, tall and imposing.
He wore a crimson priest robe, aura flickering faintly around him like firelight.
His ID floated clearly overhead.
[ID: EvilDemon]
"Oh?" Stark muttered under his breath.
The man pointed casually at the [Undead Shaman Scepter (Elite)].
"How much?" he asked, expression neutral, "It’s much better than my current scepter."
"Fifty lives," Stark answered, "It’s a powerful scepter from a boss in a zone."
EvilDemon inspected it with calm eyes.
Then he smiled and accepted.
The trade window flashed, and just like that, fifty lives transferred.
The scepter changed hands.
Stark watched him closely.
The name was familiar, but faint.
He didn’t remember [EvilDemon] standing out in his past life... maybe he’d simply forgotten.
Still, something about this man felt sharp.
"So you solo too, huh," EvilDemon said as he tested the scepter’s weight.
Stark nodded.
"Same," the man added, grin widening.
Stark’s gaze narrowed.
"But you’re a—"
"Priest?" EvilDemon laughed, "Yeah. Surprising? I could say the same about you. A mage, but you fight alone."
It was true.
Priests weren’t just heal-bots in [Eternal Soul]. Not here.
Later on, they gained frightening offensive power.
But seeing one strong enough to level solo this early was rare.
It meant one thing: this man’s class and talent were far from normal.
Their eyes met for a second longer, then EvilDemon smirked, turned, and walked deeper into the city without another word.
Stark watched him go. His instincts prickled.
He didn’t know why, but he felt this guy would matter.
He brushed the thought aside and focused on his stall.
Soon after, the last of his items were gone.
Ding!
[Lives: 434 → 889]
A tidy profit.ɴᴇᴡ ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀʀᴇ ᴘᴜʙʟɪsʜᴇᴅ ᴏɴ N(o)vᴇl(F)ire.nᴇt
Four hundred and fifty lives earned in a single sitting.
Enough to bring him closer to extracting his levels into reality.
He stretched, packed away the leftovers, and checked his inventory.
[Inventory: 2/27]
Almost empty. Plenty of room for new loot.
He stood, spinning his staff once in his hand, eyes scanning the ruined skyline.
Level 15 was the immediate goal.
He had the [Undead Soul Mage]’s gear waiting, but he couldn’t equip it yet.
Every level gained now would make the difference later.
And beyond that... the [Events].
The stronger he was when they began, the greater the rewards he could claim.
His lips curled into a grin.
"Then let’s keep moving."
He stepped out of the square, picked a new direction, and fired off a [Sovereign Vines] at the first monster he spotted.
Instant kill. Stark lowered his staff and kept walking.
The grind wasn’t over. It had only just begun.

chapters.title: Chapter 32: Grinding to Level 15, Corrosive Crystals
chapters.content:
Chapter 32: Chapter 32: Grinding to Level 15, Corrosive Crystals
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 14!]
[You have gained 5 points in all of your attributes, and 5 free points to distribute.]
---
It took around thirty minutes, but eventually Stark had killed enough monsters to push through and level up.
Along the way, he only gained 1 EP and collected 172 Lives.
Not much, but still progress.
At this point, Stark was sure more and more players were starting to realize what [Experience Decay] really was.
Some were already stuck at level 13, just like him earlier.
They’d been killing monsters nonstop, but the gains slowed down to almost nothing.
The level 11–13 monsters didn’t give enough experience anymore, which meant players had no choice but to head deeper inside the city if they wanted to keep growing.
That was the reason why the [Ruined City] was built with multiple zones in the first place. A natural filter.
’Only one more level,’ Stark grinned.
Soon, level 15.
As he walked deeper into the ruins, something caught his attention.
The name [Starfall] in his friend list lit up.
That meant she was back online.
’Some people still prioritize the real world over [Eternal Soul],’ Stark thought. ’But those who keep doing that will die when the [First Calamity] arrives.’
His thoughts flickered to Grace.
He didn’t know whether her death in his past life was because she didn’t take the game seriously... or if she had taken it seriously, but just wasn’t strong enough to survive.
After the [First Calamity], most of the world would be destroyed anyway.
From that point on, everyone would have no choice but to fully focus on [Eternal Soul].
That was also when players would start discovering the NPC towns, populated by other races besides humans.
But reaching them would take a while, so Stark pushed that thought aside.
’I should clear a zone first to push for the next level.’
Just as he thought about that—
Ding!
[Player "Starfall" has sent you a private message!]
[Starfall: I’m finally back! (ノ^∇^)]
[Starfall: You know, I didn’t want to focus on this game too much since it was too scary... but seeing you try so hard made me wanna keep going too (ㆆ ᴗ ㆆ)]
Stark grinned when he read that.
’I guess I got my answer.’
So that’s why she died before.
Grace hadn’t taken [Eternal Soul] seriously like most people.
But if she was willing to keep going now, that was a good sign.
[Starfall: I’ll try to form a team with some people, and see from there!]
[Oblivion: Good. I’ll see if I have anything to give you... for a discount.]
[Starfall: Discount?! Not even free (T⌓T)? Well, I don’t blame you, I’ll pay!]
Stark’s grin widened.
He didn’t mind helping people by giving away items he didn’t need. He had no issue with that.
But giving things away for free? That wasn’t his style.
He kept marching forward, casting spells and blasting apart the nearby monsters.
Level 11 enemies only gave around 30 exp now.
Even the level 13 ones barely gave anything worthwhile.
’I want to push deeper,’ Stark thought. ’But first, I have something else to deal with.’
At level 15, not only would he be able to equip all his gear, but he could also activate the statue near the [Ruined City]’s spawn square.
That statue wasn’t just for show, it was actually a sealed epic-rank level 17 boss.
In his past life, this statue had caused a massacre.
The moment it was summoned, the entire square transformed into a danger zone.Googlᴇ search N(o)vᴇl(F)ire.nᴇt
Anyone who stepped inside instantly faced a [Life Loss Rate] of 100.
Back then, dozens of players were wiped out in minutes.
And once the boss killed enough victims, it evolved into a legendary-rank monster.
At that point, it took waves of powerful players working together to bring it down.
That event had been the very first "wake-up call" for the entire player base.
The moment they realized just how brutal [Eternal Soul] really was.
This time, Stark planned to face the boss alone.
He couldn’t stop other players from interfering, but as long as he did the most damage, he’d get the best rewards and the experience.
And killing that boss also unlocked [Ruined City Travel], letting players move between cities.
It wasn’t a massive advantage, mostly just useful for people looking to find teammates elsewhere, but it was still worth unlocking early.
On the way, Stark encountered another [Ruined Sentinel General].
This one was backed up by a squad of normal sentinels.
But—
Sovereign Vines! Annihilating Fireball!
-25,650! -25,650! -14,910!
The lesser sentinels were instantly shredded by his vines, while the general managed to tank the first hit, only to get melted by Stark’s follow-up fireball.
When the smoke cleared, the boss was dead.
This time, the general only gave him around 2,000 experience points.
A far cry from the 20,000 it had given before.
Still, Stark pocketed 5 EP from the fight, which made it worthwhile.
Another hour passed as he hunted.
During that time, he noticed some familiar names popping up on the level rankings.
[Ghost]. [EvilDemon]. Both had hit level 14 too.
In Stark’s previous life, he hadn’t crossed paths with many of these people early on.
For example, [Ghost] had become famous later as an insanely powerful solo player.
She even had a few global announcements under her belt.
But no one ever found out what her class or talent really was. She kept everything hidden.
[EvilDemon], on the other hand... Stark had strong doubts about him dying.
The guy was most likely a ruthless lone wolf too.
The reason Stark didn’t know them before was simple: in his last life, he had spawned in the [Fourteenth Ruined City].
Completely different player base.
’Maybe these guys will handle the statue boss,’ Stark thought. ’Or maybe they’ll die. Either way... it doesn’t matter.’
Being in the [First Ruined City] meant the competition was far stronger than anywhere else.
Only the best were surviving here.
And Stark had full confidence in his own ability to stay ahead.
Not long after—
"Found one," Stark muttered, eyes narrowing.
Ahead of him was an alleyway covered in a faint silver mist.
The moment he stepped closer—
Ding!
[You are about to enter a dangerous level 15–16 zone: "Alley of Shadows"]
[Once you enter, you cannot leave unless you die.]
Zones in [Eternal Soul] came in all shapes and sizes.
Some stretched so wide they could take weeks to clear.
Others could be finished in a day, or even an hour.
Whatever the case, Stark was confident he could handle this one.
Before stepping through, he pulled open his skill panel.
’I’ve got 18 Evolution Points. Might as well burn some to make this easier.’
[Skills: Annihilating Fireball (Epic), Magic Barrier (Elite), Hand of Avarice (Legendary), Corrosive Crystal (Elite), Sovereign Vines (Legendary), Curse Flower (Legendary), Lightning Strike (Epic)]
Almost all of his skills had already been pushed up to Legendary. The weaker ones needed attention.
Ding!
[Do you wish to consume 7 Evolution Points to evolve "Corrosive Crystal"?]
"Yes."
Ding!
[You have evolved "Corrosive Crystal" (Elite) to "Corrosive Crystals" (Epic).]
[Current Evolution Points: 11.]
"Oh?" Stark tilted his head. "The only thing that changed... is that it became plural?"
[Corrosive Crystal]’s biggest weakness was always being a single-target spell.
But now, with multiple crystals... it might finally be more useful!
---
[Corrosive Crystals (Epic): Summon up to five crystals that deal 300 → 700 damage each. Applies the "Poison" status effect. 9 → 8 (4)-seconds cooldown.]
[Poison: Deals 25% → 30% of damage received for 5 seconds.]
---
"Perfect," Stark muttered.
Without hesitation, he moved on to the next skill he wanted to evolve.

chapters.title: Chapter 33: Alley of Shadows, Alley Reaper
chapters.content:
Chapter 33: Chapter 33: Alley of Shadows, Alley Reaper
[Do you wish to consume 7 Evolution Points to evolve "Magic Barrier"?]
"Yes."
Ding!
[You have evolved "Magic Barrier" (Elite) to "Strong Magic Barrier" (Epic)]
[Current Evolution Points: 4.]
’Another name change, heh.’
It was only the second time his sole defensive skill had changed names, so Stark expected something good.
---
[Strong Magic Barrier (Epic): Summon a barrier around the user that can endure attacks, it has 5,000 → 10,000 HP. 35 → 30 (15)-seconds cooldown.]
---
The description now actually showed the HP of the barrier, which was useful.
He could see before, but only in the form of a small panel.
Now that he knew it would be easier to track.
Stark knew the general damage range of monsters at each stage.
A barrier with that much HP was basically a second lifeline.
It would let him stand his ground even against things he couldn’t dodge.
"Good enough."
He didn’t hesitate further.
With his preparations done, he stepped toward the new zone.
The silver mist swirled as he passed through, the atmosphere shifting immediately.
Ding!
---
[You have entered the "Alley of Shadows"]
[Lives loss rate: 100]
[Description: A very small alleyway shrouded in darkness, filled with a few monsters and a boss, be wary of your surroundings.]
---
Stark emerged on the other side of the mist. The system wasn’t exaggerating.
The alley was suffocatingly dark, as if shadows themselves dripped from the walls.
Yet for how narrow and small it seemed, the space inside stretched unnaturally long.
Almost like a warped corridor.
He scanned quickly.
Compared to other zones, this was small.
Nothing like the [Abandoned Temple of Fate] or [Undead Soul Land].
No doubt its purpose was simple: grind spot, quick EXP, low reward, short run.
For Stark, it was perfect. Level 15 was just ahead, and this zone was the shortcut.
He moved forward without hesitation.
But the moment his boots scraped against the cobbled ground—
Fwish!
A sharp claw tore out from the side.
Stark shifted his weight and slid back, narrowly dodging.
In the darkness, shapes formed.
---
[Shadow Spirit (Level 15)]
[Rank: Rare]
[HP: 40,000]
---
There were five of them.
Pitch-black bodies hovered just above the ground, like tattered shades drifting through air.
Their hollow white eyes locked onto him.
’I guess these are the monsters...’ Stark smirked. ’Good. Exactly what I need.’
No reason to waste time. His staff slammed forward.
Sovereign Vines! Corrosive Crystals!
The cobbles beneath the spirits cracked open as thick vines erupted upward, snapping around each target.
The ground quaked as the attack landed.
-25,650!-25,650!-25,650!
Numbers bled into the air. The spirits recoiled, hissing silently.
But Stark wasn’t done.
He swung his staff again, five green shards materializing around him.
The new version of the skill required steadier aim.
But to him, it wasn’t an issue.
He flicked his wrist, each shard slicing forward and embedding into a spirit.
-7,000! -2,100! -2,100!
The poison effect spread, numbers ticking faster and faster across their bodies.
The toxic build-up shredded through their HP, eating away their last fragments.
One after another, the five spirits collapsed into drifting black smoke.
Stark lowered his staff, stepping forward without a pause.
Ding!
---
[You have killed x5 "Shadow Spirit (Level 15)"]
[You have gained 15,000 experience points!]
[You have gained 47 Lives!]
---
Hand of Avarice!
Ding!
[You have gained 29 Lives!]
Stark’s life count ticked upward.
[Lives: 1260]
With that amount, he could actually extract his levels, and thus attributes, to the real world.
He needed much more to be able to send his skills and equipments.New ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄhapters are published on N(o)vᴇl(F)ire.nᴇt
He was already half-prepared for the [First Calamity] though!
Other than [Lives], the Shadow Spirits left nothing. No drops.
"Figures." He shrugged and kept moving.
The alley stretched on.
The walls pressed tighter the further he went, shadows flickering unnaturally against his steps.
A few more monsters appeared as he pushed deeper.
[Alley Wolf (Level 15)]
[Shadow Crook (Level 15)]
Each one tried ambushing him from the dark. Each one fell just as fast.
His EXP bar crawled higher, his [Lives] steadily stacking.
Minutes later, the faint end of the alley came into view.
A faint red glow lingered in the mist.
And waiting for him was the boss.
---
[Alley Reaper (Level 16)]
[Rank: Elite]
[HP: 90,000]
---
It floated slightly above the ground, a cloaked figure with only shadows beneath its hood.
A jagged scythe rested in its hands, gleaming in the dim alley.
Stark sized it up.
Compared to the [Undead Soul Mage], it was technically weaker, it only had one phase and less HP.
The reason for that was because of the rank.
But Stark didn’t care. EXP was EXP.
His staff shot up.
Sovereign Vines! Annihilating Fireball! Corrosive Crystals! Lightning Strike!
All his spells launched in unison.
-25,650!-14,910!-7,000! -2,100! -2,100!-10,650!
The reaper’s HP chunked down by two-thirds instantly.
Smoke burst from its cloak, yet it didn’t falter.
It lunged forward, scythe raised.
Strong Magic Barrier!
A shimmering dome wrapped around Stark.
But the reaper’s body flickered, and a faint chant echoed.
Soul Buff!
Its scythe blurred.
Fwish! SLASH! SLASH! SLASH!
Six strikes in less than a second.
Crack!
The barrier shattered like glass, fragments of mana bursting apart.
The seventh swing came straight for Stark’s throat.
He ducked low, boots scraping as the blade swept over his head.
The scythe carved into the wall, sparks flashing.
’One hit from that and I’m dead.’
But Stark didn’t freeze.
No matter how strong he was, this was still a level 16 elite-rank boss, something no other player could actually defeat.
Especially in this narrow alley, where its scythe had a big range.
But that didn’t matter.
He raised his staff, ready to cast, but...
Fwish! SLASH!
The reaper cut again, forcing him back.
’So that’s your game?’ Stark’s lips curled. ’Fine.’
Another swing. This time Stark braced his staff and met the attack head on.
Clang!
The impact rattled his arms, throwing him back a few meters.
-380!
He slid to a stop, chest heaving.
The was the first instance of damage he had taken since his transmigration.
Stark gritted his teeth and raised his staff again.
Annihilation Fireball! Corrosive Crystal!1
BOOM!
The fireball detonated against the reaper’s chest, flames flaring bright in the alley.
A green shard followed, embedding and poisoning the cloak.
-14,910! -7,000!
The reaper convulsed, shadows leaking.
Its form distorted, then shattered apart into mist.
The scythe clattered to the ground.
Ding!
---
[You have killed "Alley Reaper (Level 16 Elite-Rank Boss)"]
[You have gained 48,000 experience points.]
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 15!]
[You have gained 5 points in all of your attributes, and 5 free points to distribute.]
[You have gained 8 Evolution Points!]
[You have gained 38 Lives!]
---
"Perfect."
Stark raised his hand and immediately used [Hand of Avarice].
Ding!
[You have gained 4 Evolution Points!]
[You have gained 37 Lives!]
Satisfied, he crouched and picked up the fallen scythe.
The weapon was heavy, humming faintly with the remnants of shadow energy.
Stark’s eyes narrowed as he inspected it.
I wanna note that it says "corrosive crystal" instead of "crystals" because each crystal can only be aimed at one enemy.

chapters.title: Chapter 34: Reaching Level 15, Awakening the Man of Steel
chapters.content:
Chapter 34: Chapter 34: Reaching Level 15, Awakening the Man of Steel
The weapon floated in front of Stark’s eyes, glowing faintly with a crimson outline.
[Alley Reaper Scythe (Elite): Assassin-type weapon. +73 Strength, +35 Agility, +10% movement speed while equipped. Requirement: Level 15.]
It looked sharp enough to cut through steel.
Stark didn’t plan to use it, but a weapon of this caliber was worth keeping.
He stored it in his inventory with a flick of his hand, then turned to the real prize.
At the end of the narrow alley, a chest shimmered into existence.
Brown light radiated off it, marking it as [Elite]-rank.
Stark moved closer and poured his aura over the lock.
Click—
The chest creaked open.
Ding!
[You have opened the "Elite Chest" and obtained the "Alley Reaper Cloak."]
"Hm?" Stark raised his eyebrows.
---
[Alley Reaper Cloak (Elite): Assassin-type equipment. +28 Strength, +50 Agility, +83 Physical Resistance, +68 Magical Resistance. Requirement: Level 15]
[Short Invisibility (Active Skill): Use the power of your cloak to make yourself invisible for 10 seconds. 5-minutes cooldown.]
---
"An active skill..." Stark muttered.
That alone made this cloak special.
Gear with their own skills was extremely rare.
Even if he couldn’t use it himself, the value was high.
He could sell it later, trade it, or even maybe for other stuff.
For now, he stored it away.
Once that was done, a familiar sound greeted him.
Ding!
[You have reached level 15.]
[Head back to the square to activate "Ruined City Travel."]
The system prompt was clear.
In his first life, Stark hadn’t been the one to trigger it.
He only heard about the chaos that unfolded.
This time, though, he was ahead of the curve.
He would activate it himself, and then decide how to deal with the boss that came after.
Still... it was no joke. An epic-rank level 17 boss.
Stark wasn’t sure he could beat it alone. But that didn’t mean he would back down.
[Free Points to Allocate: 25.]
[Current Evolution Points: 16.]
He quickly opened his stat panel and began distributing points.
Twenty into Spirit. Five into Agility.
Then came the real move.
[Do you wish to consume 10 Evolution Points to evolve "Annihilating Fireball"?]
"Yes," Stark said firmly.
Ding!
[You have evolved "Annihilating Fireball" (Epic) to "Cataclysmic Fireball" (Legendary).]
[Current Evolution Points: 6.]
---
[Cataclysmic Fireball (Legendary): Conjure an annihilating fireball that deals 700% → 1000% of Spirit. 14 → 12 (6)-seconds cooldown.]
---
"Perfect."
His strongest spell had now reached legendary rank.
The power gap was enormous. But there was more.
Because he was now level 15, Stark could finally equip the higher-level gear he’d been carrying.
---
[Undead Soul Mage Robe (Epic): Mage-type equipment. +43 Spirit, +25 Constitution, +78 Physical Resistance, +102 Magical Resistance. Requirement: Level 15.]
---
[Soul Staff (Epic): Mage-type weapon. +100 Spirit, +43 Agility, Cooldowns reduced by 5%. Requirement: Level 15.]
---
The moment he put them on, a surge of energy coursed through him.
His body felt lighter, sharper, stronger.
He opened his status window to see the difference.
---
[Constitution: 80 (+25)]
[Strength: 80]
[Agility: 107 (+43)]
[Spirit: 123 (+149)]
---
"Good enough," Stark muttered.
The old [Bear Mage Robe] was useless now, so he discarded it without hesitation.
No other player would actually want this piece of equipment as they all had better.
The [Revenant Staff] on the other hand still had value, so he kept it in reserve.
With everything settled, Stark stepped through the nearby portal.
Blue light wrapped around him, and he emerged back outside of the [Alley of Shadows].
’Time to head back.’
He could grind a few more levels, sure.
But time was limited.
It would take hours to get to level 16.
Or worse, other players would eventually hit level 15, and when they did, they wouldn’t hesitate to trigger the event themselves.
If that happened, Stark would lose his chance to control the battlefield and also on the [Prestige Points] from that.
So he ran.
His upgraded agility let him glide through the ruined streets faster than ever.
After about twenty minutes, the familiar sight of the spawn square came into view.
This time, however, it was far more crowded than before.
’Not optimal,’ Stark thought, ’But it can’t be helped.’
He wasn’t about to slow down his progress for no reason.
He really wanted to defeat this boss for the experience, but also for the possible loot and EP gains.
The square was buzzing with activity.
Players rested in groups, bartered for items, or simply waited.
As he looked around though, he noticed that several of the top tier players were here.
"Hm."
None had reached level 15 yet, they were still here taking a break for some reason.
And as he turned his gaze...
"Oh." Stark narrowed his eyes.
Stark noticed Grace talk to someone, and that person was none other than... Ghost.
She wore assassin gear, white hair flowing down her back.ɴᴇᴡ ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀʀᴇ ᴘᴜʙʟɪsʜᴇᴅ ᴏɴ ɴo(v)elFɪre.ɴet
Her face was hidden under the [Hide Face] feature, but her presence alone was enough to stir whispers in the crowd.
PrinceLucas barked orders to his party, preparing them for a run.
EvilDemon sat in silence, meditating.
This was a collection of some of the most dangerous players in this ruined city.
’I wonder how they’ll react,’ Stark thought.
He turned toward the edge of the square.
Just like the first time he saw it, there stood the statue of a tall, eyeless figure cloaked in stone, hands folded as if in silent prayer.
It was ominous, but Stark knew what lay beneath.
This was only its "dormant" form, the moment it activated, it would become a terrifying monster.
As he approached, a system prompt appeared.
[To activate "Ruined City Travel", you will have to defeat a unique boss.]
Unique bosses were another type of monsters you could encounter.
They didn’t respawn. Once killed, they were gone forever.
Every [Ruined City] only had one of those statues, and the moment they were gone, they wouldn’t come back.
The [Unique Boss] title was reserved to extremely powerful bosses though.
Zones could regenerate. Bosses inside them could respawn.
Even special bosses sometimes reappeared in variations.
But not unique bosses. These were once-in-a-lifetime fights.
Stark placed his hand on the pedestal at the statue’s base.
Mana surged into it, and the stone began to hum.
Ding!
---
[You have met the conditions to activate the unique epic-rank boss: "Man of Steel (Level 17)."]
[Are you sure you want to activate it? This cannot be undone.]
[Yes] [No]
---
Stark stared at the prompt.
His eyes flicked across the square.
Starfall, Ghost, PrinceLucas, EvilDemon, all of them were there, though they didn’t yet know what he was about to do.
’If I kill it fast enough... it won’t matter,’ he thought.
And with no hesitation, he selected [Yes].
It had happened in his past life anyway, and every ruined city would have to go through it.
Might as well be now.
Fwish! Boom!
The statue exploded with force, sending dust and shards across the square.
The ground shook, and gasps filled the crowd.
The stone figure trembled... then moved. Its hands unfolded.
The hood cracked apart, revealing the steel-like surface of its body beneath.
Ding!
[The "Man of Steel" has awakened.]

chapters.title: Chapter 35: The Man of Steel, Chaos in the Square
chapters.content:
Chapter 35: Chapter 35: The Man of Steel, Chaos in the Square
[The "Man of Steel" has awakened.]
The boss stirred slowly, plates grinding against each other.
Then it jumped down from the pedestal it had been standing on—
THUD!
The ground cracked under its weight.
"What the fuck?"
"Huh?"
Dozens of players in the square froze, staring wide-eyed.
Many instinctively backed away, their boots scraping against the stone floor.
The hulking figure was still shifting, not even fully transformed into its real form when a sharp notification cut through the silence.
Ding!
[Due to the influence of the "Man of Steel", this area has become a "Danger Zone".]
[Lives loss rate: 100]
Gasps erupted everywhere.
The panel hung in the air, mocking every player that stood inside the square.
The penalty applied to everyone.
Dying here meant losing one hundred lives in one go.
Most players had stacked up hundreds already, but losing that much in a single death? Unthinkable.
And worse, once you were trapped inside a [Danger Zone], logging out was impossible.
You had to endure thirty minutes before the system released you.
Panic rippled through the crowd.
But Stark? He ignored the message completely. His eyes were locked on the giant in front of him.
The [Man of Steel] towered at over ten meters tall, its bronze-colored frame reflecting its power.
Heavy and imposing, it looked like a war machine.
The moment its form settled, it raised both arms high into the air.
Fwish! BOOM!
The arms detonated.
Fragments scattered across the square, and from the wreckage extended two enormous blades of polished steel.
The [Man of Steel] swung them immediately, cutting down several nearby players in its first strike.
"Ahhh!"
"No, no—!"
Blood splattered.
The steel blades cleaved through bodies like paper.
Its movements were brutal, but frighteningly quick for something its size.
The players counterattacked, spells and arrows flashing, but the boss’s armored body absorbed most of it.
Its shell made it feel indestructible.
Stark had backed away from the initial transformation, and stayed calm.
He had been preparing for this fight.
Stark evolved all his skills for this moment.
Letting the [Man of Steel] evolve further into a legendary-rank monster would yield better loot and more experience, sure.
But Stark didn’t care about that right now. He wanted a clean kill.
The [Man of Steel] stepped forward, shaking the square as its steel feet punched into the ground.
The tremor forced many players back, scattering the unprepared.
Some chose to flee outright, running to the far edges of the square in panic.
But the ones who remained were fighters, those willing to risk their lives against a boss like this.
Stark glanced around quickly.
Grace stood firm near [Ghost], who had her twin daggers spinning, a silver aura flickering around her body.
’Perfect,’ Stark thought, ’I’ll get to see how they fight too.’
---
[Man of Steel (Level 17)]
[Rank: Epic]
[HP: 100,000]
[Description: The man of steel is a unique boss that guards the way of "Ruined City Travel". It is extremely dangerous.]
---
The boss had just as much HP as the [Undead Soul Mage], though it was two levels higher.
The reason was obvious: its defense was ridiculous.
Still, Stark wasn’t intimidated. Not with his current equipment.
He leveled his staff at the giant.
The [Man of Steel] continued forward, aiming for the square’s center.
Cataclysmic Fireball!
A fireball condensed at the tip of Stark’s staff, swelling rapidly until it matched his own size.
Fwish! BOOM!
-20,400!
The explosion rattled the air.
Stark blinked in surprise.
A single shot had ripped away nearly a fifth of the boss’s health.
Normally, [Cataclysmic Fireball] should’ve hit for 40,800.
But the boss’s passive, [Defense of Steel], halved all incoming damage.
Even so, it was a brutal opening blow.
He started to prepare another spell—
Fwish!
The boss lashed out, one steel blade slicing straight for him.
Stark dodged, only to be met by the second blade crashing toward him.
Strong Magic Barrier!
A shimmering wall of force appeared just in time.
CLANG!
-5,200!
The barrier trembled under the impact, spiderweb cracks running across its surface.
But it held. Stark grit his teeth.
’I need to hit it hard before it gets to phase two.’
Like the [Undead Soul Mage], the [Man of Steel] had two phases.
Its second phase triggered once its health dropped below 20,000, giving it an even more absurd defense and strength boost.
Luckily, these early bosses didn’t grow entirely new movesets yet, it was mostly to introduce players to phase mechanics.
Sovereign Vines!
Thick green vines shot up from the ground, wrapping toward the boss.
But the [Man of Steel] spun its blades, slicing them apart before they could hit.
Tchk! CRACK!
The vines fell, severed.
"Poison’s useless too,’ Stark thought grimly, ’Corrosive Crystal won’t stick to steel.’
Fine. Then he’d use something else.
Lightning Strike!
A jagged bolt cracked from his staff, slamming into the boss’s chest.
-15,300! (Weakness)
Sparks danced across its frame. Stark’s lips curved upward.
’Lightning, huh? So that’s the weak point.’
The damage looked weaker than his fireball, but that was only because the fireball was boosted by his spirit percentage.
In reality, the lightning’s base damage was 10,200, multiplied by 1.5 thanks to the elemental weakness.
And more importantly—
["Man of Steel" has been stunned!]
The giant froze mid-step.
Blue sparks crawled across its armored plates as the stun effect locked it down.
Normally, bosses resisted stuns completely.
But when tied to an elemental weakness, the chance skyrocketed.
Stark hadn’t expected it, but he wasn’t complaining.
The opening was all the other players needed.
"Now!" someone shouted.
EvilDemon raised his scepter.
Demonic Beam!
Fwish! BOOM!
A crimson beam slammed into the boss’s torso.
-3,000! -3,000! -3,000!
The ticks chewed away for a total of 15,000.
Ghost acted next.
She dashed from Grace’s side, her form blurring into a streak of silver light.
In one fluid leap, she launched herself upward, twin blades flashing.
SLASH! SLASH!
-7,893! -7,893!
She landed lightly, aura still crackling around her.
Stark narrowed his eyes. Every hit was halved.
Which meant EvilDemon’s attack should’ve dealt 30,000 total, and Ghost’s double strike nearly 16,000 each.
’These two... They’re monsters in their own right,’ Stark thought, ’In my past life, they must have crushed this boss easily.’
Seeing players like them firsthand was a rare experience.
Soon, after the [First Calamity], almost everyone would be struggling just to survive.
The talented and strong ones would vanish into higher-level areas, leaving the weaker behind.
But for now, Stark could study them.
He raised his staff again.
Another [Cataclysmic Fireball] roared into existence and blasted forward.
BOOM!
-20,400!
The boss’s HP bar dropped sharply.
[Man of Steel HP: 13,114/100,000]
Then the giant moved again.
Its body vibrated, a deafening hum echoing across the square.
Pressure radiated outward as its bronze plates began to glow.
The color shifted, bronze melting into polished silver.
The blades in its hands thickened and grew, doubling in length.
Its face remained eyeless, expressionless, but the aura it exuded changed entirely.
’Here it comes,’ Stark thought, coldly, ’Now it reduces attacks received by 90%.’
Ding!
[Man of Steel has entered its second phase.]
The message slammed into every player’s vision, forcing them to understand what they were now up against.

chapters.title: Chapter 36: Man of Steel’s Second Phase, Church Sanctuary Key
chapters.content:
Chapter 36: Chapter 36: Man of Steel’s Second Phase, Church Sanctuary Key
[Man of Steel has entered its second phase.]
The boss raised its massive steel blades, then slammed them into the ground with such force the entire square shook.
The stone cracked beneath its weight, and the shockwave sent dust rising in a cloud.
Then, without waiting, it launched forward.
Its glowing eyes locked directly on Stark, the one who had dealt the most damage.
It swung its two blades at the same time.
CRASH!
The blades hit Stark’s [Strong Magic Barrier], shattering it instantly into fragments of blue light.
"!!!"
Stark immediately backed away.
The barrier collapsing so fast told him everything he needed to know.
Even after recasting it, the boss would break it in two or three strikes.
That meant one thing: its attacks carried damage over 5,000.
No normal player could tank that. Not without an invincibility or evasion skill.
But Stark didn’t hesitate.
Cataclysmic Fireball! Corrosive Crystal! Lightning Strike!
Fwish! BOOM!
The spells detonated one after another.
-4,080! -700! -3,060!
The boss staggered backward.
Its health bar, even under 90% damage reduction, dropped into the red zone.
It was on the verge of death.
Even with its insane defenses, Stark’s repeated bombardment was simply too much.
His spells were relentless, each one layered on top of the last, with almost no delay.
But this time, the boss wasn’t stunned.
It roared, stepping forward with terrifying speed, and swung again.
BOOM!
The attack ripped through the square, forcing Stark to roll aside as the blade carved a deep gash through the stone.
He barely avoided it.
The pressure from its movements only grew heavier.
"Are you insane?"
A voice came from behind.
Stark glanced for a split second before focusing back on the boss.
It was [Ghost].
The assassin appeared like a shadow, twin daggers gleaming faintly under the broken light of the square.
Based on what Stark had seen and what he knew, her class was one of the strongest assassin classes in [Eternal Soul].
Combined with her skill, her talent had to be SS-Level.
SS-Level, Stark had only seen a few players in his past life with such a thing.
He had no idea if anyone else besides him possessed an SSS-Level talent, but he doubted anyone would openly admit it if they did.
"What do you mean," Stark muttered, his staff glowing again.
Sovereign Vines!
Thick vines burst from the ground, reaching toward the Man of Steel.
CLANG!
The boss sliced them apart instantly, forcing Stark to keep retreating.
Step by step, he gave ground, and the boss advanced closer and closer to the center of the square.
The majority of the players who had been watching were already gone.
Those that stayed only looked from the edges, unwilling to come close.
No one wanted to be caught in that monster’s range.
Demonic Beam!
EvilDemon pointed his scepter, firing a ray of red light.
-3,000!
The damage was decent, but against this boss, it was only a scratch.
"What do you mean," Stark repeated, bracing as the boss’s blades slammed down against his [Strong Magic Barrier] again.
The barrier cracked, then broke, but Stark’s casting speed kept him alive.
"You’re a mage!" Ghost sounded almost exasperated as she darted forward, "You’re supposed to, ugh, never mind."
She didn’t waste more words.
Her body blurred as she lunged at the boss.
Its HP was down to less than 4,000 now, almost gone.
’Fast.’
Stark’s eyes followed her.
As an assassin, she was faster than anyone else here.
And with her invisibility and burst damage, she was dangerous even to players like Stark.
Fwish! Ghost Slash!
She crossed her daggers in an arc, striking toward the Man of Steel’s chest.
CLANG!
But the boss reacted in time, raising one of its huge steel blades to deflect both attacks.
Sparks burst from the impact.
Then, without hesitation, it swung its other blade in a deadly counter, aiming straight at Ghost while she was still mid-air.
"Oh," Ghost muttered, almost casually, "Damn."
One couldn’t forget, the Man of Steel was a Level 17 Epic-Rank Unique Boss.
If anyone besides Stark had been the one to fight it directly, they wouldn’t have lasted more than seconds.
EvilDemon’s beams could only work in intervals, his cooldowns limiting him.
Ghost, on the other hand, had the agility and burst to potentially take it down, but only if she could strike without getting hit.
The fact that the boss actually parried her attack meant it wasn’t going to be easy.
And right now, she couldn’t dodge.
The blade was already descending.
But before it connected—ʀᴇᴀᴅ ʟᴀᴛᴇsᴛ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀᴛ NovᴇlFirenᴇt
Cataclysmic Fireball!
FWISH! BOOM!
-4,080!
The fireball slammed into the Man of Steel’s side.
The boss froze mid-motion, its body convulsing as the flames burned through the last of its HP.
With a metallic screech, it collapsed to the ground, its blades crashing beside it.
THUD!
Ghost fell as well, landing hard and rolling before quickly pushing herself up.
She let out a long breath.
She hadn’t died in [Eternal Soul] yet.
But being that close to instant death... it shook her more than she wanted to admit.
Ding!
---
[You have killed "Man of Steel (Level 17 Epic-Rank Unique Boss)"]
[You have gained 75,000 experience points.]
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 16!]
[You have gained 5 points in all of your attributes, and 5 free points to distribute.]
[You have gained 10 Evolution Points!]
[You have gained 73 Lives!]
---
"Phew."
Since Stark had done the overwhelming majority of the damage, and he wasn’t in a team, he received almost all the experience.
The others who contributed gained some, but his share dwarfed theirs.
And more importantly, the loot was his.
He walked over to the boss’s crumbled remains, kneeling to check the drops.
[Dual Steel Blades (Epic): Warrior-type weapon. +207 Strength. Requirement: 16]
It only had one bonus, but it was massive.
+207 Strength at Epic rank was an insane stat boost.
Though it required Level 16, for a warrior it would be a weapon worth fighting over.
Stark stored it into his inventory. It would sell for a good price.
But he wasn’t done yet.
Hand of Avarice!
The spectral hand extended from his staff, clawing at the corpse.
Ding!
It succeeded. Another drop appeared beside the broken steel body.
Stark walked forward, picking it up.
"Wow..."
What dropped wasn’t an equipment piece. It wasn’t even consumable loot.
It was something much rarer.
---
[Church Sanctuary Key: Allows the user to open the "Church Sanctuary" (Level 25 zone) and access it.]
[Note: It only has one use, meaning that upon death, you won’t be able to enter again unless you find another key.]
---
His eyes narrowed slightly.
Key items like this were special.
Beyond gear, lives, and Evolution Points, monsters could also rarely drop these.
They unlocked zones or triggered unique events, and their drop rate was low.
’Did it drop because of Hand of Avarice’s loot rank increase? Or was it just pure luck?’
Regardless, this was huge.
The Church Sanctuary was one of the most important zones in the ruined city.
Getting early access would give Stark a huge advantage in leveling speed and loot opportunities.
Of course, he wouldn’t go now.
Entering a Level 25 zone while only Level 16 would be suicide.
He’d hold onto it until the right moment.
He carefully stored it in his inventory.
’Probably won’t reach that level until the first event starts... but when I do, this key will be priceless.’
Once done, Stark stood and walked toward the pedestal where the Man of Steel had been standing.
Defeating the boss meant one more thing.
[Ruined City Travel] could now be unlocked.
In his past life, his ruined city only activated it on the second day.
But this time, he was first.
He placed his hand on the pedestal.
Light spread across it, the stone glowing before reshaping into a circular portal.
Ding!
---
[Congratulations, you have activated "Ruined City Travel" in the First Ruined City.]
[You are now able to teleport to other ruined cities as long as their own portal is active.]
[You have gained 5 Prestige Points]
---
"Good," Stark grinned.
It was another step forward.
And just as he turned, he found Ghost standing a short distance away, her gaze fixed directly on him.
There was a curious light in her eyes, mixed with amusement.
"I can see why you’re the strongest now, Oblivion," she said with a faint smile. "It was good to fight with you."
She extended her hand.
Stark met it, gripping firmly.
Starfall quickly joined them, standing right beside Ghost, and she seemed shocked of what they just did.

chapters.title: Chapter 37: Exchanging with Ghost, Reaching the Outskirts
chapters.content:
Chapter 37: Chapter 37: Exchanging with Ghost, Reaching the Outskirts
"Are you... teaming with her?" Stark asked, tilting his head.
He couldn’t believe it.
Ghost, of all people, with someone else?
In his past life, she had always been alone. Always.
No one ever mentioned her teaming up, no matter how big the event or how dangerous it was.
Ghost was the definition of a solo player.
Now, though, watching her fight alongside Grace, Stark understood why she’d never needed anyone.
The damage Ghost could deal with her class and talent was absurd.
Monsters that should’ve been trouble just melted away.
For some reason, players who went solo often ended up the strongest.
Maybe it was because their classes and talents allowed it.
Maybe it was because they were confident enough to walk alone and thus gained more experience.
Either way, they stood out from the rest.
Ghost glanced at Stark, her face expressionless as always.
"I took a liking to her," she said simply. "She doesn’t disturb... and she deals decent damage."
Stark blinked. That last part sounded more like a joke than anything.
Ghost didn’t need backup. If she wanted, she could deal with everything herself.
"Oh well," Stark sighed. He wasn’t going to dig too deep.
Since they were both right in front of him, though, it felt like the perfect chance.
"Here."
He pulled out the [Revenant Staff] from his inventory and extended it toward Grace.
It was leagues better than her current weapon.
She was still carrying the same staff Stark had given her earlier, which was already outdated compared to what he could offer now.
Grace’s eyes widened slightly, but she already knew Oblivion wasn’t the type to hand things out for free.
"How much?" she asked.
"Hm..." Stark looked at the staff for a moment. "Two lives."
He said it casually, almost like a joke. But—
Ding!
[You have received 2 lives from "Starfall"]
"Hm."
Stark nodded, satisfied. The two lives weren’t much.
For him, it wasn’t about value. It was about principle.
He didn’t want to give away anything for free.
Even if it was just one life, he’d take it.
Grace smiled faintly, almost amused. Stark wasn’t finished, though.
"I also have something for you," he said, smirking. "Though... it’ll take more than two lives for these items."
He pulled out two more treasures from his inventory: The [Alley Reaper Cloak (Elite)] and [Alley Reaper Scythe (Elite)].
Both were rare drops, and both were extremely powerful at this stage of the game.
The requirement to use them was level 15. Ghost wasn’t there yet, but she was close.
Ghost’s calm mask cracked for the first time.
Her eyes locked on the items, and Stark saw her expression shift ever so slightly.
She was extremely calm usually, but this... was insane.
She recovered quickly, though, hiding it under her usual neutral face.
"I am willing to pay any amount you ask for," she said, "But... I don’t think I have the experience to do anything else."
Stark: ?
EvilDemon, passing by in the distance: ?
PrinceLucas and his team, overhearing nearby: ?
Grace: ⚆ᗝ⚆?
Stark was genuinely confused. Did she misunderstand him?
He only meant "more than two lives" in terms of price.
Ghost probably thought it meant... something else entirely.
"Ahem..." Ghost coughed lightly, regaining her composure. "So how much do you want?"
Stark smirked. These items could easily sell for fifty lives each.
And someone would gladly pay that price.
But—
"Twenty-five lives each," he said. "I’m giving you a discount."
Ghost stared at him for a few seconds. Then, slowly, she smiled.
Ding!
[You have received 50 lives from "Ghost"]
Stark passed her the items.
Ghost tucked them into her inventory, her fingers brushing over them like she couldn’t wait to use them.
She checked the scythe first.
One of the passives glowed faintly in its description.
’A passive too... Just what is his goal?’ she thought.
Her [Assassin’s Intuition] passive skill didn’t trigger. No ill intent. No hidden scheme. Just Oblivion being Oblivion.
She bowed her head slightly. "Thank you. I’ll be going now. We need to focus on leveling before the [First Calamity]."
Stark nodded. "Good idea."
Grace waved at him before following Ghost out of sight.
Everything was falling into place.
Stark had reached level 16, and Ghost had her path forward.
But he wasn’t done yet. He needed more experience. A lot more.
That meant heading deeper into the [Ruined City] to look for stronger monsters.
He also had access to the [Church Sanctuary] now.
A level 25 zone, one of the hardest areas in the entire city.
Players avoided it in his past life even when they reached level 25.
Which, of course, meant Stark was interested.
Thankfully, [Eternal Soul] didn’t weigh him down with exhaustion.
The game had mechanics for fatigue, but the stronger you became, the less it affected you.
Stark could grind for hours without worrying about collapse.
He checked his lives again.
[Lives: 1497]
’Oh shit.’
Nearly fifteen hundred. Enough to fully transfer his levels to the real world if he wanted, but his skills... would take more.
All of his skills were epic-rank or legendary-ranking.
Transferring each one cost seven hundred and fifty to a thousand lives.
He didn’t have anywhere near enough yet.
And then there was his staff. He’d need lives to carry that over too.
The square had finally calmed down.
The chaos from the appearance of the [Man of Steel] earlier had sent waves of panic through players.
This was the first time they had seen a [Lives loss rate] be set so high.
But now, with the danger zone cleared, the tension was gone.
Stark didn’t linger. He slipped out of the square, no one daring to follow.
’Even deeper now,’ he thought, grinning.
Dozens of monsters blocked his way through the ruined streets.
Dozens more lurked in alleys and broken courtyards.
None of them slowed him down.
His [Cataclysmic Fireball] wiped out the [Ruined Sentinel General] in one hit.
His [Sovereign Vines] ripped apart groups that tried to ambush him.
The deeper he went, the stronger the monsters became.
Near the square, they were level 11. Midpoint, they climbed to level 14, then 15.
And beyond that? Stark knew he was heading straight into the end-zones of the [Ruined City].
And then—
Ding!
[You have reached the "Outskirts" of the "Ruined City"]
[Lives loss rate: 20]
The system prompt confirmed it.
This wasn’t just stronger monsters, it was a warning.
[Eternal Soul] liked to remind players how dangerous the world could be. Lives loss could spike at any time.
From 5 to 20. Just like that.
For normal players, it was terrifying.
For Stark? Stronger monsters meant faster growth.
He took another step forward, and the moment he did...
Fwish! BOOM!
The ground split open. Stone erupted from the earth.
Figures rose from the ruined ground, shaped like warriors but carved from rock.
Their hollow eyes glowed faintly.
In the middle of their foreheads, a swirling orb pulsed with energy.ɴᴇᴡ ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀʀᴇ ᴘᴜʙʟɪsʜᴇᴅ ᴏɴ
---
[Ruined City Guardian (Level 17)]
[Rank: Elite]
[HP: 65,000]
---
They had no weapons. They didn’t need them. Their fists were boulders.
The health and strength of monsters were also slowly climbing as Stark went on.
But that was expected. Beyond the [Ruined City], the world truly opened up.
Stark gripped his staff tighter.
Cataclysmic Fireball! Sovereign Vines!
Fwish! Boom! Swash!
-40,800!-35,775!
Two of the guardians collapsed instantly, crumbling into piles of stone.
[Eternal Soul] was designed to be brutal.
Normal players struggled with elites, even at their own level.
Yet Stark was dominating.
His grin widened.
"Come to me, experience points. I really need to hit level 25!"
He lifted his staff again, already preparing his next wave of spells.
The guardians moved in, their massive stone fists swinging like hammers.
Stark didn’t back down.

chapters.title: Chapter 38: You are Tired, Extracting Levels to the Real World
chapters.content:
Chapter 38: Chapter 38: You are Tired, Extracting Levels to the Real World
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 17!]
[You have gained 5 points in all of your attributes, and 5 free points to distribute.]
---
It had taken hours of grinding.
Stark pushed through wave after wave of monsters, killing them without any hesitation.
And finally, he hit his target.
None of the nearby monsters could touch him anymore.
As long as he didn’t bump into an over-leveled one, he was fine.
Everything else was just fuel for his growth.
And the best part?
[You have gained 17 Evolution Points!]
[You have gained 379 Lives!]
"Perfect," Stark muttered. His face lit up with satisfaction.
The grind was starting to drag on, though.
[Experience Decay] was kicking in hard, and the amount required to reach the next level was absurd.
[Level: 17 (7,200/100,000)]
The numbers didn’t lie. It would only get worse from here.
But while testing things, Stark had discovered something else.
Back at level 16, he’d tried killing a level 11 [Ruined Sentinel General].
The fight was easy. He expected a small reward because of decay.
What shocked him was different, he got no Evolution Points.
The first time he’d killed that boss, he received 7 EP. Now? Nothing.
"...So it applies here too." Stark narrowed his eyes.
That confirmed it. There wasn’t just [Experience Decay] and [Lives Decay].
There was [EP Decay] as well. Bosses only dropped good EP rewards if they were the same level or higher than him. Otherwise, it was wasted effort.
Meaning... he couldn’t slack.
If he wanted power, he had to continuously take on monsters equal to his level or stronger.
That suited him just fine.
While leveling, Stark had also been stacking up items, filling up his inventory.
’I need more space,’ Stark thought. ’I need to find another way to expand my storage.’
Later, when he reached the first NPC town in [Eternal Soul], this would matter even more.
Because NPCs weren’t useless decorations.
They could buy loot too. And they sold equipment.
The catch? NPC gear wasn’t cheap.
And if Stark wanted to compete against top players, he’d need room for resources.
Before he could plan further, a panel appeared.
[You are tired.]
"Oh." Stark blinked.
That only happened if you stayed too long in [Eternal Soul].
It didn’t hurt him now, but the penalty would worsen the longer he ignored it.
Sluggish movements. Reduced combat power. If he pushed, it’d be suicide.
He had half-expected not to see the warning at all.
In his last life, he’d spent months inside this game, barely blinking.
But that was only because the further you advanced, the less "tired" you would be.
He’d thought maybe his body was just... immune. Apparently not.
This was the system’s way of forcing breaks.
Stark sighed. He couldn’t ignore it forever.
Still—
’I have time. Enough to reach 25 before the first event,’ Stark thought with a grin. ’I’ll be fine.’
For now, he’d do one last thing before logging off.
He opened the [Extraction Menu].
---
[1. Extract Class and Talent] (Completed)
[2. Extract Level]
[3. Extract Skills]
[4. Extract Equipment]
[5. Extract Bloodline (Not available)]
[6. Extract ??? (Not available)]
---
He picked the second option instantly.
[Do you wish to use 1,000 Lives to extract your levels to the real world?]
[Note: This will synchronize your levels in "Eternal Soul" to the real world, up to level 25.]
He already knew the details. Levels could be synchronized to the real world.
The cap was 25 for now. Beyond that, the cost skyrocketed.
Everyone who played should’ve realized something by now.
If the [First Calamity] had "First" in its name... there would be more.
It wasn’t just calamities either. Events. Bosses. Threats. The system wouldn’t stop throwing them in humanity’s face.
But Stark didn’t care. Not yet.
"Yes."
Ding!
[You have consumed 1,000 Lives.]
[You have synchronized your levels (up to 25) to the real world.]
His attributes carried over as well.
Which meant his body outside the game was no longer "normal."
Stronger, faster, tougher, everything stacked up.
With this durability alone, a normal bullet would bounce off him.
[You are exhausted.]
"Yeah, yeah." Stark rolled his eyes at the message.
The system was persistent.
He couldn’t feel the exhaustion himself, but the panel didn’t care about his opinion.
Ding!
[Do you wish to leave "Eternal Soul"?]
[Yes] [No]
For the second time, he selected [Yes].
His body broke down into countless glowing blue fragments. Slowly dissolving, until he was gone.
He’d be back soon enough. For now, he needed a few hours of rest in the real world.
...
Meanwhile.
"Oh," Grace muttered. "Oblivion went offline."
She was standing next to [Ghost], her current teammate.
They had been grinding together for a while now.ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ NovᴇlFir(e).nᴇt
Even giving her best effort, Grace could barely manage a quarter of Ghost’s damage.
Ghost was on another level.
"I find it weird you’re friends with that guy," Ghost said casually, cutting down a level 17 [Ruined City Guardian].
Fwish! Slash!
[Weakness hit! Instant kill!]
The monster dropped instantly.
That wasn’t just raw power. That was Ghost’s hidden edge.
She wasn’t a normal assassin.
She had the hidden class [Vengeful Assassin], already one of the strongest assassin paths.
And her Talent? Even more broken. SS-Level [Eternal Ghost].
It granted her two passives right now. One of them was what she had just used.
[Passive #1: If you manage to hit an opponent’s weakness, there is a big chance you will instantly kill them.]
That one sentence explained why Ghost was feared.
Even bosses weren’t safe. If she found the weak point, she could instantly deal the entire HP pool as lethal damage.
A [Ruined Sentinel General] with 35,000 HP? Dead in one strike.
Of course, against monsters like [Man of Steel] that had no obvious weak spots, this passive did nothing.
But for everything else? She carved through them like paper.
’Still,’ Ghost thought, watching the monsters respawn around them, ’my leveling speed is slowing.’
Grace, meanwhile, fired bolts of magic from a distance.
She wasn’t as fast, but she made herself useful.
"If only I had a healing spell," Grace sighed. "I wish I had rolled a priest or something."
Ghost shook her head with a grin. "I don’t think that’s how it works. I feel like... [Eternal Soul] picks the class and talent that suits you best."
"You think so?" Grace frowned, scratching her chin. "Maybe... I guess that means I just need to try harder to be a support mage, huh?"
It made sense.
Most mage players chased flashy attack spells.
Fireballs, lightning, explosions. They wanted to be the center of every fight.
But there was another path. Support mages.
Instead of killing everything themselves, they boosted allies with buffs and tactical control.
Some would even say support mages were more useful than pure damage dealers.
Grace seemed to realize that.
Her eyes lit up with determination.
’If I can support [Ghost]... and maybe even [Oblivion]... that’d be perfect for me.’
"Alright, let’s keep moving," Ghost said, grabbing the drops from the last corpse. "Oblivion’s offline. Good chance to get ahead."
Grace tilted her head.
She didn’t really understand why Ghost was so competitive.
Oblivion hadn’t shown much interest in racing anyone.
But Ghost clearly wanted it. So Grace simply followed.
Together, they stepped deeper into the ruins.
Ding!
[You have reached the "Outskirts" of the "Ruined City"]
[Lives loss rate: 20]
They had finally arrived at the same area Stark had been farming for hours.
Needless to say, it would take them a while to catch up, allowing him to rest.

chapters.title: Chapter 39: Real World Attributes, Heading Even Deeper
chapters.content:
Chapter 39: Chapter 39: Real World Attributes, Heading Even Deeper
Stark’s body reformed in the real world the moment he left [Eternal Soul].
The sunlight bleeding through his window.
Outside, people were walking around like nothing had changed.
Some hurried to work, others sat at cafés, sipping coffee, laughing, living their "normal" lives.
Even after experiencing all of this and having to fight monsters to reach level 3.
To them, [Eternal Soul] was still just a game. Something they could ignore.
Stark snorted.
A mistake. One that would kill them sooner or later. But not his problem.
All he needed now was a few hours of rest.
Just enough to reset his body, calm his nerves, and then he’d dive right back into the game.
Still, before collapsing into bed, Stark opened his status window for the second time in the real world.
---
[ID: Oblivion]
[Class: Mage of Oblivion (Tier-1)]
[Talent: Infinite Evolution (SSS)]
[Level: 17 (7,200/100,000)]
[Lives: 876]
[Constitution: 90]
[Strength: 90]
[Agility: 117]
[Spirit: 133]
[Skills: None.]
---
"Phew."
There it was. His real-world sync.
The levels he gained inside [Eternal Soul] carried over. Meaning his attributes carried too.
He clenched his fist. The strength behind it felt real.
The density in his muscles, the sharpened reflexes, it was all there.
Of course, equipment didn’t transfer. Neither did the ability to use skills.
But still, stats alone made him far beyond any normal human.
He could crush steel with his bare hands if he wanted.
And right now, he was sure of one thing: no one else on Earth had power like his.
Most players hadn’t even cracked level 10 yet.
They had no idea. They didn’t know that once you reached the [Eternal Continent], the wall between reality and game shattered.
That power could bleed out. That you could carry it into the real world.
Only those that reached the [Eternal Continent] could give information.
"Can’t save everyone," Stark muttered. "Leave them to their own fate."
He stretched once, tossed himself onto the bed, and stared at the ceiling.
Compared to his past life, he was already stronger.
Back then, he had relied on Max and Seren for too much.
This time? He was carving his own path.
The corners of his mouth twitched upward. Satisfied.
Not even a full day had passed, and he had already rewritten his future.
And eventually, he feel asleep.
...
Five hours later, Stark’s eyes snapped open.
That was all he needed now.
The deeper you went into [Eternal Soul], the less you required sleep.
Your body changed. Your energy surged. Fatigue faded faster, replaced by vitality.
Food, too, became different.
Some NPC meals could keep you awake and sharp for days.
But now? Five hours was plenty. His body felt light, his thoughts clear.
No reason to stay here any longer.
Ding!
[Do you wish to enter "Eternal Soul"?]
[Yes] [No]
"Yes."
His body dematerialized. The real world dissolved.
And then—
Ding!
[You have returned to the "Eternal Continent".]
[You are full of energy.]
Stark grinned. "Good."
No hesitation. First thing he did: check the leaderboard.
---
[Level Leaderboard:]
[1. Oblivion: Level 17]
[2. Ghost: Level 17]
[3. EvilDemon: Level 17]
[4. Starfall: Level 16]
[5. PrinceLucas: Level 16]
[6. GodOfViolence: Level 16]
[7. DivineGoddess: Level 16]
[8. BraveCop: Level 15]
...
---
The names hadn’t changed. Same top ranks, same faces.
Stark still at the top. Even after all these hours.
But the pace would slow now. The experience curve steepened after level 15.
Players would realize just how sharp the climb was.
He eyed the second spot. Ghost.
Still there. Still keeping up.
And Grace, her leveling speed shocked him too.
Not on her own, of course. Ghost’s help carried her forward.
But Stark still couldn’t wrap his head around it.
Ghost, THE Ghost, one of the hundred strongest in his past life, choosing her of all people?
Still, he shoved the thought aside.
Right now, he had other priorities.
The [Outskirts] of the [Ruined City] stretched around him.Tʜe source of this ᴄontent ɪs ɴovel(ꜰ)ɪre.nᴇt
Crumbling walls, broken buildings, and an oppressive silence.
Every death here drained 20 lives. The monsters, too, were stronger.
But what caught Stark’s attention most was the density of zones.
More than outside.
The logic was simple: the deeper you went, the more danger, the more experience.
Players needed faster, riskier ways to grow. Zones delivered that.
And somewhere in this broken city... the [Church Sanctuary].
He had no plans to enter, not yet.
A level 25 zone was suicide after all, but at least he wanted to know where it was.
Still, he shook his head.
Leveling came first.
If he reached level 25 before the first event, then he’d be in position to claim the items he needed.
’Each event bring a new opportunity, and I already have a general idea of what I want,’ Stark grinned, ’Better get this over with.’
He stepped forward, deeper into the outskirts.
He encountered some level 17 monsters on the way.
They lunged at him. They died in seconds. His spells tore through them like paper.
But the experience bar barely moved.
No EP, either.
Frowning, Stark pulled open his panel.
[Current Evolution Points: 33.]
"...Oh?"
He blinked. Then the realization hit.
Almost all of his skills were already at legendary-rank. Only three remained at epic.
And the cost to evolve epic to legendary was ten EP each.
Which meant... he had enough to push every last skill into legendary.
His lips curved upward.
’Perfect!’
He was just about to do it, curiosity burning in his chest, eager to see what kind of evolutions would appear.
But...
Fwshhh!
Ruined Bite!
Stark’s instincts screamed, and he twisted aside.
A flash of teeth, a shadow lunging—
SNAP!
A massive jaw clamped down where his neck had been a heartbeat earlier.
He landed in a roll, staff in hand, eyes narrowing.
And when he analyzed the monster that attacked him... he noticed that it was a level 18 boss!
’Finally,’ Stark thought, ’Took long enough.’
He had only encountered level 16 and level 17 monsters until now, so seeing a new level was good.
---
[Ruined City Dog Leader (Level 18)]
[Rank: Rare (Boss)]
[HP: 75,000]
---
It loomed over him, nearly four meters tall.
Fur blackened, chunks missing like rotting flesh, eyes glowing faint red.
Its breath stank of decay. Around it, a pack circled, around half a dozen of smaller beasts, each snarling.
---
[Ruined City Dog (Level 18)]
[Rank: Uncommon]
[HP: 60,000]
---
"Perfect," Stark muttered.
The pack growled, forming a circle.
The leader stood at the center, fangs bared.
"Let me kill you all so I can evolve my skills."
His staff lit up as he pointed it at them, and mana surged.
Cataclysmic Fireball!
A blazing orb bloomed at the staff’s tip, swelling in size, pressure shaking the air.
He unleashed it.
Fwoooosh! BOOM!
-42,300!
The explosion ripped through the dogs.
The leader staggered, half its health bar gone in one shot.
The others fared worse, two-thirds of their HP erased instantly.
One spell. The battlefield changed in an instant.
Growls turned to furious howls.
Ding!
["Ruined City Dog Leader" has entered a "Berserk" state.]
"Oh?"
Being "berserk" didn’t actually count as a new phase for a boss or monster, but it greatly enhanced their attributes and killing intent.
And...
RUINED ROAR!
The leader threw its head back and howled.
The sound rattled the ruins, shook the ground.
And from the shadows, more dogs poured in.
The pack more than doubled.
Every single one received a buff, their movements sharper, their attacks deadlier.
Stark exhaled, a grin spreading across his face.
"Haha... guess I should’ve expected that."
Dozens of red eyes glared at him. Dozens of bodies prepared to leap.
And Stark simply lifted his staff again.
"Come on, then."

chapters.title: Chapter 40: Killing the Dog Pack, 24 Hours Have Passed
chapters.content:
Chapter 40: Chapter 40: Killing the Dog Pack, 24 Hours Have Passed
All the dogs surrounding Stark had been buffed by the [Ruined Roar] of the leader.
Their fur bristled, eyes glowing faintly red from the effect.
Their movements had become sharper, their snarls more vicious.
Each step they took cracked the rubble beneath their claws.
But even then... it didn’t bother Stark that much!
When a dozen dogs rushed at him together, he didn’t even flinch.
He simply spun his staff in his grip, planted his feet firmly on the broken street, and activated his [Strong Magic Barrier].
A shimmering dome of light snapped into place around him just in time—
BAM! BAM! BAM!
All the dogs slammed into it at once, claws screeching across the surface, fangs snapping against it with crazed force.
The barrier shook violently, spiderweb cracks spreading fast, but it didn’t collapse.
"Good enough," Stark muttered with a smirk, ’Killing the leader will remove the buff, then the others will be defenseless.’
His grin widened as he raised his staff toward the ruined city dog leader.
Sovereign Vines!
The ground beneath the dogs split open with a violent rumble.
Dark-green vines shot out like spears, slamming into every single dog in the area.
Their yelps echoed in the air as the impact sent them tumbling.
-36,150!
The numbers floated up, bright and satisfying.
A normal player might have had to fight for several minutes with a well-coordinated team to bring down this pack.
Unless you had a class or a talent that was outrageously powerful, the [Ruined City Dogs] and their leader were simply too much to handle solo.
But for Stark... It only took two spells.
The leader froze mid-step, as the vines crushed through its chest.
Its 75,000 HP bar plummeted to zero in an instant, and the massive beast collapsed onto the cracked street, lifeless.
Beside it, several of the lesser dogs, already weakened from the earlier [Cataclysmic Fireball], dropped dead as well, leaving only a handful still standing.
Those that survived skidded to a halt, growling uncertainly.
Their glowing eyes darted from their fallen leader back to the lone human standing in front of them.
The confusion didn’t last long.
They began to tremble.
They couldn’t understand it, how had one human, just one, killed their entire pack so easily?
And so... instinct took over.
They turned tail and tried to run.
"Oh hell no," Stark grinned, raising his staff high. "You’re not getting away."
Cataclysmic Fireball! Corrosive Crystals! Lightning Strike!
The spells erupted in rapid succession.
A roaring fireball exploded against the fleeing pack, consuming a cluster of them in flames.
Five more were pierced clean through by his corrosive crystals.
And the last dog, the farthest one, was struck by a crackling bolt of lightning.
Its body stiffened mid-leap, locked in place as arcs of electricity danced violently across its fur.
Stark walked forward, staff lowered, watching them drop one after another.
"None of you are leaving."
The dogs must have realized it now.
No matter how fast they ran, no matter how desperately they struggled, they couldn’t escape this human.
One by one... they fell.
Ding!
---
[You have killed "Ruined City Dog Leader (Level 18 Rare-Rank Boss)"]
[You have killed x14 "Ruined City Dogs (Level 18)"]
[You have gained 69,000 experience points.]
[You have gained 8 Evolution Points!]
[You have gained 56 Lives!]
---
This wasn’t quite enough to level up, but Stark was close, and satisfied.
Hand of Avarice!
[You have gained 6 Evolution Points!]
[You have gained 48 Lives!]
"Perfect."
He bent down, picking up the few items the dogs had dropped.
[Ruined City Fur (Rare)], [Ruined Dog Claw Dagger (Uncommon)], and a couple other scraps.
Not bad, but his inventory was starting to look dangerously full.
’My inventory is yet again starting to fill up,’ Stark thought with a click of his tongue.
He’d have to see if any players were selling backpacks soon, though he doubted it.
Every single player in the [Ruined City] already knew by now that inventory space was limited, and that made any storage item worth a fortune.
For now, though, he pushed that problem aside and opened his status.
[Current Evolution Points: 47.]
"Perfect."
He only needed three more to evolve a legendary skill into mythical.
But instead of rushing it, Stark decided against it.
He much preferred evolving his three remaining epic-rank skills to legendary first.
And so he did.
[Do you wish to consume 10 Evolution Point to evolve "Stronger Magic Barrier"?]
"Yes."
Ding!
[You have evolved "Strong Magic Barrier" (Epic) to "Powerful Magic Barrier" (Legendary)]
[Current Evolution Points: 37.]
---
[Powerful Magic Barrier (Legendary): Summon a barrier around the user that can endure attacks, it has 10,000 → 20,000 HP. 30 (15)-seconds cooldown.]
---
"Good."
With that barrier in place, it would take either a powerful boss or an incredibly high-damage monster to even break through.
Most enemies couldn’t touch him now.
The cooldown hadn’t gone down, but it hadn’t gone up either. That was good enough.ʀᴇᴀᴅ ʟᴀᴛᴇsᴛ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀᴛ No(ᴠ)ᴇlFire.nᴇt
Moving quickly, he shifted to his next two skills.
[Do you wish to consume 10 Evolution Point to evolve "Corrosive Crystals"?]
"Yes."
Ding!
[You have evolved "Corrosive Crystals" (Epic) to "Plague Crystals" (Legendary)]
But instead of stopping to check the panel, Stark instantly moved to the next one.
[Do you wish to consume 10 Evolution Point to evolve "Lightning Strike"?]
"Yes."
Ding!
[You have evolved "Lightning Strike" (Epic) to "Storm of Lightning" (Legendary)]
[Current Evolution Points: 17.]
’Perfect.’
He pulled up the panels together.
---
[Plague Crystals (Legendary): Summon up to 5 → 10 crystals that deal 700 → 1000 damage each. Applies the "Poison" status effect. 8 (4)-seconds cooldown.]
[Poison: Deals 30% → 40% of damage received for 5 seconds.]
---
[Storm of Lightning (Legendary): Releases a storm of lightning that will hit any enemy within radius, dealing 500% → 800% of spirit and also has a chance to apply "Stun". 20 → 18 (9)-seconds cooldown.]
---
Now every single one of his combat skills gleamed gold in his menu.
---
[Skills: Cataclysmic Fireball (Legendary), Powerful Magic Barrier (Legendary), Hand of Avarice (Legendary), Plague Crystals (Legendary), Sovereign Vines (Legendary), Curse Flower (Legendary), Storm of Lightning (Legendary)]
---
Stark clenched his fist.
With this power, he felt like he could even challenge the [Church Sanctuary] zone at level 25 already.
But he shook the thought aside.
The [Church Sanctuary Key] could only be used once.
Wasting it on overconfidence would be stupid.
’Six days until the [Ghost Hunt] event... I’ll grind until then.’
He had to reach at least level 25 before leaving the [Ruined City].
...
Hours passed in the [Outskirts].
Stark grinded relentlessly, killing everything in his path.
Most monsters here were level 16–19, and they went down easily under his spells.
The [Ruined Cities] were massive, sprawling across what felt like endless streets and collapsed towers.
It made sense, they had to be big enough to fit hundreds of thousands of players at once.
But size came with risk.
Monsters lurked in every corner, and progress was slow.
Still, Stark pushed forward.
By the time he stopped, he had leveled up twice.
---
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 18 + Level 19!]
[You have gained 10 points in all of your attributes, and 10 free points to distribute.]
[You have gained 27 Evolution Points!]
[You have gained 398 Lives!]
---
While grinding, he’d been testing too.
Fighting monsters below your level gave far less experience and lives, that much was obvious.
But when he checked, he confirmed something else.
With [Evolution Point Decay], he got no evolution points from enemies three levels below him.
One level lower gave him half. Two levels lower gave him a third.
Above his level, though, the rewards were slightly better.
It was clear: if he wanted to keep evolving fast, he had to fight tough opponents. No shortcuts.
Just as he was about to head toward a level 20 zone, a sharp ding rang out.
[You have gained 5 Evolution Points your talent’s passive.]
"Damn."
He had almost forgotten about that.
---
[Infinite Evolution (SSS): Upon killing strong monsters, there is a chance to obtain "Evolution Points", allowing you evolve your skills.]
[Passive: You gain 5 Evolution Points every 24 hours, it may increase with time.]
[Current Evolution Points: 49.]
---
That meant twenty-four hours had officially passed since the opening of [Eternal Soul].
Stark clenched his fist, smiling faintly.
"I’m infinitely stronger than I was in my past life. Perfect."
But just as he thought that—
A panel appeared in front of every single player in the [Eternal Continent].
Ding!
[The "First Calamity" is coming in 28 days.]

chapters.title: Chapter 41: More Players Have Arrived, Trying to Ambush Oblivion?
chapters.content:
Chapter 41: Chapter 41: More Players Have Arrived, Trying to Ambush Oblivion?
[The "First Calamity" is coming in 28 days.]
Of course, since this was the very first [Global Event], the one that would change the entire world, it was obvious [Eternal Soul] would keep pushing it.
Every single day, an announcement for all players on the [Eternal Continent] would appear, counting down the days.
And even if you weren’t inside the game, if you were in the real world, you would still see it flash before your eyes.
That made it even more ominous.
It drilled the countdown into your brain, like a reminder that the end was creeping closer.
In Stark’s past life, players had thought they were prepared.
They had farmed, leveled, and stacked up on items.
But when the day came... it wasn’t enough.
No one could understand the sheer scale of chaos that erupted.
Still, for now, Stark was satisfied with his progress for day one.
The 5 EP from his [Infinite Evolution] talent weren’t much, but it was still reassuring to know he had a passive gain ticking at all times.
In retrospect, it meant that even if he sat around and did nothing for two weeks, he’d walk away with 70 evolution points just for existing.
But Stark had no intention of sitting idle.
The real value came from killing monsters.
That was the reason this talent was terrifying, it snowballed with his pace.
’Maybe I’ll even be able to evolve the talent itself. Speed up the rate of EP gain. Or double the amount I get. If that’s possible...’ Stark smirked.
The thought of it alone made him restless.
Still, his inventory was stuffed to the brim now.
And the annoying part was that he hadn’t found a backpack yet, not even a basic one.
’I guess it’s time to move back to the square and sell my items.’
Sure, he could dump weaker items and keep farming for better ones, but there was no reason to waste loot like that.
The earlier he sold, the more demand there’d be.
The plan was simple: unload the loot, cash in the lives, then head straight back to the outskirts.
From there, he’d push deeper, into the level 20+ zones.
But—
Ding!
[Player "Starfall" has sent you a private message!]
[Starfall: Hey, Oblivion, me and Ghost found some weird zone in the outskirts. ʕ ◕ᴥ◕ ʔ]
"...?"
Stark blinked.
Why were they telling him this?
[Oblivion: Can’t you and Ghost clear it? With her damage and your... support, it should be possible.]
[Starfall: No! Ghost wanted to enter, but it said that she needed a key to enter! (ಥ﹏ಥ)]
Stark’s eyes narrowed at once.
’A zone that needs a key?’ His mind raced. ’Could it be the [Church Sanctuary]?’
That was the hardest zone in the entire [Ruined City].
He had planned to clear it last, but if they stumbled on the entrance this early, it was a blessing.
He didn’t know its exact location in his past life.
Now, he had a lead.
[Oblivion: What’s the name of the zone?]
[Starfall: The "City Sewers", it’s a level 22-24 zone! (✪‿✪)ノ]
"Oh."
