The monster’s strikes cracked the ground open, forcing Stark to maneuver carefully.
But finally, his barrier skill came off cooldown again.
Invincible Magic Barrier!
The shield reappeared, glowing bright.
Andregil smashed into it with both gauntlets at once—
CRAAACK!
The barrier shattered instantly. Over 40,000 damage in one strike.
But Stark only smiled faintly.
"...Dead."
Storm of Lightning! Blazing Meteor!
Zap! BOOM!
-86,508! -144,180!
The spells tore through the monster.
Andregil staggered, crimson aura flickering, health bar dropping to zero.
[Andregil HP: 0/1,000,000]
The titan froze mid-swing. His single eye dimmed.
His massive body pulsed with failing energy.
"No..." his voice was guttural, fading, "I was... supposed... to destroy everything..."
The words never finished.
His body collapsed sideways, crashing into the ruins of a building.
Dust and smoke rose into the air. And just like that... it was over.
The boss that had required a global effort in Stark’s past life.
The boss that had cost tens of thousands of lives and over a day of constant struggle.
Now, killed by him alone in barely an hour and a half.
’Perfect.’
Ding! Ding! Ding!
System announcements rang out, broadcast across the world.
---
[Player "Oblivion" is the first to kill a mythical-rank boss!]
[You have gained 15 Prestige Points!]
---
Ding!
---
[Player "Oblivion" is the first to kill the "First Calamity" boss: Andregil, Lord of Calamity.]
[You have gained 10 Prestige Points!]
---
The survivors everywhere froze as the message appeared.
"Holy shit, what is that?"
"Hey, I saw that [Lord of Calamity] monster, it was terrifying..."
"Same, I saw it destroy entire squares and kill hundreds of players, that thing’s a nightmare..."
Shock spread. But so did something else: resolve.
"If Oblivion can do it... then we can’t give up."
"Yeah. We can’t die here."
Without intending to, Stark had created a ripple effect.
His victory lit a fire in the survivors’ hearts.
...
Elsewhere...
"Heh," Ghost allowed herself a rare grin, "Of course."
Grace exhaled, her voice shaky.
"T-That [Lord of Calamity] was the thing we saw destroying everything... Luckily Oblivion killed it. I hope people are safe!"
"Unlikely," Ghost replied bluntly, "But killing it prevents more deaths. The worst of it is over now."
"...True," Grace admitted, her shoulders heavy.
...
Slash!
Max’s blade cut down another corrupted beast.
"We keep killing monsters and even bosses," he roared, sweat dripping down his face, "but we can’t even come close to that guy..."
Seren’s face was grim.
"That Lord of Calamity destroyed the entire city. We even died once when it rampaged through our street."
"There’s nothing we can do except focus on surviving."
"Yeah," Max sighed, his eyes dimming, "But once we enter [Eternal Soul] again after this... I’m sure more opportunities will open."
...
The world trembled.
But for the first time since the calamity began... small hope returned.

chapters.title: Chapter 82: Calamity Boots, Blessing Another Item
chapters.content:
Chapter 82: Chapter 82: Calamity Boots, Blessing Another Item
Ding!
---
[You have gained 30 Evolution Points!]
[You have gained 3,000 Lives!]
---
Hand of Avarice!
Ding!
---
[You have gained 20 Evolution Points!]
[You have gained 2,800 Lives!]
---
The boss’s corpse dissolved into motes of light after the fight.
Andregil’s remains left a scatter of drops across the scarred plaza.
Stark picked them up, one by one, reading the panels as he always did.
---
[Calamity Boots (Legendary): Physical Resistance +271, Movement Speed +17%. Requirement: Level 25]
[Calamity Shockwave (Active Skill): Slam your boots into the ground to release a shockwave toward enemies. 5-minutes cooldown.]
---
[Calamity Gauntlets (Mythical): Warrior-type accessory. +1,500 Strength, Attack Speed +31%. Requirement: Level 25]
[Calamity Strength (Passive): The user deals 2x damage while wearing the gauntlets.]
---
He left the rest of the items in his backpack as they were useless to a mage, but the boots fit nicely.
He traded out his shabby [Tower Wolf Fur Boots] without a second thought.
The gauntlets were different.
Mythical gear on their own were rare.
Gauntlets that doubled physical damage... that was borderline absurd for a non-warrior user.
Stark stepped back and looked at the crater where Andregil collapsed.
The monster had been the reason whole districts fell.
In the previous life thousands had died because they couldn’t beat that thing in time.
Here and now, it was dead on the start of day two.
He let the weight of that sink in for half a breath.
He’d prevented a full day of carnage in this city.
That didn’t mean everything was safe, every other city still had its own Andregil, and there were still monsters roaming.
But at least the biggest threat was gone in his own.
"Alright," Stark mumbled, "The only thing left to do is to kill all the monsters and bosses I see."
He would leave none of them standing.
And so, with that thought in mind, Stark rushed forward into the city, shooting spells at every monster he saw.
The second batch of monsters was indeed stronger than the first.
But to Stark... it made no difference!
Vines of Fate! Storm of Lightning! Blazing Meteor!
Slam! Zap! Boom!
The rare and elite mobs fell in groups.
And the bosses in the squares or the streets stood no chance either.
For hours he kept that pace.
The city turned into a graveyard for the calamity’s monsters.
Each kill added to his pile of Lives.
But eventually... And the bosses in the squares or the streets stood no chance either.
Ding!
[Your "Heart of Sanctuary" has recharged.]
"Oh?"
The condition for this [Special Item] to recharge was that Stark needed to kill monsters, and it seemed like... he had killed enough!
[You are now allowed to "bless" another item.]
He had met the conditions, and so he didn’t waste any seconds.
But in comparison to what most would do in this case... Stark didn’t "bless" any of his equipment.
Stark thought differently.
He unclipped his [Calamity Fur Backpack], the legendary pack he’d looted earlier, and held it out..
He focused the power of the special item on it and...
Ding!
[You have used the "Heart of Sanctuary" on "Calamity Fur Backpack"]
Stark’s inventory space was getting filled once more.
He was also fine in terms of fighting capabilities, so he didn’t feel the need to bless any other items.
Especially since he knew they could easily be replaced in the near future.
But on the other hand... the backpack would surely remain with him for a while!
Ding!
[You have blessed the "Calamity Fur Backpack"!]
Fwish!
Crimson aura began to surround the backpack, boosting its capabilities.
Stark could bless ANY type of item with the [Heart of Sanctuary], meaning that even the [Revenant Bell] could actually possibly be "blessed."
’I’ll have to try that next time.’
Still, he checked his new item.
---
[Calamity Fur Backpack (Legendary): +50 storage slots. Requirement: Level 25]
[Sanctuary Blessing: Doubles the space given by this backpack.]
---
Stark blinked.
A two-fold bonus meant the backpack now offered +100 slots.
’Perfect,’ he thought.
The next times he could use the [Heart of Sanctuary] again though, he’d try to use it on his special item.
Once the blessing settled in, he went right back to work.
Stark continued his genocide of the monsters until the second day ended.
The rest of the day slid by in a blur of motion.
Because of some weird effects of [Eternal Soul] and the current global event, AKA the [First Calamity], no one actually needed to sleep: they didn’t get tired.
The reason was unknow, but it was probably to make it "easier" to continuously fight.
Ding!
---
[You have gained 49 Evolution Points!]
[You have gained 3,729 Lives!]
---
He had significants gains once more, though even with all of that, none compared to the mythical-rank monster.
This went to show just how strong it was compared to all others.
Regardless, the sun went down, and then back up.
Ding!
---
[The final day of the "First Calamity" will now begin.]
[Over 80% of your civilization has died.]
[The rest of you have done well until this point, but the end is near.]
---
’Wait a damn minute.’
Stark couldn’t remember everything...
But in his previous life the figure had read was "over 85%" at this point.
This meant that for some strange reason, less people died.
’That’s... not normal.’
He wanted to wonder why, he couldn’t actually dwell on it too much.
He felt no vanity about it. This day would be the worst.
Epic-rank monsters would now appear.
This was the third and final batch of the [First Calamity], the most deadly one of all.
In his past life, this batch in addition to the presence of the [Lord of Calamity] caused the majority of deaths of those that survived till this point.
But now that he killed Andregil in his city... it was much safer!
Of course, bosses still roamed as they too spawned with the third batch, but it still could work out!
The dark vortex above swirled and roared as more monsters spawned.
---
[Calamity Rat (Level 25)]
[Rank: Epic]
[HP: 170,000]
---
[Calamity Bull (Level 25)]
[Rank: Epic]
[HP: 200,000]
---
Their HP varied, but all of them were epic-rank, with hundreds of monsters ready to attack.
Stark, just like before, wasn’t even concerned.
In fact, some of the monsters even seemed troubled as they looked at him, as if hesitating.
But right as Stark was about to engage with all of them...
Fwish... BOOM!
A pulse of power, subtle at first, stole through the world like a ripple.
It sent a shiver down the spine of all the players still alive.
"What the fuck was that?"
"Holy shit... more monsters?"
On the other hand, Stark’s eyes narrowed.
Even he seemed confused, after all, this had never happened either.
But as he looked around, he noticed something strange.
All the monsters around him was looking at the sky, as if hypnotized.
He tilted his head and looked up to do the same.
And... The sky itself opened.
’Holy shit.’
A monstrous crimson eye formed inside the vortex and fixed itself on the world.
The eye focused, and Stark felt a cold pressure against his nerves.
It felt like it was looking specifically at him.
Ding!
[You think you are clever, don’t you, Heir of Oblivion.]
[Let me show you what true calamity is, then.]
Ding!
[You have met the "God of Calamity"]
’Are you serious?’

chapters.title: Chapter 83: The God of Calamity, Calamity Buff, Extracting the Mount Bell
chapters.content:
Chapter 83: Chapter 83: The God of Calamity, Calamity Buff, Extracting the Mount Bell
Ding!
---
[???, God of Calamity (???)]
[Rank: ???]
[HP: ???]
[Description: ???]
[Skills: ???]
---
There was no information. Nothing.
The status panel was completely blank, as if the system itself refused to describe the being.
But Stark knew.
This was the [God of Calamity]. One of the gods of [Eternal Soul].
In his past life, he had never once seen a god.
He hadn’t even heard about anyone else meeting one.
No matter how far humanity advanced, no matter how strong people became.
Much like the other civilizations, the gods stayed out of reach.
For nine years, not a single trace of them ever appeared.
They were probably simply too "far" for them to reach, even though nine year passed.
And now, one was staring directly at his world.
The pressure it released was suffocating. Heavy.
Stark could feel it crushing down on the Earth itself.
It felt like it could destroy it with a single breath.
’It also called me [Heir of Oblivion].’ Stark’s eyes narrowed. ’Hm.’
Neris, the strange woman he had met in the [Abandoned Temple of Fate] and later in the [Church Sanctuary], had told him something.
She said the ancient gods weren’t watching yet.
That it was too early.
But this? This was clearly a god.
So what the hell was it? Did the gods notice him already?
Or was the [God of Calamity] not one of the "ancient gods" at all?
Perhaps there were [Gods] and [Ancient Gods].
And either way... how many gods actually existed in [Eternal Soul]?
The questions kept piling in his head, but none of them had answers. Not yet.
To find out, he would have to go further than in his past life.
Trigger events he hadn’t before. Reach places he never touched.
Only then would the truth come out.
[You shall face the wrath of Calamity, and so will your entire world.]
The voice was heavy, distorted, echoing inside every living being.
All the monsters in the world froze where they stood, gazes locked upward at the eye in the sky.
Their bodies shook as if hypnotized, unable to move.
And then—
Fwish! Boom! Boom!
A massive crimson pulse spread through the sky, washing over the entire world in an instant.
Every single monster was hit by it.
And as Stark braced himself against the shockwave.
[This bastard keeps trying to come back no matter what. We won’t allow it.]
Stark’s thoughts sharpened, ’The [God of Oblivion], I presume.’
The eye in the sky distorted violently, as if it was being torn apart by invisible chains.
Then, in a blink, it vanished completely.
The sky twisted, the crimson light faded, and the familiar dark vortex returned above the city.
All over the world, players and survivors had seen that eye.
Everyone had felt that oppressive gaze.
Fear spread like wildfire. But here, for now, it was gone.
At least, that’s what Stark thought.
Because as he lowered his gaze back to the streets, to the monsters that had spawned during the third batch...
’Hm.’
Something was different.
Their bodies were covered with pulsing crimson veins.
Their eyes glowed a deep, unnatural red.
He quickly pulled up their status panels again.
---
[Calamity Rat (Level 25)]
[Rank: Epic (Calamity Buff)]
[HP: 220,000]
---
[Calamity Bull (Level 25)]
[Rank: Epic (Calamity Buff)]
[HP: 250,000]
---
His expression hardened. The difference was obvious.
Their HP had jumped. Their strength was higher.
Their entire presence had changed.
’This isn’t normal.’
None of this had ever happened in his previous life.
The [God of Calamity] had spoken to him directly.
And now, the monsters were buffed because of it.
That much told him everything he needed to know.
The [God of Oblivion]... the being these gods feared and thus sealed.
If Stark was being called its [Heir], then it meant he was the last remnant of it.
That much was obvious.
And that also meant these gods were strong enough to interfere directly with events.
But they were still bound.
Stark caught it immediately.
The [God of Calamity] hadn’t killed him directly. It probably couldn’t.
It still needed to follow the rules of [Eternal Soul].
Perhaps because there were "higher beings" preventing it.
That’s why it chose to strengthen the monsters instead of striking him down.
Which meant only one thing: it underestimated him.
The [Calamity Rats], [Calamity Bulls], even a few [Calamity Snakes] slithering across the ruined streets, had no fear in their glowing red eyes.
They wanted to kill him. But Stark wasn’t worried.
If anything, that made things easier.
"Fine then."
Blazing Meteor! Storm of Lightning! Crystals of Death! Vines of Fate!
Boom! Crack! Fwoosh!
The street exploded in light and fire.
Spells slammed into the calamity-buffed monsters, tearing through dozens of them at once.
-288,360! -173,016! -45,000! -22,500! -22,500! -160,344!
The numbers flooded his vision.
The ground split open under the force.
Ding!
[You have gained 1 Evolution Point!]
[You have gained 98 Lives!]
Hand of Avarice!
[You have gained 104 Lives!]
"Good."
Even buffed, it didn’t matter.
His damage was overwhelming. They couldn’t keep up.
But he wasn’t stupid. He knew this wasn’t just about him.
Every monster in the world now carried this calamity buff.
That meant every other player, every other survivor, had to deal with stronger, faster, deadlier enemies.
He clenched his jaw.
The [God of Calamity] hadn’t targeted his city only, but the entire world.
That much was clear. But the destruction could still spread like wildfire.
Even [Ghost] and [Starfall] might have trouble surviving this.
Especially if a legendary-rank boss carried the buff.
If anyone weaker than him faced one of those things, they were finished.
He couldn’t waste time. He needed to clean up as fast as possible.
But before that, he had something else to do.
[Lives: 11,479]
His total had risen nicely thanks to killing Andregil and wiping out waves of monsters.
This was more than enough for what he needed.
He could finally extract his [Mount Bell (Ghost Wolf)] into the real world.
It cost 10,000 Lives. A heavy price, but worth it. Especially now.
The ghost wolf’s speed and agility would let him sweep through the city, crushing everything in his way.
Ding!
[Do you wish to use 10,000 Lives to extract your "Mount Bell (Ghost Wolf)" to the real world?]
"Yes."
He didn’t hesitate.
It was his most expensive purchase yet, but it was necessary.
Ding!
[You have consumed 10,000 Lives.]
[You have extracted your "Mount Bell (Ghost Wolf)" to the real world.]
The bell appeared in his hand, glowing faintly.
All around him, the sounds of fighting echoed through the streets.
Screams, roars, explosions.
The chaos was even worse than before.
’I need to move quickly.’
He raised the [Mount Bell] and shook it.
Fwoosh!
The [Ghost Wolf] appeared.
Its body shimmered, translucent silver fur gleaming under the broken sunlight.
Golden eyes locked onto him, calm and loyal.
It was pleased. It had been waiting for two days after all!
"Wolf," Stark’s voice was steady. "We’re circling the city. Every monster we see, we kill."
The wolf growled low in its throat, understanding instantly.
Stark climbed onto its back without hesitation.
In the next instant, it sprinted forward, paws barely touching the cracked ground as it raced through the streets.
’The ghost wolf won’t fight. Byt all it has to do is carry me while I do the rest.’
That was the plan.
But just as he prepared for his rampage—
Ding!
[Player "Starfall" has sent you a private message!]
[Starfall: Two legendary-rank bosses that are buffed like crazy surrounded us. Ghost is stubborn, but I don’t think she can handle them...!]
[Oblivion: Location?]
[Starfall: Near the giant tower. Please come quickly if you can! (⋟﹏⋞)]
Stark grinned. Perfect.
Not only could he save Ghost and Starfall, but he’d also get rid of two legendary-rank bosses at once.
"Let’s go."
The ghost wolf howled, then darted toward the giant tower like a silver blur.

chapters.title: Chapter 84: Calamity Minotaur and Calamity Sentinel, Ghost’s Class and Talent
chapters.content:
Chapter 84: Chapter 84: Calamity Minotaur and Calamity Sentinel, Ghost’s Class and Talent
Star Healing! Immunity Shield!
Grace stood at the rear, her staff glowing as she worked nonstop to keep Ghost alive.
She was a support-mage through and through.
Her bright magic wrapped around Ghost like a shield, soft light clashing against the crimson pressure flooding from the two monsters before them.
Ghost herself was already in motion, her twin daggers flashing as she darted between attacks, weaving through the deadly swings of two legendary-rank bosses.
"Even with that buff..." Ghost’s voice was low, sharp, her eyes narrowing behind her hood. "These monsters shouldn’t be this strong. That eye... it definitely had something to do with it."
Grace shivered at the mention of the giant eye.
Every player on Earth had seen it.
That colossal, crimson eye glaring down from the sky for a few seconds before vanishing.
For most, it was nothing more than a terrifying vision, but they had felt it.
The weight. The fear. The crushing force that made even the strongest tremble.
What they didn’t know was that Stark had seen more: panels, text, the truth behind that being.
Only he knew that the creature had been the [God of Calamity].
To everyone else, it was just horror.
And when that horror faded, the monsters changed.
Every single creature on Earth had been branded with a [Calamity Buff].
Ghost could still carve through most enemies if she pushed herself.
Her skills, her talent, and her hidden-class gave her more strength than nearly anyone else.
But legendary-rank bosses with that buff?
Even for her, this was pushing it.
Her daggers clashed against crimson armor, sparks flying, her body barely dodging the minotaur’s massive swings.
’Oblivion...’ Ghost thought, her instincts flaring.
Her [Assassin’s Intuition] never lied, and right now, it screamed at her.
’You had something to do with this.’
She didn’t know how. She didn’t know why.
But her gut told her Stark was connected to the eye, to the buff, to all of it.
There was no time to question him though.
Her focus locked back onto the two monsters towering over her.
---
[Calamity Minotaur (Level 25)]
[Rank: Legendary (Calamity Buff)]
[HP: 550,000]
---
[Calamity Sentinel (Level 25)]
[Rank: Legendary (Calamity Buff)]
[HP: 600,000]
---
’I need to hit their weaknesses,’ Ghost thought grimly, ’That’s the only way my passive will trigger.’
Her SS-Rank talent, [Eternal Ghost], was broken.
Her first passive worked against ANY type of being, whether it was a basic monster, boss or player.
Everyone who knew about it feared her for that reason alone.
But the catch with that was that he had to actually find and land a blow on those weaknesses.
Still, she had to try.
Slash! Slash!
Her daggers blurred as she went for the minotaur’s exposed head, the only part of its body not protected by armor.
The beast was a towering wall of muscle, two meters tall with a massive club that could smash houses to rubble.
Each swing carried enough force to crush her bones outright.
The [Calamity Sentinel] was no easier.
A tall knight clad in crimson armor, wielding a long sword with precision and discipline.
If the minotaur was brute force, the sentinel was sharp, refined killing intent.
They attacked in perfect rhythm, one striking while the other retreated, giving her no breathing room.
"S-Should I attack?" Grace asked hesitantly, her staff glowing faintly. "I have some offensive spells...!"
"No," Ghost’s reply was calm as she ducked under a club swing. "Just focus on helping me."
The ground split as the minotaur’s club smashed down where she had been standing.
Dust exploded outward.
Ghost blurred to the side, vanishing in a flicker of movement.
Fwish!
The sentinel’s blade slashed for her neck—
Bam!
It connected with a shimmering barrier instead.
Grace’s [Immunity Shield].
Ghost exhaled sharply, giving the girl a brief glance before vanishing again into motion.
Grace’s presence was the only reason she was still alive.
And it wasn’t just shields.
Because even when Ghost was harmed...
Star Healing!
Wounds closed across Ghost’s side where blood had been dripping moments ago, her body pulled back toward peak condition.
For a support-mage, Grace was beyond valuable.
Her [Star Prophet] class was one of the rarest support classes.
But what made her terrifying wasn’t her class. It was her talent.
[Goddess of Luck], An SS-Rank talent.
Her luck stat was absurdly high, tilted so far in her favor that chance itself bent for her.
Though she still hadn’t activated it for some reason.
She was wasted in Stark’s past life, never fully dedicating herself to the game, dying too early to matter.
But now? With Ghost as her partner, she was thriving.
The two made a solid team.
Strength Buff!
A golden aura flared around Ghost, and her movements sharpened.
She dashed toward the minotaur again, daggers flashing.
The beast swung its massive club, but she twisted past it, her figure blurring like smoke.
Ghost Slash!
Her daggers struck the minotaur square in the face.
-47,400! -47,400!
Blood sprayed, the beast reeling back.
But the instant-kill didn’t trigger.
"Tch, seriously?" Ghost hissed.
BAM!
The sentinel slammed its blade into her side, sending her crashing across the ground.
"M-My healing is still on cooldown, hold on!"
Ghost spat blood, her health dropping sharply.
Her vision blurred for a second, her body screaming in pain.
Her second passive threatened to trigger.
---
[Eternal Ghost (SS-Rank)]
[Description: The "Eternal Ghost" will never die, no matter how much they are struck. From the shadows, they will reduce all to nothing.]
[Passive #1: If you manage to hit an opponent’s weakness, there is a chance you will instantly kill them.]
[Passive #2: Upon receiving a mortal wound, the "Eternal Ghost" will endure it and be strengthened, fighting back from the brink of death.]
---
She had never triggered that second passive before.
When she died to [SoulsGod] in her past life, it hadn’t activated because she had been stunned.
But now... now it felt like it was close.
Roooarr!
The minotaur bellowed, rushing forward, not toward her, but toward Grace.
"Hah?!" Grace froze, eyes wide.
’Shit,’ Ghost thought, her heart pounding, ’Not fast enough—!’
The club lifted high, aimed directly at Grace’s head.
Grace shut her eyes, bracing for death and the loss of 100 Lives.
But before the strike could land—
Piercing Bone Spikes!
Fwish! Bam! Bam! Bam!
Fifteen skeletal spikes erupted from the ground, impaling the minotaur’s chest, arms, and legs.
Each spike tore through flesh and bone.
-36,000! -36,000! -36,000!
In an instant, 540,000 damage ripped through the beast.
Its health bar emptied, the creature collapsing with a thunderous crash.
Its club fell to the ground, shattering the earth.
Grace gasped, spinning around.
She didn’t need to see him. She already knew who it was.
Oblivion was here.
Thump!
Stark landed lightly from his [Ghost Wolf], staff in hand, his expression calm and unshaken.
The wolf’s translucent form stood behind him, golden eyes gleaming.
"Sorry for being late." His gaze flicked to the [Calamity Sentinel], then to Ghost. "Let’s deal with the other one."
Ghost blinked at the sheer destruction his spell had caused, surprise flickering in her eyes before she masked it.
She gave a curt nod, daggers tightening in her grip.
The sentinel didn’t hesitate.
Fueled by the buff, it charged directly at Stark, sword blazing crimson.
"Hit it from behind," Stark said calmly, "It’ll be dealt quickly after that."
Ghost froze for half a second. Her eyes narrowed.
’Wait. Does he know about my class’s passive?’
Her class, [Vengeful Assassin], was a hidden-class.
Almost nobody knew its abilities.
One of its passives was that if she struck an enemy outside their line of sight, she dealt ten times her normal damage.
And Stark... had just told her exactly how to use it.
Or perhaps he just said that out of nowhere?
She didn’t have time to question him.
She blurred into [Ghost Invisibility], vanishing from sight.
Normally, she didn’t risk using it against bosses, if she dropped aggro, enemies would immediately target Starfall.
She wouldn’t let Grace die like that.
But with Oblivion here, holding aggro? She could.
The sentinel’s sword carved downward toward Stark.
Grace lifted her staff, "Immunity Shield—!"
But Stark didn’t even need it.
Storm of Lightning!
Lightning exploded around the sentinel, forcing its body to seize up, stunned for a fraction of a second.
-173,016!
And in that frozen instant—
Ghost reappeared behind it.
Ghost Slash!
-237,000! -237,000!
Her blades tore through the back of its armor, her hidden-class passive amplifying her damage tenfold.
The sentinel staggered, its health bar plunging.
It tried to recover, but it was already too late.
Its HP hit zero, its armored form collapsing to the ground with a metallic crash.
Ding!
The fight was over. Two legendary-rank bosses lay dead.
Grace’s eyes lit up, relief flooding her face.
"We... we did it!"
Ghost, however, didn’t relax.
Her eyes stayed locked on Stark, sharp and suspicious.
’He knew about my passive,’ she thought, ’I never told anyone except for Starfall, and she didn’t tell him about it.’
She couldn’t figure it out.

chapters.title: Chapter 85: End of the First Calamity, At Least He Tried!
chapters.content:
Chapter 85: Chapter 85: End of the First Calamity, At Least He Tried!
Stark took the items from the [Calamity Minotaur], while the loot from the [Calamity Sentinel] was handed to Ghost and Starfall.
It was only fair.
Ghost had done most of the work in that fight, and Stark wasn’t about to pretend otherwise.
The majority of the damage had come from her. That made the gear hers.
Still, even if the equipment went to her, Stark wasn’t left empty-handed.
He had gained something much more valuable.
Ding!
[You have gained 8 Evolution Points!]
[You have gained 102 Lives!]
The spectral hand appeared out of his staff, clawing at the fallen corpses.
Hand of Avarice!
Grace took an instinctive step back.
"What the hell is that thing?" she asked, her eyes narrowing at the ghostly hand rummaging through the boss remains.
"Just something I use," Stark replied casually.
Ding!
[You have gained 7 Evolution Points!]
[You have gained 94 Lives!]
"Good," Stark muttered, scanning the notifications.
[Current Evolution Points: 175.]
That number made his pulse quicken.
His evolution points had never been this high before.
With that amount, he could soon push two of his mythical-rank skills up to ancient rank.
The power spike would be massive.
Unfortunately, [Blazing Meteor] was still out of reach.
That skill required 250 EP, and even after grinding this hard, Stark wasn’t close.
If anything, the sheer gap told him exactly what he’d need to do in the future: hunt down more bosses, and stronger ones.
Normal monsters weren’t going to cut it anymore.
The truth was simple: powerful bosses like Andregil gave the highest EP.
If Stark wanted to keep climbing, he’d have to take more risks and face more of those kinds of enemies head-on.
But that was a problem for later.
For now, 175 EP was a good place to be.
"Alright," Stark said, swinging up onto the ghost wolf’s back.
Its spectral form shifted slightly under him, but it carried his weight without issue.
"Stay safe."
He was preparing to ride off when he suddenly froze.
"Oh, right."
Stark opened his inventory and pulled out the [Church Devout Staff (Epic)] he had taken from the [Church Sanctuary].
---
[Church Devout Staff (Epic): Mage-type weapon. +278 Spirits, +27 Agility. Requirement: Level 25]
[Light Orb (Active Skill): Launches a light orb that explodes on impact, dealing 30,000 damage. 20-second cooldown.]
---
It was a solid weapon.
A proper mage-type staff, and far stronger than anything Grace was carrying now.
He tossed it to her.
Grace caught it, eyes widening. "Thanks! My [Goddess of Luck] talent still doesn’t seem to be working though... I didn’t fulfill the conditions yet."
Stark simply nodded.
He knew Grace’s talent was [Goddess of Luck], but the exact mechanics behind it were a mystery to him.
Still, he could already imagine how broken it would be if she ever managed to fully activate it.
If she could max out her luck stat, then every drop, every reward, every outcome would bend in her favor.
It wouldn’t just mean getting the best loot from every monster, t would mean changing the very odds of survival.
And if she could extend that luck to her allies, even just slightly, it would be game-breaking.
Pair that with Ghost’s ability to mow down enemies in bursts, and the two of them together would be unstoppable.
For Stark, the EP from the two bosses was more than enough.
But Grace still sent a little something his way.
Ding!
[You have received 50 Lives from Starfall.]
He accepted it without hesitation, then urged the ghost wolf forward.
The mount’s form blurred as it rushed through the broken streets.
Even after two legendary bosses were down, the city was still crawling with monsters.
Stark’s eyes narrowed.
’Alright, [God of Calamity]. Let’s see who’s stronger, me, or your pets.’
Behind him, Ghost glanced at Grace.
"Do you think he has anything to do with those buffed monsters?" she asked. "Oblivion is so... weird."
"I don’t think so," Grace said after a pause, shrugging, "And even if he was involved, wasn’t it that giant eye that powered them up? Otherwise, why would he be fighting so hard to wipe them out?"
Ghost stared at her for a long second, then exhaled softly.
"...Fair enough."
Grace nodded to herself. "I’ll try to get a skill that lets me distract monsters. If I can pull their attention, you’ll be able to strike from behind."
Ghost blinked at that. It was... actually a good idea.
Her damage from behind was multiplied tenfold.
If Grace could safely draw aggro without putting herself in danger, Ghost could shred nearly any monster at this stage.
"Not bad," Ghost admitted.
A faint smile crossed her lips.
"Let’s just focus on surviving for now."
...
Meanwhile...
Ding!
[You have died.]
Max let out a furious roar.
"What the fuck are we supposed to do? None of this makes sense!"
Seren’s face was pale.
"The monsters suddenly became so much stronger after that giant eye appeared..."
"We can handle the regular ones," Max muttered, teeth clenched, "But the bosses? Forget it. We should run the second we see one."
"Agreed." Seren’s voice was barely above a whisper.
They weren’t alone in that thought.
Across the entire world, players had started avoiding bosses entirely.
They had enough lives stocked up to absorb a few deaths, but the risk of fighting these new, powered-up bosses was too high.
The entire situation had shifted in an instant.
And it was so much worse than what Stark remembered from his past life.
"Ahhh! Get away from me!"
"Shit, this is impossible!"
Slash!
Screams echoed across ruined streets as players fell one after another.
Some lost their final lives, disappearing permanently.
Max’s expression twisted as he watched.
"We can’t risk it. We have more than enough lives to die a dozen times, but... I don’t want to gamble it all away."
"Yeah..." Seren’s voice trembled, "We don’t even have all our abilities yet. We should just be careful."
At this point, they both knew the truth: their world was done.
The only option left was to survive long enough for the [Final Calamity] to end, so they could return to [Eternal Soul].
...
The last day of the [Final Calamity] bled away like that.
Stark never slowed down. Not once.
Every step, every second, his eyes were sharp, catching the faintest flickers of movement.
He didn’t even need detection skills, his instincts were honed to a razor’s edge.
Whenever he saw something, he struck immediately.
Spells flew like lightning, annihilating anything in his path.
Even bosses fell before he could take a breath.
The ghost wolf’s mobility only made it easier.
Hours passed.
And then, suddenly...
"Huh."
Stark frowned. For the first time, he couldn’t find any monsters.
He rode down one empty street, then another. Minutes passed. Nothing.
"Well."
He had killed too many. Hundreds, maybe more.
It wasn’t surprising that the area had gone quiet.
Fifteen minutes later, he finally came across a single [Calamity Snake] harassing a group of players.
It died in seconds.
The city was far too large for him to wipe out every single monster.
But at this point, Stark had personally slaughtered an enormous portion of them.
And so eventually...
Ding!
A global announcement echoed across the minds of every survivor.
[The "First Calamity" is now over.]
"Yes!"
"Oh my god, finally..."
"Shit... we lost too many."
[Over 98% of your civilization has died.]
[Congratulations, you somehow managed to have the biggest amount of casualties among all civilizations!]
Stark stared at the panel, expression neutral.
He had fought tooth and nail, tried to carve open paths of survival.
But in the end, more people had died than in his past life.
The death rate had jumped from 95% to 98%.
And that last announcement? About being the civilization with the most casualties?
That had never appeared before.
’Oh well,’ Stark thought, letting out a quiet sigh, ’It is what it is.’
He had done what he could.
No one could have predicted that a god would interfere and buff the monsters.
At least he tried.

chapters.title: Chapter 86: Back to Eternal Soul, SSS-Rating
chapters.content:
Chapter 86: Chapter 86: Back to Eternal Soul, SSS-Rating
The moment the [First Calamity] ended, the dark vortex above the world finally vanished.
The sky cleared.
What replaced the swirling void was a magnificent, cloudless blue.
For just a second, if someone looked up, they might have believed everything was fine.
That this was just a normal day.
That nothing had happened.
But that illusion didn’t last long.
The truth was impossible to ignore.
Entire cities lay in ruins. Buildings flattened. Streets torn apart.
The scars of destruction stretched across every horizon.
The sky might have healed, but the world had not.
’From 95% to 98%... because of the monsters’ [Calamity Buff],’ Stark thought, standing still amidst the wreckage.
His expression remained calm, unreadable.
He didn’t dwell on guilt more than necessary.
He had fought with everything he had, and his intentions had been good.
But the [God of Calamity] had interfered, twisting everything.
Even someone like him could only do so much.
He had managed to thin out the monsters in this city.
A few other top players across the globe had done the same.
But for the majority of people? They stood no chance from the start. As expected.
Still, despite the devastation, Stark hadn’t walked away empty-handed after killing those monsters.
Ding!
[You have gained 103 Evolution Points!]
[You have gained 6,380 Lives!]
His eyes flickered across the panels.
The rewards were staggering, far beyond what he had gained before.
But considering the sheer number of buffed monsters he had slain, it was only natural.
’Not bad,’ Stark thought.
The system added one more line of information.
Do note that the gained evolution points include the 5 he gets daily from his talent.
[Current Evolution Points: 278.]
[Lives: 8,105.]
’God damn.’
That was more EP than he had ever seen gathered at once.
His mind instantly began calculating options.
With that many points, several of his skills could evolve right now.
In fact, if he wanted, he could push [Blazing Meteor] from ancient-rank to ascendant-rank immediately.
The thought alone sent a thrill through him.
The destructive potential would skyrocket. But Stark paused.
The higher he went, the more expensive it would become.
His skills were entering the "upper" ranks now, and those weren’t something to throw points at carelessly.
That was the path. And each step up demanded more than the last.
He was still considering his options when the system interrupted him.
Ding! Ding! Ding!
[Congratulations to all of those who survived the "First Calamity."]
[You may now go ahead and explore "Eternal Soul" and whatever awaits you beyond.]
And that was it. Nothing more.
The announcement was simple, but the effect was immediate.
"I’m out of here!"
"Fuck this, I’m not staying on Earth another second!"
"Wait, don’t forget about the [Tired] mechanic. You’ll get forced back eventually."
"Damn it, who cares, I’m still going!"
One after another, the survivors began vanishing.
Almost all of them chose to return to [Eternal Soul].
After what they had just endured, no one wanted to remain on Earth any longer than necessary.
The [Global Event] was over. They had survived.
That meant they could finally go back to the game, leaving behind the chaos and despair of their ruined world.
Humanity had been reduced to scraps.
With over 98% of the population dead, most survivors already believed Earth itself was finished.
Luckily, there was one small mercy.
The monsters that had remained after the [First Calamity] vanished the moment the event ended.
For now, Earth was safe again. Or, at least, empty.
Ding!
[Player "Ghost" has sent you a private message!]
[Ghost: We will be going ahead into "Eternal Soul." We want to check out our advancement task and the rest.]
[Oblivion: Alright.]
Stark closed the panel without hesitation. He had the same plan.
Now that the [First Calamity] was finished, every player’s advancement task had been completed.
The weak had been eliminated.
Almost nobody below level 20 or 25 had survived.
The few who did had either been carried or had absurd luck.
But for the rest, the ones who endured, completing their advancement task was guaranteed.
Ding!
[Enter "Eternal Soul" to check out all the panels related to yourself.]
Stark glanced at the prompt.
He couldn’t check his rewards here. Not yet. That was fine.
He had hoped to obtain a new mage skill book from the [First Calamity], but nothing had dropped.
A small disappointment, though not crippling.
His damage was already high enough to kill the strongest level 25 monsters.
Stark thought it was perhaps it was time to diversify his skills.
For exemple, a way to heal himself would be good.
Mages were one of the most versatile classes.
They could summon, heal, and wield destructive magic.
But versatility came at a cost.
To most, it was still considered one of the weaker classes.
Not only because of the mana usage, but also cooldowns.
’I’ll reach 300 EP first,’ Stark thought, gaze steady. ’Then I’ll evolve three skills at once.’
He stood in the ruined plaza, gazing around at what was left of his city.
Buildings burned. Smoke drifted. Ash hung in the air.
He let out a quiet sigh.
’The other civilizations and the ancient gods...’ His eyes narrowed. ’Hm.’
He closed his eyes and focused on the game.
Then a new panel shimmered into view.
Ding!
[Do you wish to enter "Eternal Soul"?]
[Yes] [No]
"Yes."
Fwish!
His body broke apart into glowing particles, dissolving into the system’s pull.
During the calamity, it had been impossible to leave.
But now, freedom returned.
And so, Stark disappeared.
...
Fwish!
The particles reformed inside the cathedral of [Shell City].
He blinked once, adjusting to the sudden shift.
The air here felt clean. Untouched.
A panel appeared instantly.
[Olikar, Quest NPC (Dead).]
"..."
Stark dismissed it.
He already knew Olikar’s fate, and he had nothing more to say about it.
If anything, he was glad he had visited this place before the [First Calamity].
It was quiet. Isolated. Nobody else would come here yet.
’Perfect,’ Stark thought.
Privacy was exactly what he needed to check his panels.
But just as he took his first step—
Ding! Ding! Ding!
Panels flooded his vision.
He already knew what they were.
---
[You have completed your Tier-2 Advancement Task: "Survive the First Calamity."]
[Rating: SSS]
---
’Damn.’
His lips curled slightly.
He had never gotten an SSS rating before.
In his past life, almost nobody had.
Not even Ghost or EvilDemon, who had both been monsters in their own right.
To get an SSS rating would mean that you had absolutely dominated the [Advancement Task].
And Stark had done exactly that!
Ding!
[Your level has been unlocked. You may now gain experience points.]
’Finally.’
The restriction lifted. He could start leveling again.
Of course, it wasn’t infinite.
The system would only unlock progression until the next advancement task, which was at level 50.
After that, another trial awaited.
For most players, the pace would slow dramatically here.
The experience required was enormous.
But Stark didn’t care.
He had no intention of matching others’ pace.
He intended to leave everyone else behind.
[Level: 25 (0/200,000)]
’Good.’
And then, the real prize.
The second reward of completing an advancement task: [Class Advancement].
Ding!
[You have fulfilled the condition for your "Class Advancement."]
Nobody could evolve their [Talents] yet. That would come later.
But this was the moment his [Mage of Oblivion] class could ascend to its next tier.
Stark grinned. His pulse quickened.
"Here we go."
Ding!
[Your "Mage of Oblivion" class has evolved!]
[Tier: 1 → 2]

chapters.title: Chapter 87: Tier-2 Mage of Oblivion, Increased Firepower!
chapters.content:
Chapter 87: Chapter 87: Tier-2 Mage of Oblivion, Increased Firepower!
[Mage of Oblivion (Unique Hidden Class)]
[Tier: 1 → 2]
[Class Passive #1: All your magic damage is multiplied by 15 → 20.]
[Class Passive #2: Your MP recovery is multiplied by 15 → 20.]
[Class Passive #3: All your spells’ cooldowns are reduced by half.]
---
’Perfect.’
It didn’t look like much.
In fact, compared to some other classes, it might even seem bland.
But to Stark, this was more than enough.
His damage multiplier increased again and his mana recovery grew even stronger as he would need it in the future.
He didn’t gain a new passive just yet, that would come further down the line, but that didn’t matter.
His strength had risen tremendously from this one tier increase.
Every spell he had would now hit harder.
With that, Stark was done checking everything.
He had survived the [First Calamity], completed his [Advancement Task], and evolved his class to Tier 2.
Now there was only one goal left. Kill monsters.
He would grind until he hit level 30, because that would allow him to finally step into the [Demonic Ruins] and complete Olikar’s quest.
Afterward, at level 40, he would be able to enter the [Land of Mist].
That place... it would be the most dangerous global zone so far.
Even more dangerous than the [First Calamity].
But Stark wanted it.
He wanted to reach the [Land of Mist] because that was when he could finally unlock his first bloodline.
Bloodlines were special.
They could physically enhance someone, grant new skills, unlock abilities, and push a player far beyond normal limits.
Weak players became strong. Strong players became monsters.
And the bloodline Stark was aiming for was one of the strongest early-game bloodlines in existence: the [Spirit Devourer].
Of course, it wasn’t free.
To get it, he would need to kill the strongest monster in the [Land of Mist].
The problem was, Stark didn’t know the exact method to reach it yet.
’Hm.’
He pushed that thought aside for now.
There would be time to figure it out.
Stark turned around after glancing one last time at the spot where Olikar’s body had been.
’I guess I’ll complete your quest now.’
Stark wished Olikar could have told him more about the other civilizations, but it was fine.
He pushed open the cathedral doors and stepped back into the main square of [Shell City].
The difference was clear. The number of players had dropped heavily.
Much less than even in his past life.
A ninety-eight percent death rate. Humanity had been butchered.
Even many of the level 25 players who made it to this point had died in the calamity, unable to survive its chaos.
And it was mainly because of the [Calamity Buff].
Still... Stark didn’t care.
As long as he could keep moving forward, it didn’t matter.
’I wonder if the other gods will intervene again at some point.’
That was his only worry now.
He didn’t know if they could actually do something directly to kill him, but the possibility was always there.1
He stepped further into the square.
"This was insane..."
"Oh well, the world was overpopulated anyway."
"What the fuck are you talking about? This entire thing was a calamity!"
"Nice pun."
Other players nearby spoke about what they had seen and their experiences.
Of course, none of them could compare to Stark.
Then the whispers began.
"Oh, look. It’s Oblivion."
"Really?!"
"It is, holy shit!"
To most players, the strongest survivors were like gods at this point.
They were the ones who stood firm when everything else crumbled.
The ones who endured what others couldn’t.
Stark ignored them. He didn’t care about fame.
As long as his reputation was solid, he was satisfied.
He grabbed himself a small meal before leaving [Shell City].
Then he shook the [Mount Bell (Ghost Wolf)], summoning the mount once again.
The wolf appeared, tilting its head.
Stark tossed it another piece of meat.
The wolf ate it happily.
’No increase in loyalty,’ Stark noted, ’Oh well.’
He climbed onto the ghost wolf’s back and gave the order.
"We’ll head to the level 25–30 area. I need to reach level 30 as fast as possible."
The wolf howled and charged forward at full speed.
Stark remembered several zones that matched his target level range.
If he cleared them all, his level would rise quickly.
He also needed to sell equipment eventually, but not now.
Most players didn’t have enough [Lives] to afford his gear.
Too many had died too many times during the calamity.
If it hadn’t been for the [Calamity Buff], Stark might have done it.
He opened his inventory.
[Inventory: 128/152]
He still had space. The equipment could wait.
The [Lives] he would gain later were far more valuable for the future.
So he pressed forward.
After a few minutes, the land shifted.
A massive pit opened before him, the entrance to the [Demonic Ruins].
A glowing barrier blocked the way.
Ding!
[You cannot enter the level 30–40 zone "Demonic Ruins" as you do not have the required level.]
’Wasn’t planning to anyway.’
He smiled faintly. Soon, though.
Soon he would be able to walk into that place.
It felt good to finally push forward.
He had been stuck at level 25 for too long.
Now, with [Tier 2] secured, he could grow again.
Other level 25 players who survived the [First Calamity] must have also completed their advancement tasks.
That meant Ghost and Grace had too.
Sometimes a class that evolved further would receive a new passive.
At the beginning, meaning [Tier 0], most classes only had one passive.
The stronger ones gained two.
For example, Ghost and Grace both had two passives.1
But Stark... he had three!
And he would surely unlock even more as his class evolved.
For now, he was satisfied.
A few minutes later, he encountered the first monsters.
"Oh, it’s some of those things again."
Ahead, a group of [Ground Spiders] crawled across the terrain, ripping apart another monster and feasting on it.
---
[Ground Spider (Level 26)]
[Rank: Rare]
[HP: 350,000]
---
They had abnormally high HP for their level, but Stark didn’t care.
He had killed one before. He would kill them again.
Among them, a larger spider moved forward, armored and more menacing.
---
[General Ground Spider (Level 27)]
[Rank: Epic (Boss)]
[HP: 500,000]
---
The group noticed Stark and rushed forward, their long dark legs tearing into the dirt.
The [General Ground Spider] hissed.
A crimson glow erupted around it, buffing its allies. A terrifying sight to most.
To normal players, death would be certain.
But Stark only grinned.
’I already know all about you.’
He remembered his fight before.
[Ground Spiders] were immune to lightning.
And their exoskeletons were thick, able to block most attacks.
Unless the head was struck directly, or unless the attack was too powerful.
And in this case...
Blazing Meteor! Piercing Bone Spikes!
Fwish!
-384,480! -384,480! -384,480!1
Stark’s [Blazing Meteor] exploded across the area, fire tearing through everything.
The spiders shrieked, burning instantly.
All of them died in one strike. All but the [General Ground Spider].
It rushed forward, crimson glow burning.
Fwish! Fwish!
The ground erupted.
Bone spikes shot up in an instant, piercing into its armored body, driving through its head.
-48,000! -48,000! -48,000!1
The spider screeched once, then collapsed.
Its HP hit zero. It was dead.
’Looks like I’ll manage just fine.’
Stark smirked to himself.

chapters.title: Chapter 88: More Experience Needed, Ancient-Rank Hand of Avarice!
chapters.content:
Chapter 88: Chapter 88: More Experience Needed, Ancient-Rank Hand of Avarice!
Ding!
[You have killed x7 "Ground Spiders (Level 26)"]
[You have killed "General Ground Spider (Level 27 Elite-Rank Boss)"]
[You have gained 64,000 experience points.]
[You have gained 7 Evolution Points!]
[You have gained 148 Lives!]
---
"Good."
Stark currently needed 200,000 experience points to level up.
The next advancement task and level lock would come at level 50, the next major milestone.
Of course, reaching it would take time.
For other players, it would take even longer, but even for him, it wouldn’t be easy.
Leveling up was only going to get harder.
Still, Stark didn’t mind.
As long as he could keep killing strong monsters and taking risks, he would keep rising.
That much was certain.
At his current level, 25, he required 200,000 experience points to move forward.
Every level afterward, the requirement increased by 20,000.
That meant by level 50, he would need 700,000 experience points for a single level!
And because of the [Experience Decay], it is understandable why it would take longer.
Even for him, that was going to take some time.
Especially since experience reset back to zero every single level.
But of course, thanks to his high damage, he knew killing hundreds of monsters woul be easy.
’Oh well.’
Hand of Avarice!
Ding!
---
[You have gained 6 Evolution Points!]
[You have gained 7 Evolution Points!]
[You have gained 151 Lives!]
[You have gained 72 Lives!]
---
"Nice."
Two of the [Ground Spiders] dropped [Spider Exoskeleton (Rare)] armor.
Stark stored them into his inventory and kept moving forward.
’I already know why there are so many spiders nearby.’
When several monsters of the same type gathered in one place, it usually meant there was a zone tied to them close by.
Of course, most people would take one look at that kind of zone and say, "hell no."
They would avoid it altogether.
Seren, in Stark’s past life, had been terrified of spiders.
Because of that, their party had skipped that zone entirely.
But now? Stark was alone.
He wasn’t afraid of spiders either. So why wouldn’t he go?
He continued onward, hunting more [Ground Spiders] as he rode atop the [Ghost Wolf].
Every kill was clean, his spells crushing them easily.
At one point, he encountered another boss: a [Ground Mole (Rare-Rank Boss)].
It didn’t survive for long.
Ding!
---
[You have gained 46,000 Experience Points!]
[You have gained 9 Evolution Points!]
[You have gained 194 Lives!]
---
And eventually, Stark found what he was looking for.
A cave entrance. Its walls and ground were covered in thick spider silk.
Ding!
[You are about to enter a dangerous level 26–28 zone: "Spider Silk Nest"]
[Once you enter, you cannot leave unless you die.]
’Good.’
In his previous life, Seren had stopped them from going further at this exact point.
Stark had contested the decision, but Max and Seren both refused, and the party turned back.
This time, things were different.
This time, Stark wouldn’t lose this chance.
Even if the place was dangerous, it was worth it.
In fact, it was perfect.
A zone like this was one of the best ways to raise his level.
His top priority now was reaching level 30 as fast as possible.
The [Demonic Ruins] were the best grinding ground between [Shell City] and the [Land of Mist].
But before going inside... Stark had something else to do.
[Current Evolution Points: 307.]
His EP had steadily increased through all his hunting.
Now, he had more than 300, enough to evolve three skills.
He was confident he could clear the spider nest even without evolving them, but this was the perfect chance to test out his new abilities.
Ding!
[Do you wish to consume 100 Evolution Points to evolve "Hand of Avarice"?]
"Yes."
Ding!
[You have evolved "Hand of Avarice" (Mythical) to "Hand of Avarice" (Ancient)]
[Current Evolution Points: 207.]
Stark’s eyes lit up.
He had been waiting for this. He quickly opened the new description.
---
[Hand of Avarice (Ancient): Can be used on corpses, has a 125% → 150% chance to obtain another loot reward. In addition, if the loot is an item, there is a 30% → 50% chance to increase the rank by one.]
---
’Damn!’
This was huge.
The chance of obtaining extra loot increased by twenty-five percent, which meant it would trigger even more often.
On top of that, the chance to increase an item’s rank had almost doubled.
Fifty percent. One out of every two items had a chance to upgrade.
If he looted an item now, there was a fifty–fifty shot it would become stronger than before.
And in the future... if this skill continued evolving... maybe that chance would reach one hundred percent.
Just the thought made Stark grin.
But he didn’t waste time. He had two more skill evolutions to go through.
[Do you wish to consume 100 Evolution Points to evolve "Invincible Magic Barrier"?]
"Yes."
Ding!
[You have evolved "Invincible Magic Barrier" (Mythical) to "Unbreakable Magic Barrier" (Ancient)]
He immediately selected the other skill.
[Do you wish to consume 100 Evolution Points to evolve "Piercing Bone Spikes"?]
There were two reasons he chose it over [Storm of Lightning] or [Vines of Fate].
The first was simple: [Piercing Bone Spikes] did more damage.
It was focused damage, yes, and he needed to be accurate, but it was far more effective against single targets.
The second reason was even more practical.
His lightning and vine skills didn’t work well against spiders.
Their resistances and natural defenses reduced their effectiveness.
But the bone spikes could effectively harm them.
"Yes."
Ding!
[You have evolved "Piercing Bone Spikes" (Mythical) to "Piercing Skeletal Spikes" (Ancient)]
[Current Evolution Points: 7.]
He had spent everything.
It would take a long time to save enough EP for more evolutions, but that was fine.
It took 250 EP to evolve an ancient-rank skill after all.
’Perfect.’
Now it was time to check the details.
---
[Unbreakable Magic Barrier (Ancient): Summon a barrier around the user that can endure many attacks. It has 40,000 HP → 100,000 HP. 30 (15)-seconds cooldown.]
---
[Piercing Skeletal Spikes (Ancient): Summon 15 skeletal spikes from the ground to pierce an opponent. Each spike deals 2,000 → 3,000 damage and has a chance to cause "bleeding". 20 (10)-seconds cooldown.]
---
’Holy shit.’
The difference was massive.
First, the [Unbreakable Magic Barrier].
Its HP had jumped to one-hundred thousand. That was terrifying.
A monster like Andregil might be able to break it in a few hits, but for smaller enemies? No chance.
They would need to swarm him in numbers just to stand a chance at breaking through.
Then came [Piercing Skeletal Spikes].
This was the strongest deal-damage skill in his arsenal now.
If every spike landed, the total damage would exceed one million.
Of course, Stark knew that realistically, only about one-third of the spikes would land.
But even so, the numbers were absurd.
And if he caught an enemy off guard, like he had with the [Church Assassin] or the [Calamity Minotaur], the result would be an instant kill.
’Perfect.’
The cooldowns hadn’t gone down, but they hadn’t gone up either.
That was good enough.
Stark clenched his fists, excitement running through him.
His power had jumped again.
And with that done, he turned his focus back to the cave entrance.
He stepped inside without waiting.
Ding!
[You have entered the "Spider Silk Nest"]
[Lives loss rate: 500]

chapters.title: Chapter 89: Spider Silk Nest, Spider Queen
chapters.content:
Chapter 89: Chapter 89: Spider Silk Nest, Spider Queen
The lives loss rate of the [Spider Silk Nest] was high, especially for such a zone.
Five hundred lives drained if you died.
For any normal player, that alone was enough to turn them away.
But Stark? He didn’t even flinch.
He had already gone through the [Church Sanctuary], a zone where the lives loss rate was double this.
Compared to that nightmare, this was nothing more than a warm-up.
He stood in the first chamber of the cave, the zone’s entry point.
The space was small, circular, and covered in thick, gleaming strands of silk.
They stuck to the walls like veins, hanging loosely from the ceiling, spreading across the ground in tangled webs.
The air itself smelled faintly of mold and something rotten.
No spiders appeared yet, but he could hear faint rattling in the distance, like claws tapping against stone.
He gripped his staff tighter.
He was ready to unleash an attack the second something came crawling out of the dark.
Unbreakable Magic Barrier!
He also cast his barrier on himself.
The translucent dome appeared around him, humming with power.
Stark wasn’t about to get caught off guard in a place like this.
Even if he was ambushed, the barrier would buy him time.
This zone wasn’t supposed to be massive. Mid-sized at most.
But even then, mid-sized didn’t mean safe.
He exhaled slowly, then walked forward.
Out of the initial chamber and into the unknown.
The next room stretched out before him: massive, sprawling, and webbed with tunnels on every side.
The ceilings were high, the floor covered in silk like carpet.
"Oh, shit..." Stark muttered under his breath. "This might be bigger than I thought."
This was a pretty big nest.
And since it was the spiders’ nest, that meant one thing, he was standing in the very heart of where they lived.
Summoning the ghost wolf here would only cause problems.
Tight spaces, silk everywhere, the beast would just thrash and get stuck.
Worse, it would panic.
Stark didn’t need that. So he went alone.
He picked one of the tunnels leading deeper into the nest.
But the moment he stepped inside, he heard a hiss.
Eight legs scraped against stone. Shadows shifted ahead.
And het met face to face with several spiders.
There was the usual [Ground Spiders], but also two other types.
---
[Miner Spider (Level 27)]
[Rank: Elite]
[HP: 360,000]
---
[Small Spider (Level 26)]
[Rank: Uncommon]
[HP: 100,000]
---
The [Miner Spider] stood out immediately.
Pickaxes were fused to its legs, the jagged iron heads glinting in the light.
The smaller spiders, though weaker, crawled in groups, skittering fast along the silk.
The [Ground Spiders] hissed the loudest, leading the charge.
The whole swarm rushed him.
Blazing Meteor!
The tunnel lit up.
-384,480! -384,480! -384,480!
The explosion was deafening.
Flames ripped through the passage, burning silk, stone, and flesh alike.
When the smoke cleared, nothing was left but ash and twitching, charred legs.
Every single spider was dead.
Do note that when outside, [Blazing Meteor] would result in a meteor came crashing down from the sky.
But inside zones like this?
The meteor simply blasted out of Stark’s staff like a projectile, smashing into enemies with devastating force.
Ding!
---
[You have killed x4 "Ground Spider (Level 26)"]
[You have killed x2 "Miner Spider (Level 27)"]
[You have killed x12 "Small Spider (Level 25)"]
[You have gained 30,000 Experience Points.]
[You have gained 124 Lives!]
---
Hand of Avarice!
The spectral hand clawed at the spiders’ corpses, and indeed, the loot he got was higher!
[You have gained 158 Lives!]
One of the items even upgraded automatically.
[Miner Spider Pickaxe (Epic): Can be used to mine or attack, though extremely weak.]
Not much of a weapon. More like a tool.
But Stark stored it away anyway.
You never knew what might come in handy later.
"Not bad."
He continued forward, deeper into the nest.
Every fight gave him what he wanted: lives and experience.
People often underestimated them, but Stark would need as many as he could get.
After all, extracting your abilities to the real world was indeed useful, but only during some of the [Global Events].
In most other cases, you would spend your time inside of [Eternal Soul].
And the reason why Stark wanted lives so much even after the [First Calamity] was over was because they would be needed in the future.
For example, in the very next town, and further in [Eternal Soul], having lives would be crucial.
He wasn’t going to be caught unprepared.
The tunnels twisted and stretched endlessly.
He fought group after group of spiders.
[Ground Spiders], [Small Spiders], [Miner Spiders].
All fell before him.
His spells burned through their lines like paper.
An hour passed.
And then... silence.
’They’re either hiding... or there aren’t any left.’
Stark doubted the latter.
Monsters weren’t completely mindless. He knew that extremely well.
Even they, in front of an overwhelming opponent, would hide or try to run away.
The [Inferno Fox] back in the [Novice Continent] had tried to flee when it realized it couldn’t win.
And even the [Calamity Goblins] in the [First Calamity] turned and ran when Stark showed up.
In here, spiders had some instinct for survival too.
They’d retreat if slaughtered too easily.
This world wasn’t a "game", after all, was it?
Ding!
[You have gained 2,178 Lives!]
Even with [Hand of Avarice], sometimes you just didn’t get Evolution Points.
It didn’t matter. The lives alone were worth it.
Then came the real reward.
[Congratulations! You have leveled up to Level 26!]
[You have gained +5 to all attributes, and +5 free points.]
"All in Spirit."
He distributed the points immediately.
His body hummed with new power, spirit energy rushing through his veins.
[Level: 26 (127,000/220,000)]
Already halfway to his next level.
At this rate, he’d reach Level 30 faster than he thought.
A few more zones, a few more risks, and he’d be ready for the [Demonic Ruins].
But first—
The tunnels eventually converged into one.
A massive corridor stretched forward, silk covering the ground like a carpet.
At the far end, a cavern opened up.
"The boss room," Stark muttered.
He walked without hesitation.
The chamber he entered dwarfed all the others.
Silk coated every wall, dangling from above in thick strands.
The floor was littered with cocoons, dozens of them, some the size of a man.
They pulsed faintly, like something inside still moved.
The moment Stark stepped inside—
Fwip!
A barrier appeared behind him, sealing the tunnel.
There was no turning back now.
Then—
HISSSSS!
The hiss was loud enough to shake the chamber.
From the shadows above, something massive stirred.
Boom!
The ground shook as the spider dropped from the ceiling.
---
[Spider Queen (Level 28)]
[Rank: Legendary (Boss)
[HP: 1,000,000]
---
One million HP. The same as Andregil.
Three levels higher than the [Lord of Calamity].
It wasn’t stronger than the Lord, not exactly.
But it was close. Close enough to be a threat.
The spider queen loomed over him, her body armored in the thickest exoskeleton Stark had seen.
Eight black eyes glowed in the dark, staring down at him with cruel hunger.
A tiny crown of bone and silk rested atop her head, marking her as the ruler of this nest.
"More food..." she hissed, voice echoing in the chamber. "Good..."
Her legs tapped against the floor in a steady rhythm.
"Come forth... my children."
The cocoons around Stark trembled.
Crack! Crack! Crack!
’More experience.’ Stark’s lips curled into a grin as he raised his staff.
But his eyes never left the Spider Queen.
He pointed his staff at her, aura flaring.
"Gotta get rid of you."

chapters.title: Chapter 90: Fighting the Spider Queen, Status Meters
chapters.content:
Chapter 90: Chapter 90: Fighting the Spider Queen, Status Meters
Stark raised his staff, ready to unleash destruction on the [Spider Queen].
But right as he was about to attack...
Ding!
A panel appeared in front of him.
[Silk Bind: 4%]
’Knew it.’ Stark’s eyes narrowed. ’So it’s time [Eternal Soul] introduced the [Status Meters].’
Status effects had always been a part of the game.
The usual ones were simple enough: fear, confusion, paralysis, sleep.
Annoying, but manageable.
But these were the "basic" forms, or the more "common" ones.
The bar in front of him wasn’t one of those.
The [Status Meters] were in a completely different category.
Stronger. Rarer. More dangerous.
Instead of hitting instantly like normal effects, they appeared as a bar that filled up slowly based on the actions and environment.
And once it hit 100%, you were done.
The effect took hold, and in most cases, you were helpless.
Players could mostly encounter them when fighting bosses.
’If this was just a normal [Bind], I’d break out of the silk.’ Stark glanced down.
Strands were creeping around his boots, spreading out from the sticky floor.
Slowly, methodically, they wound tighter and tighter.
But this wasn’t normal. The bar ticked upward, slowly but steadily.
At 100%, he wouldn’t be able to move at all.
He’d be completely immobilized.
The different types of [Status Meters] were infamous.
[Whisper], [Deep Sleep], [Terror], [Death], each one nastier than the last.1
The actions of the boss also influence how high the meter climbs.
It could go slowly or... all of a sudden shoot to 100.
A full bar meant doom, and depending on the type, doom came in different forms.
Sometimes you’d be locked in place.
Sometimes you’d lose control of your own body.
Sometimes you’d simply die.
And then there was the worst of them all: [Instant Death].
Reach 100%, and you were gone permanently, your lives wouldn’t save you.
Stark exhaled slowly, gaze locked on the queen.
Thankfully, very few monsters had access to that one.
He had never encountered it. Not in his past life at least.
The only reason players knew about it was because some NPCs spoke about it.
But he knew... somewhere out there, it existed.
Nine years of playing [Eternal Soul], and even then, players seemed to have only scratched the surface.
There were mechanics, bosses, and systems no one had seen yet.
But that was fine.
For now, the only bar that mattered was the one crawling upward under his feet.
It was a timed battle, if you didn’t defeat the [Spider Queen] fast enough, you would die.
Blazing Meteor! Piercing Skeletal Spikes!
The spells roared to life.
Boom! Swash!
-389,280!
The meteor slammed into the Spider Queen’s thorax, flames exploding across her armored body.
The hit alone shredded nearly a third of her health.
Before the fire cleared, skeletal spikes erupted from the floor, jagged white bones bursting upward.
Most of them clattered harmlessly against her thick exoskeleton, leaving only scratches.
But five struck her head directly.
-72,000! -72,000! -72,000! -72,000! -72,000!
Purple ichor sprayed across the chamber as the queen shrieked.
Her eight eyes flickered with rage.
"Useless food..." she hissed, her voice dripping with venom.
Crack! Crack! Crack!
The cocoons scattered across the floor burst open all at once.
Dozens of spiders spilled out, legs scraping the ground, hissing as they swarmed toward Stark.
Slam! Slam! Slam!
They crashed against his [Unbreakable Magic Barrier], dozens of sharp legs stabbing and scraping.
The dome trembled under the assault, but it held strong.
100,000 HP. Their pitiful strikes wouldn’t be enough.
Stark grinned, "Too bad."
Blazing Meteor!
BOOM!
The explosion shook the chamber.
Fire engulfed every spider around him.
Silk burned away, corpses scattered across the ground.
The force of the blast shattered his barrier too, leaving him exposed, but the spiders were gone.
The Spider Queen roared.
"My children!" Her screech was loud enough to rattle the walls. "You will... PAY!"
["Spider Queen" has entered a "Berserk" state.]
’Oh well.’ Stark shrugged.
She didn’t have a second phase at least!
But he noticed that the silk at his feet tightened, moving faster than before.
[Silk Bind: 26%]
The queen’s berserk state was ramping up the rate.
The bar climbed faster, pressing him into a tighter corner.
He didn’t care. He still had time.
Fwish!
The Spider Queen lunged, closing the gap in a blink.
One of her enormous legs swung down like a blade.
Stark ducked, rolling to the side.
Another leg slashed at him, and he barely sidestepped in time.
Her speed was incredible. Each strike carried enough force to split stone.
Clang!
He blocked one with his staff.
The staff vibrated violently in his hands.
He knew that if he tried that too often, the weapon would shatter.
But he had no choice. Strike after strike came down.
Stark weaved, deflected, ducked, dodged.
The queen’s screeches filled the cavern, each hiss sharper than the last.
[Silk Bind: 74%]
His jaw tightened. ’The rate’s tripled since she went berserk.’
He didn’t have much time left.
One mistake, one delay, and he’d be locked in place.
No more waiting. It was time to end this.
Blazing Meteor! Piercing Skeletal Spikes!
The meteor roared from his staff, streaking toward the queen.
Fwish!
Silk Barrier!
Her legs moved in a blur, weaving thick threads into a cocoon around her body.
The meteor crashed into it and exploded, but the silk held.
The blast spread flames across the chamber, yet she stood untouched inside her shield.
Then she lunged, her shriek piercing the air.
"DIE!"
Her legs scythed toward Stark, aimed to cut him in half.
Slash! Slash! Slash!
But before she could land a killing blow, the ground erupted.
Jagged skeletal spikes speared upward, piercing straight through her head.
-72,000! -72,000! -72,000!
The queen froze. Her massive body trembled.
Her health bar plummeted to zero.
Her eight black eyes flickered once... then dimmed forever.
Boom!
Her body crashed to the ground, lifeless.
[Silk Bind: 94%]
The bar froze. Then slowly, it began to drop.
The moment the queen died, the [Status Meter] was gone.
Stark let out a sharp breath. "Nice."
He lowered his staff, surveying the battlefield.
Dozens of spider corpses littered the chamber, their charred legs twitching in the fading flames.
Ding!
---
[You have killed x11 "Ground Spider (Level 26)"]
[You have killed x4 "Miner Spider (Level 27)"]
[You have killed x2 "Guardian Spider (Level 28)"]
[You have killed x23 "Small Spider (Level 26)"]
[You have killed "Spider Queen (Level 28 Epic-Rank Boss)"]
[You have gained 173,500 Experience Points.][Congratulations! You have leveled up to Level 27!]
[You have gained +5 to all attributes, and +5 free points to distribute.]
[You have gained 13 Evolution Points!]
[You have gained 378 Lives!]
---
’Damn.’
The rewards were solid.
He’d leveled up again, his attributes rising steadily.
The spiders had dropped loot too, though none of it seemed immediately useful.
Hand of Avarice!
The spectral hand swept over the corpses.
Ding!
[You have gained 13 Evolution Points!]
[You have gained 489 Lives!]
But that wasn’t all.
The Spider Queen’s corpse glowed.
Another item appeared: golden light shining brilliantly in the dark chamber.
Stark’s eyes widened.
’Triggered extra [Evolution Points] and an evolved item?’
This fight had really paid off. He bent down and picked it up.
A necklace, its pendant shaped like a spider’s fang, gleaming faintly in the firelight.
[Spider Necklace (Legendary): If wearing this necklace, no spiders will attack you unless you strike first.]
"Wow."
This was huge.
With this, entire spider zones would become trivial.
The monsters wouldn’t attack at all unless provoked.
Players could walk right through to the boss.
It was practically a free pass.
’Too bad both my necklace slots are taken.’
Still, he wasn’t about to throw it away.
He tucked it into his inventory, along with the rest of the loot.
[Inventory: 146/152]
’Damn. Almost full.’
He exhaled, rolling his shoulders.
The chamber was quiet now, the queen and her children dead.
But as he looked deeper into the room, he noticed something odd.
At the very back, one of the larger cocoons split open, not with spiders, but with light.
Behind it, a gate shimmered into existence.
And beyond the gate... a chest.
[Epic Chest]
Stark grinned. "The real reward."

chapters.title: Chapter 91: Epic-Rank Silk Bind, Ghost Wolf’s Loyalty Increases!
chapters.content:
Chapter 91: Chapter 91: Epic-Rank Silk Bind, Ghost Wolf’s Loyalty Increases!
Stark advanced through the chamber, his boots crunching lightly on threads of silk that clung stubbornly to the stone.
The vast nest behind him was quiet now, littered with spider corpses.
At the very end of the cavern, bathed in a faint purple glow, sat his prize.
The chest, it pulsed faintly, the light breathing in and out.
The moment he laid eyes on it, Stark knew.
’Epic-rank.’
His lips curled faintly upward.
He walked closer, the glow spilling over his face.
He rested one hand against the chest, pouring mana into it.
The runes carved along its surface shimmered, clicking one after another.
Click!
The lock snapped open, and the chest’s lid creaked slowly upward.
Ding!
[You have opened the "Epic Chest" and obtained the "Silk Bind" skill book.]
"...Oh shit." Stark blinked.
Another skill book. He reached inside and pulled it free.
The cover was bound with a silver spider emblem.
[Skill Book: Silk Bind (Epic). Mage-Type Skill Book Requirement: Level 28]
"Hm."
This was the third time he’d gotten a skill book from a zone chest.
First had been [Curse Flower]. Then [Lightning Strike].
Both had proven extremely useful. And now this.
’Can’t use it yet.’
His current level was only 27.
But once he hit 28, it was his. And it looked good.
Stark already had damage. He already had defense.
What he lacked were ways to completely restrict his enemies.
This would solve that problem.
He slid the book carefully into his inventory.
Fwish!
As if responding to the chest’s opening, a portal shimmered into existence beside him.
White light swirled like mist inside the frame.
Without hesitation, Stark stepped forward and passed through.
Fwish!
Light folded around him, and then he was outside again.
The [Spider Silk Nest] was still open, but it would take time for the boss to respawn.
"Good." Stark brushed dust from his sleeve.
Another zone cleared. Another reward in hand.
His level was climbing steadily. But he wasn’t done. Not even close.
Level 27 was good progress. Still, he needed three more levels.
Only at 30 would he qualify to access the [Demonic Ruins], and with it, Olikar’s quest.
He exhaled.
’Alright. Level up to 28 first, then return to [Shell City].’
There was another issue too. His inventory.
[Inventory: 147/152]
Almost full. He needed to sell soon. The problem was timing.
It had only been a few hours since the [First Calamity] ended.
Most players were still recovering, their lives drained.
Few would have enough to buy from him.
Still, Stark didn’t want to lower his prices as he was already doing them a favor.
If buyers didn’t appear, he’d have no choice but to sell to NPCs.
The lives NPCs offered for loot were pitiful compared to what players would pay.
But even worse than losing profit was the risk of his [Reputation].
Reputation between towns and NPCs could affect you, and if it reached the lowest level, you could even be banned from entering it.
Your reputation decreased if you commited crimes or repeatedly killed NPCs inside.
And on the other hand, it increased if you did good.
’My [Slayer] status shows faintly now,’ Stark thought, eyes narrowing, ’But if it rises higher...’
Currently, at [Slayer I], NPCs didn’t actually react.
After all, there was just a faint crimson outline when they stood close.
But at [Slayer II] or [Slayer III], things would change.
The crimson glow would deepen. NPCs would notice.
They’d recoil from him, fear him. Maybe even refuse service.
In this world, NPCs weren’t mindless beings.
The higher your [Slayer] status, the more noticeable it would be after all.
And in the future, when players thinned out and NPCs became vital, reputation would matter.
Still, Stark didn’t see how his slayer status could increase any more than it was.
Perhaps [Slayer II], but he hadn’t even reached [Slayer III] in his past life, so he should be fine... right?
He pushed the thought aside. No sense worrying now.
Stark decided to check the leaderboard.
Ding!
---
[Level Leaderboard:]
[1. Oblivion: Level 27]
[2. Ghost: Level 25]
[3. SoulsGod: Level 25]
[4. Evil Demon: Level 25]
[5. Starfall: Level 25]
[6. CardMaster: Level 25]
[7. GodOfViolence: Level 25]
[8. DivineGoddess: Level 25]
[9. AwShucks: Level 25]
[10. AlphoxTheDragon: Level 25]
...
---
Thousands of names filled the list as many reached level 25.
But only one name stood at the top, ahead of them all: Oblivion.
Even Ghost and Evil Demon with their high speed and power couldn’t match him right now.
And Stark wasn’t about to let them close the gap.
Ring!
He shook the [Mount Belle] and his ghost wolf materialized beside him.
Stark swung onto its back in one motion.
"Let’s head deeper," he said, patting its neck, "As close as we can get to the [Land of Mist] as that’s where the strongest monsters are."
The wolf’s body trembled faintly. Fear rolled off it. But it obeyed.
Whoosh!
It burst forward, sprinting across the ruined streets with supernatural speed.
Monsters rose from shadows, drawn by the sound.
Stark didn’t even slow.
He fired spells off the back of the wolf, each one striking clean.
Ding! Ding! Ding!
Notifications scrolled past.
Kills confirmed. But the experience was low.
[Experience Decay] hit hard against monsters close to his level.
Lives, though, those were always welcome.
Minutes passed. The wolf sprinted without pause.
Then, suddenly...
It slowed. Its claws dug into the ground, pace faltering.
’Here it comes.’ Stark’s eyes sharpened.
