A few moments later, the [Mist Summon] bar started rising again.
[Mist Summon: 3%... 4%... 5%]
’My best bet is to head to the edge of the zone,’ Stark thought.
The further you were, the faster the bar would fill.
But on the other hand, there would be stronger monsters.
And that meant that if Stark killed them, the bar would be reduced even more!
It was an actual dilemna.
’Still... stronger monsters mean more experience,’ Stark reasoned, ’And maybe better loot.’
He weighed his options for a second.
He both wanted to get experience but also wanted to challeng the [Guardian of Mist]...
In his mind, he could still hear the distant sound of the ghost wolf’s howl from earlier.
The [Night Walk] ability of that mount would have been perfect here, letting him hide.
But the wolf was injured, and Stark wasn’t about to summon it just to get killed again.
He grinned.
"Alright, fine. I got it."
He tightened his grip on the staff and looked forward.
"I’ll just keep moving forward, kill everything, and then wait."

chapters.title: Chapter 115: Full Status Meters, The Guardian of Mist is Summoned
chapters.content:
Chapter 115: Chapter 115: Full Status Meters, The Guardian of Mist is Summoned
Ding!
[Warning!]
[Mist Summon: 90%]
After around twenty minutes of avoiding most enemies as he headed deeper, Stark’s [Status Meter] bar was almost full.
He didn’t know exactly where he was now, but judging from how far he’d gone since the center, he guessed he was close to the edge.
The density of the fog was different here.
And soon enough, he started seeing shapes ahead that confirmed it.
---
[Mist Slime (Level 47)]
[Rank: Epic]
[HP: 900,000]
---
[Eyeless Abomination (Level 48)]
[Rank: Legendary]
[HP: 1,000,000]
---
Both monsters stood still in the mist like statues.
They were getting stronger and more imposing as their levels got higher.
The deeper he went, the stronger they became.
But Stark didn’t stop. He didn’t even slow down.
He resisted the temptation to test them.
He could feel how dangerous they were just from the aura they gave off, but that wasn’t fear, it was excitement.
He smirked faintly before lowering his stance and moving past them.
Since these monsters were stronger, he could indeed use [Bind of Silk] on them without them dying.
Their HP was extremely high after all.
If they tried chasing him, he could restrain them and leave.
The [Mist Slime] was the easiest to avoid.
It was massive, slow, and barely reacted to anything that didn’t come right up to it.
’Once I defeat the [Guardian of Mist], I’ll be able to do whatever I want with these things.’
[Mist Summon: 97%]
Stark exhaled slowly.
The number kept rising, each percent taking roughly ten seconds at this depth.
Each monster that he killed reduced the bar by five to seven percent.
So, he did what he did best: he waited.
[Mist Summon: 98%]
His hand hovered above the hilt of his staff
Every few seconds, the fog shifted unnaturally, as if reacting to the meter itself.
[Mist Summon: 99%]
And right when he was about to get ready for the fight, something caught his attention.
’Huh.’
There was an opening in the ground ahead, a dark, circular hole leading downward.
It looked like a tunnel, glowing faintly with pale mist.
Without wasting time, Stark rushed toward it before the bar could reach full.
Ding!
[You are about to enter a level 42–45 zone: "Mist Cave"]
He stopped. The message floated before him, crisp and clear.
’A zone notification!’
He’d heard of this place before but had never entered it.
But the name alone told him enough: it wasn’t what he was looking for.
Not only because the levels didn’t match.
But also...
The real bloodline boss wouldn’t be found in a zone with a name as plain as [Mist Cave].
[Eternal Soul] had a habit of giving major areas dramatic names.
And after nine years in his past life, Stark could recognize it.
Still, it was tempting.
He’d come back later for sure.
Because at that moment—
[Mist Summon: 100%]
The bar flared brightly, filling completely before flashing silver.
Fwish! Ding!
[You have been inflicted with "Mist Summon" as the "Status Meter" has reached 100%]
One needed to remember that [Status Meters] were still statuses, meaning they actually affected the player’s state.
When a meter filled, it didn’t trigger an event.
It inflicted something on that player.
And as said once before, the status were much stronger than the normal ones.
The stress of watching your bar climb while knowing what was coming... most players couldn’t handle it.
Fwish!
The mist around Stark began to twist violently.
In the corner of his vision, a faint symbol appeared, an icon shaped like a swirling fog.
---
[Status Effect: Mist Summon]
[Description: The "Guardian of Mist" is here.]
---
That line was always the last thing players saw before it happened.
And this time was no different.
The fog thickened until visibility dropped to nothing.
Then, through the gray haze, a massive silhouette appeared.
A heavy thud echoed through the mist as the shape stepped forward, its form slowly materializing.
Ding!
[The "Guardian of Mist" has been summoned.]
The creature was enormous, around five meters tall.
Its frame built from stone and earth, but its joints and empty spaces were made of swirling mist.
Four arms. Four spears.
Two of solid stone, two of shimmering fog.
Its carved eyes glowed faintly white as it stared down at him.
This was the monster every player feared, the executioner of the [Land of Mist].
"Trapped..."
Its deep voice echoed across the fog, almost vibrating through the ground.
The guardian lifted all four spears at once.
"In my domain..."
Fwish!
A wave of pressure burst from the creature, sweeping through the mist like a gale.
The next moment, the ground beneath Stark vanished.
His vision blurred. The air twisted.
Ding!
[You have been transported to the "Mist Domain"]
The scenery changed instantly.
He stood now in a desolate arena made entirely of gray fog and shattered stone.
Visibility was low, but he could feel the guardian’s presence pressing down from all sides.
This was the place where the guardian slaughtered players.
It was designed so that once summoned, it could fight you alone.
"Die..."
Spear Throw!
The guardian raised all four weapons and hurled them simultaneously.
Four streaks tore through the air, each one howling like thunder.
For most players, this first attack would be the end.
But Stark was more than ready.
Fwish!
He sidestepped two of the spears.
The other two slammed into his barrier, making it shimmer violently.
-13,200! -12,500!
The hits barely scratched him, only a quarter of his barrier’s HP.
Snap!
The guardian snapped its fingers.
The ground below it rumbled as two new stone spears rose from the dirt, while the surrounding mist solidified into two more.
It had completely restored its arsenal in a second.
---
[Guardian of Mist (Level 50)]
[Rank: Mythical (Special Boss)]
[HP: 4,000,000]
---
Bind of Silk!
Stark instantly cast his spell.
If it worked, even for a few seconds, it would be massive.
But—
Slash!
The guardian swung one of its spears, cutting through the silk threads as if they were air.
"The mist shall take you..."
It lowered its body, all four spears now aimed straight at him.
Then it lunged.
Fwish!
Blazing Meteor! Crystal of Death! Piercing Skeletal Spikes!
Three spells launched in perfect succession.
A meteor burned from above, a crystal shot forward, and skeletal spikes erupted from the ground all at once.
But the guardian’s movements were fast.
It threw one spear upward, smashing the meteor before it could land.
A second spear deflected the crystal mid-air.
And with an almost graceful leap, it avoided the wave of spikes entirely.
’That thing’s agility is insane for its size.’ Stark exhaled sharply, ’No wonder it terrified everyone.’
Even in his past life, he’d hated this thing.
Still, once a player defeated the [Guardian of Mist], the [Mist Summon] status disappeared permanently for them.1
You could never meet it again.
The guardian roared and swung down its three remaining spears in a blinding arc.
BOOM!
The impact shattered the ground.
Shards of stone and mist scattered everywhere.
But Stark was already moving.
Torrent of Lightning!
Zap! Zap! Zap!
Three lightning bolts shot, slamming into the guardian’s chest before it could recover.
-1,169,640! -1,169,640! -1,169,640!
Three hits. Nearly all its HP gone in seconds.
The guardian staggered, its body crackling from the electric bursts.
"A..." Its voice trembled, "...God...?"
Stark’s eyes narrowed as he heard that, his grip tightening on his staff.
Blazing Meteor!
He raised it again, but this time, the guardian reacted faster.
"No..."
A blinding silver light poured from its eyes.
"I... won’t allow it..."
Mist Claws!
Two colossal hands of fog burst from the ground, slicing the meteor into pieces before it could fall.
Then it pointed all four arms at him again.
"I... will kill..."
"Hm."
Stark didn’t even flinch.
His focus sharpened, calm as ever.
The mist howled between them, the air tense with the weight of two powers colliding.

chapters.title: Chapter 116: Defeating the Guardian of Mist, New Skill Book!
chapters.content:
Chapter 116: Chapter 116: Defeating the Guardian of Mist, New Skill Book!
Slam! Slam! Slam!
The [Guardian of Mist] pounded its twin spears into the ground again and again, each strike shaking the air, each echo rolling like thunder through the white fog.
The shockwaves splintered across the battlefield, breaking loose chunks of stone.
Stark barely moved.
His eyes stayed locked on the towering figure in front of him.
His grip on the staff didn’t tighten or tremble.
He simply shifted his weight slightly to the left, just enough for the next spear to smash into the ground where his body had been half a second ago.
"..."
He didn’t speak. He didn’t need to.
Instead, his mana pulsed, sharp, refined, perfectly timed.
Bind of Silk! Thorny Vines of Fate! Torrent of Lightning!
Three spells unfolded almost simultaneously, each one weaving seamlessly into the other.
Threads of white silk shot forward, snapping tight around the guardian’s legs.
Vines laced with shimmering green thorns erupted from the ground, curling around its body.
Then lightning burst through the mist, three piercing bolts, all striking toward its chest from different angles.
But the [Guardian of Mist] wasn’t some slow brute.
It twisted its body, cutting through the silk and vines as if they were paper.
Then, with a single motion, it commanded the mist around it, and spectral claws formed from the vapor, blocking all three lightning strikes in midair.
The bolts fizzled out against the translucent claws.
’Hm...’ Stark’s gaze sharpened.
Those [Mist Claws] were circling constantly around the guardian, almost like its personal orbiting defense system.
Every time Stark moved forward, they reacted instantly, slashing out, forcing him to dodge or rely on his barrier to tank the hit.
Slash!
A claw cut across him, but the strike only sparked against his protection.
[Unbreakable Magic Barrier: 17,900/100,000]
The number flickered briefly at the corner of his vision.
Still, Stark didn’t seem the least bit worried.
He knew the difference between danger and pressure.
The guardian might have been powerful, fast, reactive, disciplined, but it wasn’t invincible.
Not against him. If even one of his spells landed, it would be over.
Blazing Meteor! Crystal of Death!
Two high-tier spells fired in rapid succession.
One from above, one from below, a perfect pincer strike.
"Futile..." The guardian’s voice rumbled low, almost regretful, as it stopped its assault and focused entirely on defense.
Every time Stark launched an attack, the creature abandoned all offense to block it.
It was playing carefully and smartly.
It wasn’t trying to overpower him anymore.
It had realized who it was facing: a mage.
And a mage could burn through mana faster than any warrior burned stamina, and its cooldowns were much higher.
If it just outlasted him, waited for his mana to empty or his barrier to collapse, it would win.
The guardian knew that. Stark knew that too though.
Mist Claws hovered protectively in front of the guardian, ready to block or slice depending on what came next.
Clang! Slash!
Each time Stark’s spells met the defense, the mist rippled like glass.
Deflected! Blocked!
But Stark’s eyes didn’t dim.
If anything, they gleamed brighter.
Because if he knew how the enemy would react, then he also knew how to end it.
"None of your attacks... will work..." the guardian said again, its voice trembling like air in the fog, "I have sensed... the aura... of a God on you..."
"Hm."
Stark exhaled softly, expression unreadable.
He didn’t need to ask which god.
The [God of Oblivion], it was always that.
Still, it didn’t matter who watched. He needed to win first.
And so, instead of casting another spell, Stark moved.
He lifted his foot high, and slammed it into the ground.
Calamity Shockwave!
The impact tore through the mist with a deep crimson pulse.
The shockwave expanded outward like a ring of fire, distorting the fog into swirling spirals.
The guardian froze for just an instant, a fraction of a second of disruption.
Then its body shuddered, regaining balance.
"You cannot—"
Before it could finish, Stark’s hand shot up.
He gripped the [Revenant Bell] around his neck and gave it a hard shake.
Bam!
A piercing blue wave burst out, sharper, colder, the sound of shattering souls.
Soul Shockwave!
The two effects combined, physical shock followed by spiritual disruption.
One alone might not have worked.
But back-to-back? Even a special boss staggered.
The guardian’s body went still, mist rippling violently around it.
’Now.’
Torrent of Lightning! Piercing Skeletal Spikes!
Three lightning bolts formed instantly, whirling into arcs as Stark guided them with precise movements.
They cut through the air from three different angles, converging toward the guardian’s chest.
Slash! Slash! Slash!
Even stunned, the [Mist Claws] reacted automatically, blocking the attacks before they hit.
But that was exactly what Stark wanted.
Because the moment those claws shifted position, the ground beneath the guardian cracked open, and fifteen bone spikes erupted upward like a trap closing shut.
Piercing Skeletal Spikes!
Each one slammed into the guardian’s torso, shoulders, and legs, impaling through the mist flesh and nailing it to the ground.
-72,000! -72,000! -72,000!
Over a million total damage in an instant.
The [Guardian of Mist] froze, then its form began to dissolve.
The claws shattered, the fog thinned, and the massive body crumbled apart into a collapsing heap.
Fwiiiish—
The [Mist Domain] that had surrounded them began to fade, the walls of white mist swirling before evaporating entirely.
Stark found himself standing once again in the [Land of Mist], the endless, pale forest of vapor spreading out all around him.
And at his feet, the guardian’s body remained.
Not vanishing like most monsters. Not turning into mist.
’Not all of it was controlled by the fog...’ Stark’s eyes narrowed, a sharp grin forming, ’That means... it won’t disappear!’
Ding!
---
[You have killed "Guardian of Mist (Level 50 Special Boss)"]
[You have gained 1,500,000 experience points.]
[Congratulations! You have leveled up to Level 42 + Level 43 + Level 44!]
[You have gained 15 points in all attributes and 15 free points to distribute.]
[You have gained 34 Evolution Points!]
[You have gained 2,100 Lives!]
---
Hand of Avarice!
The spectral black hand shot out from Stark’s staff, plunging deep into the guardian’s corpse.
Energy surged back into him like a current of light.
Ding!
[You have gained 28 Evolution Points!]
[You have gained 2,130 Lives!]
And then, something glimmered on the ground.
Three items dropped.
Stark crouched down, scanning them with focused eyes.
The mist had cleared entirely now, and his [Mist Summon] meter was gone.
He could move freely across this zone without worrying about the summoning event triggering again.
He extended his hand toward the first glowing item.
[Skill Book: Elemental Spears (Legendary): Mage-type skill book. Requirement: Level 50.]
’Oh shit,’ Stark muttered, eyes widening, ’A new skill book... and a legendary one too.’
He could already feel the mana radiating from it, powerful, pure, raw.
A level 50 spell would completely outclass everything he currently had.
And if he evolved it like his other skills to ancient rank...
A grin tugged at his mouth.
He stored it in his inventory instantly, already imagining the destruction it could bring.
If it was anything like the guardian’s spear attacks, the damage potential would be absurd.
Next, he checked the second item.
---
[Earth and Fog Spear (Mythical): Warrior/Sentinel-type weapon. +7,300 Strength, +2,000 Agility. Requirement: Level 50.]
[Spear Call (Passive): After throwing the spear, you can call it back to your hand after a second.]
---
A solid weapon, but not for him. He was no warrior.
Still, the value was impressive.
The stats alone made it worth storing or selling later.
Then his attention shifted to the last drop, the one he’d pulled directly from the guardian’s corpse using [Hand of Avarice].
It gleamed faintly in a swirl of silver mist.
’Hah,’ Stark’s grin widened, ’This is the one I wanted.’
He crouched again, fingers brushing the cold surface.
The notification appeared.
[Mist Repellant Ring (Mythical)]

chapters.title: Chapter 117: Mist Repellant Ring, Level 50 Requirement
chapters.content:
Chapter 117: Chapter 117: Mist Repellant Ring, Level 50 Requirement
[Mist Repellant Ring (Mythical): When wearing this ring, will allow the user to see perfectly fine inside the "Land of Mist". Requirement: Level 50]
This was precisely the item Stark wanted.
With that, he could finally see where he was going.
That meant one thing, he would be able to find the zone where the bloodline boss was.
Of course, Stark had only heard bits of information about it.
The only reason he even knew about the bloodline and its monster was because other players in his past life had talked about it.
They complained about how impossible it was.
How that place chewed people alive and left no traces behind.
When facing a bloodline boss, it would actually say "Bloodline Boss" next to the rank, and even show the exact bloodline you’d receive if you managed to defeat it.
That way, players knew exactly what they were risking their lives for.
But this setup wasn’t a reward, it was bait. A trap by the system.
It wanted players to see the reward glowing in front of them, close enough to touch, only for it to crush them seconds later.
After all, the zone Stark was aiming for was a level 50 zone.
And once a player went past level 50, it would lock forever for them. No second chances.
If you missed the window, that was it.
So back then, most players who saw the [Spirit Devourer] bloodline tried their luck.
They ran into that zone with excitement, chasing what looked like a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity.
But they only respawned one after another, if not had been killed permanently.
And it made sense.
The [Bloodline Bosses] were unique.
Only one of each existed in the whole world.
Killing one meant no one else could ever get that same bloodline again.
That was part of what made them legendary.
But also terrifying.
Because [Bloodline Monsters] were in a completely different class from anything else.
Some of the strongest boss types in [Eternal Soul].
They were simply... unfair to fight, and always had crazy mechanics and conditions to fight them.
Even Stark knew this was a straight path into danger, but that didn’t matter.
He needed that bloodline.
Anything that gave him even an advantage was worth it.
He stored the ring in his inventory, saving it for when he hit level 50, and decided to focus on leveling as fast as possible.
Then, he turned toward the [Mist Cave] he had seen earlier.
Ding!
[You are about to enter a level 42–45 zone: "Mist Cave"]
’Should I go in?’ Stark scratched his chin, eyes fixed on the entrance.
If he went to the edge of the [Land of Mist] now, he’d face level 48–50 monsters instead, and those would give far better experience.
’I want to be as fast and efficient as possible,’ he thought.
Still, the [Mist Cave] might hold useful items.
He could probably sell some drops, make quick gold.
But right now, he didn’t really need items or lives.
So...
’I’ll come back later,’ he decided as he turned around.
The [Land of Mist] was hard enough to move through as it was, and until he could see clearly, pushing forward blindly was pointless.
Once he wore that ring, though, it would be a different story.
He turned his back on the cave and headed deeper into the mist.
On his way to the outer edge of the [Land of Mist], two familiar figures appeared in the fog.
The [Mist Slime (Level 47)] and the [Eyeless Abomination (Level 48)] he had avoided earlier.
Stark stopped, his eyes narrowing slightly.
The two monsters stared back.
Their sluggish bodies tensed the moment they recognized him.
The silence lasted a second.
Then, both roared and charged forward.
’Hah,’ Stark thought.
It was funny, really.
To them, it probably looked like he had run away before because he was weak.
But now they were about to realize just how wrong they were.
Bind of Silk!
The spell activated instantly, silk threads bursting from his staff.
They flew straight at the [Eyeless Abomination], wrapping around its gray, corpse-like frame.
The creature’s claws lashed out wildly, but too late.
The silk tightened, locking its limbs and forcing it still.
-783,360!
Its body jerked violently as it lost nearly all its HP in a single cast.
Seeing that, the [Mist Slime] reacted.
Its body rippled as it oozed forward, surrounding the [Eyeless Abomination].
The silver fluid seeped into the cracks of its companion’s body.
And then—
Mist Healing!
-500,000!
"Huh."
Stark blinked.
So the slime was actually a support-class monster. Those were rare.
Most monsters attacked mindlessly, even alone.
But a few, like this one, had been designed to work in groups, healing and buffing their allies.
It was interesting. But it didn’t matter.
The slime tensed, gathering itself to lunge forward and protect its companion.
After all, this human had run away earlier, so he must be weak, right?
Torrent of Lightning!
Lightning gathered around Stark, his staff crackling as he aimed at both targets.
Zap! Zap! Zap!
Six lightning bolts shot forward, each one aimed perfectly.
-1,175,040! -1,175,040! -1,175,040!
Both monsters froze mid-motion before collapsing.
Dead. They didn’t even have time to scream.
Even these level 47–48 monsters were nothing but fodder in front of Stark’s power.
Ding!
---
[You have killed "Mist Slime (Level 47)"]
[You have killed "Eyeless Abomination (Level 48)"]
[You have gained 46,000 experience points!]
---
’Nice. The experience here’s much better since I’m only level 44,’ Stark thought, grinning.
[You have gained 1 Evolution Point!]
[You have gained 174 Lives!]
’Damn,’ Stark muttered under his breath.
This was the first time in a long while that normal monsters had given him Evolution Points.
He almost forgot they could even drop EP.
The rate was just so low it barely ever happened.
Still, he wasn’t going to complain. Every point counted.
Bosses would always be the main source, but it was good to get small bonuses here and there.
He stored the two drops that had fallen and kept moving.
The mist around him never changed, it always looked the same.
Endless white, drifting, quiet.
Only the faint echo of his boots and the occasional glimmer of a monster’s eyes broke the stillness.
And yet Stark moved with confidence.
Every step took him deeper into the unknown.
Monsters appeared now and then, [Mist Hounds], [Corrupted Spirits], even another [Eyeless Abomination].
Each time, he dispatched them quickly, barely slowing down.
An hour passed.
Ding!
[Congratulations! You have leveled up to Level 48!]
Stark gained four levels in an hour.
Only two more to go before hitting level 50.
He closed the window and let out a quiet breath, his eyes gleaming faintly under the pale glow of the mist.
He could feel the difference already, his magic output, his speed, everything had grown sharper.
And more importantly, he had gained over fifty Evolution Points in that span alone.
[Current Evolution Points: 128.]
’Heh. Only one of my offensive skills is still at mythical-rank,’ Stark thought, a grin stretching across his face.
If this pace continued, he’d reach level 50 soon.
He didn’t think he’d hit 250 Evolution Points before then, but it didn’t matter.
128 was more than enough to evolve another skill.
He was almost ready.
Soon, he’d wear that [Mist Repellant Ring], step into the bloodline zone, and hunt down the bloodline boss.
Stark glanced at the fog-covered horizon, then back down at his panel.

chapters.title: Chapter 118: Sharp Crystals of Death, Blessing the Demon Horns
chapters.content:
Chapter 118: Chapter 118: Sharp Crystals of Death, Blessing the Demon Horns
[Do you wish to consume 100 Evolution Points to evolve "Crystals of Death"?]
"Yes!"
This was the only offensive skill Stark still had stuck at mythical-rank.
Aside from that, only [Curse Flower] was still mythical, everything else had already ascended to ancient-rank.
No normal player could even dream of reaching such a stage, and even Stark himself found it hard to believe how far he’d come.
Ding!
[You have evolved "Crystals of Death" (Mythical) to "Sharp Crystals of Death" (Ancient)]
[Current Evolution Points: 28]
---
[Sharp Crystals of Death (Ancient): Summon up to 10 → 15 crystals that deal 2,500 → 5,000 damage each. You can now shoot up to 5 crystals at one enemy. Applies the "Poison" status effect. 10 (5)-seconds cooldown.]
[Poison: Deals 50% → 75% of damage received for 5 seconds.]
---
"Damn."
Stark couldn’t help but grin.
He had gotten this skill back at level 2, and it had stayed with him through everything.
Now that it had evolved, the difference was massive.
[Crystals of Death] had always been his weakest skill.
It didn’t deal that much damage compared to his others, even with the poison effect, and it was limited to striking only one crystal per enemy at a time.
But that limit was gone now.
He could launch five crystals at once, each one dealing doubled damage.
And with the poison buffed too, the total damage potential was absurd.
If Stark’s quick math was right, this skill could now deal around one million damage in just a few seconds.
And with its short cooldown, it was deadly.
He imagined chaining it with his other abilities and almost laughed.
The low-level skill that used to feel like a filler was now a powerful spell.
Even more reason to look forward to what awaited him at level 50.
The skill book for [Elemental Spears] would outclass anything he had.
A level 50 skill in [Eternal Soul] wasn’t just stronger, it was on another plane entirely, at least compared to the ones before it.
Satisfied, Stark pressed onward.
Hours passed as he cut his way through the monsters infesting the [Land of Mist].
The fog around him swirled endlessly, thick and pale.
But thanks to the [Mist Repellant Ring] in his inventory, he knew he’d soon be able to travel freely through the deeper zones.
For now, though, he continued farming as he needed to gain as much experience points as possible.
Each kill dropped some exp, and his progress bar crept closer and closer to its goal.
And so after another hour of relentless combat—
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 49!]
[You have gained 5 points in all of your attributes, and 5 free points to distribute.]
"Almost there," Stark muttered.
Just one more push and he’d be at level 50.
Then he could finally challenge the bloodline boss and claim the [Spirit Devourer] bloodline for himself.
But as Stark got ready to continue after killing more monsters... another notification appeared.
Ding!
[Your "Heart of Sanctuary" has recharged.]
"Oh?"
That caught his attention.
The last time the [Heart of Sanctuary] had recharged was back on the second day of the [First Calamity], barely two days ago.
It hadn’t been long, but when inside [Eternal Soul], so many things happen that you sometime lose your sense of time.
He quickly opened his inventory and reviewed his current equipment.
---
Weapon: Divine Staff (Legendary)
Hat: Demon Horns (Mythical)
Chest: Demonic Wyvern Scales Robe (Legendary)
Boots: Calamity Boots (Legendary)
Necklaces: Revenant Bell (Special Item), Dark Necklace (Epic)
Rings: Small Space Ring (Rare)
Backpacks: Normal Backpack (Common), Snake Backpack (Epic), Calamity Fur Backpack (Legendary)
---
He studied the list for a moment, tapping his fingers against his staff.
’Let’s see... The [Divine Staff] and [Calamity Fur Backpack] have already been blessed.
I could bless something new, or replace one of their old blessings with a new one.’
Ding!
[You can bless items that have been blessed before, but it will result in changing their previous blessing into a new one.]
"Oh?"
That was interesting, but he immediately shook his head.
There was no point in changing what already worked.
His staff was perfect as it was.
’Alright... what about the [Revenant Bell]?’
That item had been on his mind for a while.
It was one of the most unique items in his entire collection, a "special item" with both passive and active traits.
But then again, there were the [Demon Horns] and the [Demonic Wyvern Scales Robe], both of which were extremely powerful.
If he blessed one of them, the reward could be incredible.
The system’s blessings were always tied to the nature of the item itself.
His [Divine Staff] had gained a 20% damage boost because it was a weapon.
His [Calamity Fur Backpack] had doubled its storage space because it was, well, a backpack.
So if he blessed something like the [Revenant Bell], the effect would likely tie into one of its special abilities.
The question was: was that really worth it right now?
He crossed his arms and stared at the mist for a few minutes, thinking deeply.
While he pondered, a stray monster lunged at him from the fog.
Without even looking, Stark raised his hand and unleashed a bolt of lightning that fried it instantly.
The thing barely had time to scream.
These low-level mobs weren’t even a threat anymore.
Still, Stark knew he needed to make the most strategic choice possible.
The bell was strong, yes, but he’d likely keep wearing it for a long time.
Its ability to prevent life loss on death was rare and valuable.
The robe was excellent too, but armor could always be replaced.
The horns, though... those were rare.
Hats and headpieces in [Eternal Soul] were far less common than robes or boots, and mythical-tier ones were nearly unheard of.
After another moment of silence, Stark made his decision.
’Yeah. The horns it is.’
He took a deep breath and activated the relic.
Ding!
[You have used the "Heart of Sanctuary" on "Demon Horns"]
Crimson light immediately enveloped him, swirling up from the ground before seeping into the curved horns that jutted from his head.
He felt heat and energy coursing through them as the aura merged into their demonic power.
Ding!
[You have blessed the "Demon Horns"]
---
[Demon Horns (Mythical): These horns are proof that an individual has bested a strong demon. +2,000 Strength, +1,000 Spirit, +500 Agility, +1,000 Constitution. Requirement: Level 38.]
[Demon Approval (Passive): Your reputation with demons will be SLIGHTLY improved while wearing these horns.]
[Sanctuary Blessing: The demonic aura of the horns powers your form. Your Constitution is multiplied by x5.]
---
"Holy—"
Stark’s eyes widened as he opened his stats panel.
[Constitution: 250 (+1,800)]
That meant his total Constitution was now 2,050, which was 20,500 HP normally.
But with the blessing’s x5 multiplier, that became 100,000 HP.
One hundred thousand!
That was equivalent to his entire [Unbreakable Magic Barrier].
For the first time, Stark felt like an actual fortress.
Even if he took several powerful hits, he could survive without instantly dying.
He grinned.
This was exactly the kind of edge he needed for what was coming.
Blessing the [Revenant Bell] might have been interesting, but this... this was perfect.
’Yeah, I made the right call.’
He glanced down at the bell hanging from his neck anyway.
---
[Revenant Bell (Special Item): When carried, death will not result in any lives lost. 6-hour cooldown.]
---
It was an incredible piece of equipment.
Most players would probably do a lot of things to own something like that.
But Stark hadn’t died even once since [Eternal Soul] started.
It was a good backup plan, nothing more.
And his decision had just multiplied his total survivability fivefold.
That was more than enough.
The [Heart of Sanctuary] was now on cooldown again.
He wouldn’t be able to use it until he killed enough monsters to recharge it. But that was fine.
By then, he’d have hit level 50 and be ready for what came next.
The monsters around him were growing stronger the deeper he went.
Mist twisted around jagged rocks, and faint shapes loomed in the fog.
The sound of movement echoed through the air, heavy, metallic.
It sounded like armor clinking. Someone, or something, was walking toward him.
Stark stopped moving and gripped his staff tightly, lowering his stance.
The faint crimson glow of his newly blessed horns pulsed in rhythm with his heartbeat.
’Only one more level,’ he thought, eyes narrowing.
Then he smiled.
’Let’s see what’s next.’

chapters.title: Chapter 119: Reaching Level 50, Tier-3 Advancement Task
chapters.content:
Chapter 119: Chapter 119: Reaching Level 50, Tier-3 Advancement Task
As Stark looked forward, the mist around him began to shift.
The air grew heavier, and faint metallic echoes rang through the haze.
Then, three armored figures slowly emerged from the fog, their forms solidifying into shape.
---
[Mist Sentinel Trio (Level 50)]
[Rank: Legendary (Special Boss)]
[HP: 1,500,000 HP]
---
At first glance, the HP seemed unusually low for a legendary-level 50 boss.
But Stark knew better.
It wasn’t one enemy, it was three.
In [Eternal Soul], most bosses fought alone or with normal monsters supporting them.
But sometimes, rare boss types appeared, those that came in pairs, trios or even more.
Each one counted as part of the same encounter.
Which meant each of these three sentinels had 1.5 million HP.
To clear the boss, Stark had to kill all three.
He smirked. "That’s fine."
Each of the sentinels looked identical.
Their armor shimmered like condensed mist, and in their hands, they carried long silver blades that glowed faintly in the fog.
Their movements were synchronized, precise, and unnervingly fluid, as if they shared one mind.
When they charged, they did it together.
The ground shook as their armored boots struck in unison.
Stark didn’t move.
Bind of Silk!
White silk shot out from his hands, splitting into three threads aimed at each of the sentinels.
But before the threads could tighten, the sentinels swung their blades, slicing through the bindings cleanly.
The coordination between them was perfect, one covering the other’s blind spot, every step calculated.
’Figures,’ Stark thought. ’Trio bosses always have this kind of synergy.’
Still, it didn’t matter. He only needed to break that flow once.
If he managed to kill even one, the other two would lose their rhythm.
The three sentinels lunged forward, blades cutting through the mist with blinding speed.
Stark raised his staff, activating his [Unbreakable Magic Barrier].
The impact hit like thunder.
CLANG!
Two slashes connected, one from his left and one from behind.
The barrier held, but Stark felt the recoil as his feet slid backward through the mist.
He couldn’t dodge from three sides at once.
But he didn’t need to.
He stepped back, planting his staff into the ground.
"Let’s see how you handle this."
Blazing Meteor! Sharp Crystals of Death!
The sky above them ignited, and a burning meteor tore through the mist.
Teh crystals followed afterward, streaking like bright shards of destruction.
The sentinels looked up and tried to block the meteor with their blades, but the force behind the spell was overwhelming.
BOOM!
A fiery explosion tore the mist apart.
-1,578,720! -1,578,720! -1,578,720!
The ground trembled.
When the smoke cleared, all three sentinels were gone, erased in an instant.
"Damn..." Stark grinned, lowering his staff.
It was the first time he had seen [Blazing Meteor]’s full power since equipping the [Demonic Wyvern Scales Robe].
The increase in spirit from both the robe and his [Demon Horns] was insane.
The meteor had wiped out three level 50 legendary bosses in one cast.
The extra crystals he’d fired simply dispersed into nothing, their targets already dead.
Ding!
---
[You have killed "Mist Sentinel Trio (Level 50 Special Boss)"]
[You have gained 300,000 experience points.]
[Congratulations! You have leveled up to Level 50!]
[You have gained 5 points in all attributes and 5 free points to distribute.]
[You have gained 17 Evolution Points!]
[You have gained 219 Lives!]
---
Hand of Avarice!
[You have gained 32 Evolution Points!]
[You have gained 410 Lives!]
Stark’s smile widened.
’Perfect.’
He had reached the cap, level 50, right after defeating a special boss.
He walked forward, gathering the loot left behind.
Three identical swords shimmered on the ground: [Mist Sentinel Sword (Legendary)].
He picked them up and tossed them into his inventory. It was almost full now.
’Guess I’ll need a better backpack soon.’
Once he reached the next major city, he planned to trade or buy something stronger.
Dropping items from monsters was nice, but buying from specialized shops was faster once he had the lives.
As he was sorting through his inventory...
Ding!
A global announcement rang in the ears of every player.
---
[Congratulations to player "Oblivion" for being the first player in the world to reach Level 50!]
[You have gained 15 Prestige Points!]
---
"What the hell?"
"Already?!"
"Holy shit, but the second in the leaderboard is only at level 40!"
"Ten level difference, how?!"
Other players were confused and shocked, and it wasn’t unexpected.
Even Stark was slightly surprised by his fast growth, even though he had done it all by himself.
Still, he moved on quickly as more panels appeared.
Ding!
---
[Congratulations, you have reached Level 50.]
[Your experience will now be locked until you complete your advancement task.]
[Depending on your task rating, your class may evolve in different ways.]
---
This was it, the Tier-3 Advancement Task.
Unlike the first two advancement missions, which were the same for everyone, starting from level 50, advancement tasks became personal.
They adapted to each player and where they were.
For some, it meant finding an item.
For others, clearing a zone or defeating a boss.
And for players at the top like Stark, it meant the hardest possible specialized challenges.
Ding!
[You will receive the hardest Tier-3 Advancement Task possible at your level.]
"Hah." Stark couldn’t help but grin. "Of course."
[Eternal Soul] loved testing limits.
It always tried to crush those who climbed too high, to remind them that there was always something stronger waiting.
But that didn’t scare him. He welcomed it.
Ding!
[Tier-3 Advancement Task: Clear the "Blood Mist" zone by defeating its boss, "Kaiser, The Spirit Devourer."]
The name froze him for a moment.
Then his eyes narrowed. The [Blood Mist] zone.
The most dangerous part of the [Land of Mist].
And the name of the boss, "Kaiser, The Spirit Devourer", confirmed it.
It was the same bloodline boss Stark had been planning to find.
So the system wanted him to face it now.
’Heh.’ He smirked. ’I guess it wasn’t lying about being the hardest.’
In his past life, nobody had ever managed to defeat Kaiser.
Countless players had tried, drawn by the promise of the [Spirit Devourer] bloodline, only to be wiped out again and again.
This task would have been a death sentence for anyone else.
But Stark wasn’t anyone else. And he wasn’t planning to die.
He dismissed the floating panels and exhaled, letting the mist settle around him once more.
Silence filled the area. The only sound was the faint whisper of the wind.
Then he smiled.
’Alright.’
[Level: 50 (Locked)]
His level bar had frozen, just like at level 25.
No matter how many monsters he killed, his experience wouldn’t move.
Advancement tasks were designed that way, to force players to face new trials before progressing further.
Experience wouldn’t even accumulate.
Every bit of progress was blocked until the task was complete.
So, most players rushed to clear it as quickly as possible.
But Stark wasn’t "most players."
He wanted a perfect completion rating.
Because the higher the rating, the stronger the class evolution. It would be the same this time.
He adjusted his grip on the staff and opened his inventory once more.
Two items he’d been holding onto were now finally usable.
[Elemental Spears (Skill Book)] and [Mist Repellant Ring (Mythical)]
He’d kept both sealed in his inventory until he reached the required level.
"Finally."

chapters.title: Chapter 120: Using The Mist Repellant Ring and Elemental Spears
chapters.content:
Chapter 120: Chapter 120: Using The Mist Repellant Ring and Elemental Spears
[Mist Repellant Ring (Mythical): When wearing this ring, will allow the user to see perfectly fine inside the "Land of Mist". Requirement: Level 50]
---
Stark immediately wore the ring on his left hand, next to the [Flame Ring (Rare)] and [Small Space Ring (Rare)].
Both were pretty much useless now, but he still kept them on since he didn’t have anything better.
A player could equip up to five rings, so even with the new one, he still had two free slots for later.
Rings were usually considered weaker than other equipment pieces, which was the reason [Eternal Soul] allowed more of them to be worn.
And as for why players couldn’t just wear ten rings since they had ten fingers?
Well... nobody really knew. It was just how [Eternal Soul] worked.
The same logic applied to hats and necklaces.
Even if someone tried to put on a sixth ring, a transparent barrier would block it completely, making it impossible.
[Eternal Soul] didn’t joke around when it came to rules.
The moment Stark slid the [Mist Repellant Ring] onto his finger, his surroundings changed.
Fwish!
The mist that had always covered the [Land of Mist] vanished from his sight.
His entire field of vision cleared in an instant.
’Damn... it feels weird.’
He could now see everything, the flat wasteland stretching out before him, the broken rocks, the dead earth.
Somehow, the place looked even more lifeless without the fog covering it.
A few monsters wandered in the distance, but he didn’t pay them any attention.
He moved on to what truly interested him next.
[Skill Book: Elemental Spears (Legendary): Mage-type skill book. Requirement: Level 50.]
He poured his mana into the book without hesitation.
Ding!
[You have learned the skill "Elemental Spears"!]
’Nice.’
He opened his skill window immediately to check the new ability’s details.
---
[Elemental Spears (Legendary): Can summon up to 5 spears from different elements, each one capable of dealing 1,500% of Spirit. 10 (5)-seconds cooldown between each spear.]
[Available Elements: Mist, Earth...]
---
"Oh?"
It was exactly what he’d hoped for, strong, efficient, and clearly high-tier.
Right now, he only had two elements: [Mist] and [Earth].
Coincidentally, those were the same ones the [Guardian of Mist] had used earlier.
Skills like this usually came from somewhere specific, so it made sense.
The damage output was also incredible.
For a legendary skill, 1,500% of Spirit was monstrous.
As for the cooldown, it wasn’t global, it applied to each individual spear.
Meaning when he summoned a spear from one element and threw it, that specific spear would have to wait 5 seconds before being used again.
If he summoned all five spears at once, it would take 25 seconds for them all to recharge.
It was a slightly different rhythm compared to his other spells, but he didn’t mind.
It actually gave him more tactical control.
But then something else came to mind: he could evolve this skill once as he had enough EP!
Fwish!
[Do you wish to consume 50 Evolution Points to evolve "Elemental Spears"?]
"Yes."
Ding!
[You have evolved "Elemental Spears" (Legendary) to "Elemental Spears" (Mythical).]
[Current Evolution Points: 27.]
---
[Elemental Spears (Mythical): Can summon up to 5 spears from different elements, each one capable of dealing 1,500% → 2,000% of Spirit. 10 (5)-seconds cooldown between each spear.]
[Available Elements: Mist, Earth, +Fire, +Water...]
---
The new stats made him grin.
The power increased from 1,500% to 2,000%, a massive jump.
But the biggest part wasn’t even that.
Two new elements had appeared: [Fire] and [Water].
It didn’t seem like they gave any additional passive bonuses yet, but that didn’t matter.
The raw potential of this skill was ridiculous.
’If I can get all elements unlocked someday...’
He smirked. That would mean almost every enemy he faced would have a weakness he could exploit.
After all, elemental weaknesses increased damage by 1.5x, and now he had four elements already.
It was a perfect setup for flexibility in battle.
When he was done reading through the panels, Stark dismissed them all and turned toward the endless plain.
’I need to find the [Blood Mist] zone now,’ he thought, tightening his grip on his staff.
The ring made everything easier to see, but that didn’t mean the search would be fast.
The players who’d come this far in his past life had barely made it out alive, and none had ever shared how to find the zone.
Still, Stark had an advantage they didn’t: experience.
He started running across the wasteland, moving at full speed, eyes scanning the horizon for anything unusual.
Monsters appeared along the way, but he ignored every one of them.
Even when a few tried to chase, they gave up quickly.
Stark was too fast and too focused to waste time.
He passed several strange ruins, and even a few minor zones.
Zones within the [Land of Mist] were rare to begin with, he’d only seen two so far, including the [Mist Cave].
Time passed.
And thirty minutes later, he began thinking about changing his approach.
Maybe he’d missed something. But then, something caught his eye.
A faint red glow in the distance.
"Huh."
At first, he thought it was just another illusion caused by the light.
But then he looked closer.
It wasn’t light, it was mist. Red mist.
’Wait... what?’
The [Mist Repellant Ring] was supposed to completely clear any mist from the [Land of Mist].
That meant... This wasn’t part of the same mist.
It was coming from somewhere else. That realization made Stark narrow his eyes.
If this mist wasn’t from the [Land of Mist], then it could only be from one place. The [Blood Mist].
And judging by the density of the red fog, he was close.
It was deep, deep in the [Major Zone], where barely anyone had dared to go.
Stark realized he had been running at full speed for more than thirty minutes straight, which explained why he had made it this far.
He couldn’t help but wonder how any of the past players had even reached this place.
Did they just really explore this much? Or perhaps they got lost until getting there.
Still, he needed to confirm. With a focused expression, Stark dashed forward.
The closer he got, the denser the red mist became.
It wasn’t just mist anymore, it was heavy, pressing down on him like weight.
And then something strange happened. The monsters disappeared.
He looked around, realizing that not a single creature was within sight.
It was as if everything living had chosen to avoid this place entirely.
Even Stark could feel it, the air around him felt suffocating.
A wave of pressure loomed from beyond the red veil.
He exhaled slowly and stepped closer.
And then—
Ding!
[You are about to enter an extremely dangerous level 50 zone: "Blood Mist"]
[Once you enter, you cannot leave unless you die.]
Stark grinned.
’So this is it... the hardest zone in the [Land of Mist].’
He knew what was waiting for him inside. But that didn’t stop him.
Even if it was dangerous, even if no one else had ever cleared it, Stark wasn’t afraid.
If anything, he felt alive.
He took a single step forward, crossing the invisible boundary that usually separated the gray from the crimson.
The red fog swirled around him instantly, twisting like a living thing.
And as the light dimmed, Stark’s grin widened.
’Let’s see what you’ve got.’
And then—
He vanished into the [Blood Mist].

chapters.title: Chapter 121: Blood Mist Zone, Strong Bleeding Status Effect
chapters.content:
Chapter 121: Chapter 121: Blood Mist Zone, Strong Bleeding Status Effect
Ding!
---
[You have entered the "Blood Mist"]
[Lives loss rate: 5,000]
[Description: Very similar to the "Land of Mist" except that your vision is blocked by the tainted red mist.]
---
Stark took a slow breath, his expression calm as the new environment settled around him.
The air was heavy, almost thick, and every breath carried a faint metallic taste, like iron.
The ground under his boots was soft, wet, and stained red.
’Five thousand lives loss rate,’ he thought, narrowing his eyes, ’Hah... that’s brutal.’
No wonder barely anyone ever came back from this place when entering.
Dying once here meant losing 5,000 lives instantly.
A handful of high-level players might’ve had enough lives to survive that penalty, but most didn’t.
For them, entering this place was simply suicide. Still, Stark didn’t stop.
He stepped forward, and right away—
Ding!
[Strong Bleeding: 5%... 6%...]
"Oh."
A familiar mechanic.
Just like the [Land of Mist], this place had its own [Status Meter].
But this one wasn’t about summoning anything, it was about killing you slowly.
[Strong Bleeding] was a direct evolution of [Bleeding], a nasty status effect.
Instead of dealing a small periodic loss of HP, it shredded through your health over time.
The longer he stayed inside, the more dangerous it got.
Stark kept walking, his staff ready, eyes sharp.
’Some players managed to reach the boss in my past life,’ he thought, watching the meter climb.
’So there must be a way to manage it.’
[Strong Bleeding: 16%...]
"What the fuck," he muttered under his breath.
That thing was climbing way too fast.
Even with his high Spirit resistance, it didn’t seem to slow down at all.
He could barely see a few meters ahead—the red mist distorted his vision worse than the normal one ever did.
’I can’t take my time here,’ he realized.
Immediately, Stark started running.
His boots splashed into the blood-colored ground as he rushed through the haze, keeping his eyes on the faint silhouettes ahead.
’Every zone in [Eternal Soul] is possible. There’s no such thing as an impossible zone.’
He just had to find the boss before his HP drained too far.
The first monsters appeared soon after.
They stepped out of the blood mist, red shapes forming into bodies that were both familiar and terrifying.
---
[Blood Slime (Level 50)]
[Rank: Legendary]
[HP: 1,200,000]
---
[Blood Mist Reaper (Level 50)]
[Rank: Legendary]
[HP: 1,100,000]
---
[Blood Mist Wolves (Level 50)]
[Rank: Mythical]
[HP: 1,250,000]
---
A dozen monsters surrounded Stark in an instant, crawling out of the mist like ghosts made of crimson smoke.
He immediately noticed it, they were the same species from the [Land of Mist].
Only now, they’d been transformed.
Their bodies no longer gave off gray vapor, but dense red fog, pulsing with power.
’So they’re stronger versions,’ Stark thought, tightening his grip on his staff.
The monsters howled, hissed, and began to advance.
[Strong Bleeding: 58%]
"Alright then," Stark muttered, "Let’s do this fast."
Bind of Silk!
White silk exploded outward, wrapping around half the monsters before they could react.
Blazing Meteor!
Torrent of Lightning!
The spells chained together almost instantly.
A massive meteor descended from above while bolts of lightning shot through the mist.
-789,360! -789,360! -789,360!
The bound monsters couldn’t move.
The air shook as the meteor slammed into the ground.
BOOM!
A wall of red mist burst outward, vaporizing everything in front of him.
-1,578,720!
The impact alone was enough to wipe out most of them.
Only the [Blood Slimes] and one of the [Blood Mist Wolves] managed to survive, the rest erased completely.
Lightning crashed again.
-1,184,040! -1,184,040! -1,184,040!
And just like that, they were gone.
The bodies dissolved into red vapor, fading into the air like smoke.
’As expected,’ Stark thought, watching them disappear.
Monsters here didn’t leave corpses—just like in the [Land of Mist].
Still, the fight gave him confidence.
Ding!
[You have gained 319 Lives!]
A small grin tugged at his lips.
These things were stronger, yes, but they still weren’t strong enough to stop him.
His damage output was too high, his cooldowns too short.
He could chain-cast endlessly. And so, Stark kept going.
He sprinted through the [Blood Mist], slashing through every monster that dared to appear.
Dozens of them fell under his spells.
The ground trembled again and again as meteors rained down, lightning split the air, and silk tore through the fog.
It was destruction without pause.
Still, even as he cleared everything, the [Strong Bleeding] kept rising.
[Strong Bleeding: 89%...]
He frowned.
’I still don’t get how other players reached the boss,’ he thought. ’Even if they were strong, they couldn’t have killed everything this fast.’
It didn’t make sense. Unless they didn’t fight at all.
’Or maybe the boss came to them.’
He didn’t stop moving. Minutes passed.
The mist got thicker, heavier.
Even with the [Mist Repellant Ring], visibility was dropping fast.
Finally—
[Strong Bleeding: 100%]
The crimson meter hit its limit.
And right after—
Bam!
Stark winced as a sharp sting spread through his chest.
His body started to leak faint red trails: blood.
-300 HP! -300 HP! -300 HP!
He looked down and exhaled.
Every second, 300 HP drained away.
It wasn’t fatal right now, he had more than 100,000 HP, but it would wear him down eventually.
The only way to stop bleeding was to heal, or use an item that countered status effects. He had neither.
’Would’ve been nice if Grace was here,’ he muttered, ’At least she could heal.’
Still, he didn’t panic. The loss was manageable, and thanks to the [Revenant Bell], dying wasn’t even a real threat.
Even if he died, he’d just revive and try again. For now, he needed information.
So he kept walking. But at that moment, something changed.
Thump!
The ground shook faintly.
Thump! Thump!
It was rhythmic, like a heartbeat.
Stark stopped.
’What is that sound?’
The thumping grew louder, echoing through the mist.
And then came the whispers. Faint, unclear, but definitely there.
Dozens of overlapping voices, whispering words in a language he couldn’t understand.
They crawled into his mind like a cold wind.
"...aah... eth... rha... uun..."
Stark froze for a moment. He knew this.
[You are hearing the whispers of the ancient gods.]
’So that’s what it is.’
These whispers were rare and EXTREMELY dangerous.
They weren’t just background noise.
If a player listened to them too long, they started losing control, sometimes even attacking allies.
Not that Stark had to worry about that.
He’d already experienced it before. He focused his mind, tuning out the whispers.
’But it seems like these whispers are faint.’
The [Whispers] he knew about were much louder and could actually affect you almost instantly.
And it didn’t surprise him as he was way too early in [Eternal Soul] to be hearing them.
They would only appear in their true form later.
And as for the reason why they appeared? Nobody knew.
Most people assumed it was because the monsters or zones related to these whispers were linked to the [Ancient Gods].
Still, Stark focused back.
Thump! Thump! Thump!
Something massive was approaching.
The pressure alone was enough to make the mist swirl.
And then, through the red haze, he saw it. A shadow, no, a giant silhouette walking slowly toward him.
Each step it took made the ground vibrate.
When it finally emerged from the fog, Stark’s eyes narrowed.
It was tall, almost five meters, and its body was made entirely of shifting blood mist.
Its face was hidden beneath a mask of bone, and from its back, faint trails of red energy floated upward like flames.
When it spoke, the air trembled.
"The scent of blood... and such immense Spirit..."
The voice was deep, echoing from everywhere at once.
"Incredible. A feast has appeared."
Ding!
[Kaiser, The Spirit Devourer (Level 50)]

chapters.title: Chapter 122: Kaiser, The Spirit Devourer
chapters.content:
Chapter 122: Chapter 122: Kaiser, The Spirit Devourer
[Kaiser, The Spirit Devourer (Level 50)]
[Rank: Mythical (Bloodline Boss)]
[HP: 8,000,000]
[Reward: "Spirit Devourer" Bloodline]
---
That thing had double the HP of the [Guardian of Mist], and it wasn’t surprising, bloodline bosses were simply far stronger than any normal ones.
And as one might notice, it wasn’t just marked as a "Bloodline Boss."
The reward for killing it was also shown right there on the panel, clear and direct.
Kaiser, in addition to his monstrous frame, carried a massive crimson staff in his hands.
After all, he was the SPIRIT Devourer.
That alone made it obvious he was a mage-type opponent, someone who needed Spirit to attack, and thus used magic to crush enemies.
Basically, this was going to be a real duel between mages.
"Yes..." Kaiser’s crimson eyes glowed from behind his skull-like mask.
His deep voice echoed through the red mist.
"Good..."
The bloodline boss slowly raised his staff, and the air began to twist around him.
Boom!
In an instant, the blood mist swirling around Stark was blown away, forming a large empty circle of stone and lifeless dust beneath their feet.
That was their battlefield now. The "arena" had been drawn.
"A feast is only enjoyed," Kaiser said, his tone rising, "when it is proven that I am far superior..."
His bony mask stretched in what looked like a grin.
-300! -300! -300!
Meanwhile, Stark’s health continued to drain away from the [Strong Bleeding] effect.
[HP: 96,200/102,500]
Even while Kaiser spoke, the whispers of the ancient gods filled the area again, echoing in Stark’s head like faint chanting.
He tried to ignore them, but the constant droning was still there, crawling under his skin.
’This is a battle against time,’ Stark thought.
There were too many debuffs in this place, [Strong Bleeding], the faint whispers that could trigger [Insanity], and whatever else this monster could unleash.
And that’s exactly what made [Eternal Soul] so twisted.
As said before, every single zone in this world was technically possible, but many were barely so.
If someone could barely make it through, that still counted as "possible."
It was just that nobody actually could.
’They really made this world sadistic,’ Stark thought, his gaze steady.
Whatever gods designed this wanted players to break at the edge of the possible.
After all, how could any player defeat this thing while bleeding to death, with a chance of losing their mind to whispers, and against an overwhelming enemy, all while only being Level 50?
It was technically possible, sure.
But practically? No one could do it.
And yet, here he was.
’Still,’ Stark thought, ’I can’t help but wonder, if other civilizations faced the same thing, how strong did they become?’
The Calamities had hit all civilizations, wiping most out.
If there were billions and billions of people across countless worlds, then surely some produced monsters like him.
Players who refused to die.
’Well, I won’t know that right now,’ he thought, shaking his head, ’Better focus.’
Every second spent thinking was 300 HP gone.
He needed to finish this fight in under five minutes, or he’d bleed out.
At least now, he had proof that Kaiser didn’t wait for players to clear the monsters.
The boss simply came to them once they were hit with [Strong Bleeding].
That explained how other players "found" him before dying.
Blood Meteor!
Kaiser raised his staff high.
Blood energy gathered in the air above, forming into a dense, pulsating orb that began to fall toward Stark.
’Can’t afford to get hit by anything,’ Stark thought sharply.
’Barrier stays up.
Always.’
He immediately cast his protective skill.
[Unbreakable Magic Barrier]!
It shimmered around him, barely visible, but enough to block catastrophic spells.
Since [Strong Bleeding] targeted the body directly, the barrier couldn’t stop that one, but it would protect him from everything else.
Blazing Meteor!
Boom!
Stark’s own fiery meteor shot up into the air, colliding mid-way with Kaiser’s attack.
The two explosions met in the center of the red mist and detonated violently.
BOOOOOOM!
A wave of heat and pressure burst outward, pushing both back slightly.
"Yes..." Kaiser’s voice came through the fading shockwave.
"Your Spirit is powerful... I shall enjoy feasting on it..."
Then, slowly, Kaiser lifted a hand to his face and pulled his bone mask upward—just enough to reveal what lay beneath.
There were no teeth. No tongue.
Just a black pit of swirling energy, twisting and alive.
And then, that pit moved as though it were breathing in.
Spirit Devourer!
Seeing it, Stark’s eyes narrowed.
He knew instantly that this was one of the Bloodline’s main skills.
Bind of Silk!
He didn’t wait.
White threads shot out from his hand, aiming to bind Kaiser in place before the effect could reach him.
But Kaiser responded almost instantly.
Blood Claws!
His staff pulsed with crimson light, and his other arm twisted, bones stretching into massive blood-forged claws.
He slashed once—
Snap!
—and the silk threads were torn apart as if they were paper.
Then, the air pulsed again.
Ding!
[Spirit Devour: 1%... 4%... 9%...]
Another [Status Meter] appeared in front of Stark’s eyes—and it was filling up fast.
Within a single second, it jumped past ten percent.
A faint crimson thread extended from Stark’s chest, pulled toward Kaiser’s open mouth.
’Spirit Devour...’ Stark thought, ’Of course.’
He realized what was happening.
Kaiser was literally feeding on his [Spirit] stat—his magical strength.
The longer this continued, the weaker Stark would get.
"Now that the feast has begun..." Kaiser’s voice trembled with delight, the whispers of the gods growing louder in the background.
"Let us... end this..."
Blood Ray!
A surge of blood energy condensed at the end of Kaiser’s staff before firing in a straight line.
Boom!
The crimson beam slammed against Stark’s barrier, searing through the red mist.
-10,000!
’Damn.’
That hit was heavy, ten thousand damage in an instant.
This boss wasn’t just strong. His spells were fast.
If Stark had reacted even a little slower, it would’ve pierced through him directly.
But it would take much more to break his barrier though.
He moved again, circling Kaiser, focusing his energy.
Torrent of Lightning!
Blue arcs of electricity burst out of his hands, spreading through the mist.
He aimed three precise bolts at Kaiser.
Zap! Zap! Zap!
-1,184,040! -1,184,040! -1,184,040!
All three shots struck cleanly.
Kaiser staggered slightly, momentarily stunned by the impact, lightning crawling across his black armor.
"The feast fights back," Kaiser growled, but his tone was almost amused, "Yes... it is proof that this is quality..."
Stark didn’t hesitate.
He was already preparing his next spell.
He knew he couldn’t drag this fight.
The longer it lasted, the more [Spirit Devour] would drain from him.
Just a few more hits and he could finish this—
Ding!
[Spirit Devour: 93%... 97%... 100%]
The bar filled completely.
The crimson thread connecting them pulsed once, then Kaiser suddenly inhaled sharply.
Fwshhhh!
Stark felt a painful pull from deep within his chest, like something vital was ripped out.
It wasn’t physical, it was his power.
Ding!
[You have permanently lost 5 Spirit.]
’Hah... I see...’ Stark exhaled sharply, his expression hardening.
Just as he expected, the meter reset instantly.
[Spirit Devour: 0%... 2%... 5%...]
It wasn’t a one-time thing. It was a cycle.
Kaiser could keep doing it as long as he was alive, draining Spirit permanently with every full cast.
That explained everything about the Bloodline’s name, and its terrifying power.
But that also meant one thing for Stark.
If he could somehow win this... If he could claim that Bloodline for himself...
Then he would gain this same power. The ability to steal the Spirit of his enemies.
To grow infinitely stronger the longer he fought.
And in a world like [Eternal Soul], that kind of ability could mean absolute dominance.
The red mist around them pulsed, swirling faster, almost as if the zone itself reacted to the intensity of their magic.
Both of them, Stark and Kaiser, stood facing one another in the clearing, magic surging between them.

chapters.title: Chapter 123: Devouring Spirit, Kaiser’s Second Phase and Death
chapters.content:
Chapter 123: Chapter 123: Devouring Spirit, Kaiser’s Second Phase and Death
"Spirit is the most... powerful... attribute..." Kaiser said, his gaping mouth still widening as he tried to absorb more of Sam’s spirit, "Just... give in..."
"I agree," Stark nodded, his staff pointing forward, "But... I need it more than you do."
Bind of Silk! Thorny Vines of Fate! Sharp Crystals of Death! Piercing Skeletal Spikes!
Stark unleashed every spell he could think of in one breath, all flying toward Kaiser.
Threads of white silk burst from his staff, twisting like serpents.
Vines covered in dark thorns shot from the ground, followed by crystal shards gleaming with deathly energy.
And underneath it all, the ground rumbled as something far more dangerous waited to emerge.
Kaiser, of course, retaliated immediately.
Blood Claws! Blood Immunity!
He slashed through the silk like it was nothing, crimson light bursting from his claws.
The vines were torn apart just as easily, their green thorns falling to dust.
Then, a blood-red barrier appeared around him, shimmering with life energy and blocking the five crystals of death that followed.
The shards shattered against it harmlessly.
"Just let yourself... be taken..." Kaiser’s mouth grew even wider, his voice echoing across the dark chamber.
"You cannot... win—"
He didn’t finish his sentence.
The ground exploded beneath him.
Fifteen skeletal spikes erupted from below, piercing upward with deadly precision.
They came without warning, bursting through the cracked tiles and crimson mist.
That was Kaiser’s mistake, assuming the only danger came from what he could see.
He saw the silk. He saw the vines. He saw the crystals.
But the spikes? They were hidden, cast after everything else, waiting underground.
Swash!
Ten out of the fifteen spikes hit their mark, stabbing through Kaiser’s body.
He didn’t flinch. Blood didn’t even spill.
But the numbers told the story.
-72,000! -72,000! -72,000!
Each strike dealt massive damage, cutting deep into his health bar.
Yet Kaiser’s expression, or whatever could be called a face behind that bone mask, remained unchanged.
His jaw was still open, still trying to suck away Stark’s spirit.
The [Status Meter] above Stark’s head showed his spirit being drained at a steady pace.
But before Kaiser could react—
Blazing Meteor!
The spell name echoed through the clearing as a massive fireball descended from above.
Kaiser didn’t even have time to lift his staff.
BOOM!
The impact shook the ground.
Fire roared through the ruins, throwing chunks of bone and stone everywhere.
-1,576,320!
The number flashed across the screen, the largest yet.
Kaiser actually stumbled back for the first time, forced to close his mouth from the pressure.
Ding!
["Spirit Devour" has stopped.]
"Oh?" Stark muttered, lowering his staff slightly.
It seemed closing his mouth also ended the spirit-draining effect.
The faint red line connecting Stark and Kaiser vanished instantly, along with the draining pressure.
[Kaiser, Spirit Devourer: 2,151,560/8,000,000]
Only about two million HP left. Two or three more solid spells and Stark could finish it.
’This is my chance.’
He raised his staff again, readying [Elemental Spears]—
But Kaiser suddenly gripped his staff tighter.
His other hand, the one ending in long blood-colored claws, moved upward.
And—
SLASH!
He slashed his own face.
The sound of tearing bone echoed through the place.
The mask split cleanly in half and fell, hitting the floor with a sharp crack.
Behind it wasn’t a face. It was simply a mouth, a massive, horrifying mouth that stretched across his entire head.
"..." Stark didn’t react much, ’Second phase.’
It wasn’t surprising. Bloodline bosses almost always had at least two phases, sometimes three.
That was what made them terrifying, the sudden shift in power, the unpredictable attacks.
He just hadn’t expected the transformation to happen this early.
Kaiser’s body shuddered.
He slowly rose again, his new mouth opening wider than before.
"I... will..." he began, but the words melted into a gurgle as his jaw expanded unnaturally.
Fwish!
[Strong Spirit Devour: 7%... 16%... 23%...]
"Damn," Stark muttered, "this ain’t looking good."
The status meter filled much faster than before, and on top of that, Kaiser’s strength spiked.
The crimson mist surrounding the area began to flow into his mouth, fueling him with energy.
His body pulsed with dark red light, and the air itself seemed heavier. Then Kaiser attacked.
Blood Meteor! Blood Spikes!
A crimson meteor crashed from above, glowing like molten rock.
Stark jumped aside just in time to avoid it, but the ground shook violently on impact.
Before he could recover, spikes erupted from below, each dripping with blood.
They slammed into his [Unbreakable Magic Barrier], cracking it like glass.
’He’s copying me?’ Stark thought, dodging sideways as more spikes shot from the ground.
Ding!
[You have permanently lost 5 Spirit.]
He ignored the notification.
The [Status Meter] above him reset to zero, only to begin rising again just as quickly.
Kaiser could keep draining him forever if he didn’t stop him soon.
And worse, Stark was still bleeding.
[Strong Bleeding] ticked away at his health, cutting his HP by half already.
He didn’t have long left.
Mist Illusion!
Kaiser raised his hands, and crimson mist filled the entire clearing.
The world turned red.
Figures began appearing all around Stark, identical copies of Kaiser, each radiating killing intent.
"I... will... win..."
Torrent of Lightning!
Bolts of electricity shot from Stark’s staff, piercing through three of the illusions.
They vanished instantly, bursting into smoke. But there were still more.
’Enough,’ Stark thought, his patience gone.
He stopped retreating. His grip tightened on his staff.
’All or nothing.’
Instead of backing away, he charged forward, full speed, straight at Kaiser.
With his high Agility and all his boosts active, Stark moved like a blur.
The clones all turned toward him, raising their staves.
Thorny Vines of Fate!
Dozens of vines burst from the ground, tearing through the illusions and shredding them one by one.
’They can’t fight back,’ Stark realized as he ran, ’Only the real one can attack.’
Sure enough, the true Kaiser swung his claws to block the vines, cutting them apart.
"Die...!" Kaiser growled.
He lifted his staff again.
Blood Spikes! Mist Spears!
Spikes burst from the ground, forcing Stark to leap sideways mid-run.
A moment later, several crimson spears of condensed mist shot toward him.
He dodged most, but a few still hit, cutting deep.
Crack!
His [Unbreakable Magic Barrier] shattered completely.
"Foolish..." Kaiser’s voice echoed.
He raised his claws high.
"Die... and be devoured..."
He was ready to cleave Stark apart.
Even without spells, those claws could tear through armor and bone. But Stark grinned.
’Close enough.’
He pointed his staff upward.
Elemental Spears!
Five magic circles appeared around him, glowing bright orange.
Normally, he’d be able to choose elements depending on the enemy, but this time, he didn’t waste time thinking.
’All fire.’
The [Mist] attribute clearly wouldn’t work, and the others were uncertain.
The reason he chose [Fire] instead of the [Water] and [Earth] was because [Blazing Meteor] worked before, so why would he risk it?
Fwish!
Five fire spears formed and shot forward instantly.
"Huh—"
Boom! Boom! Boom!
Each hit dead center, exploding in bursts of flame that lit up the whole room.
-1,573,920! -1,573,920! -1,573,920!
Each spear dealt as much damage as [Blazing Meteor].
Five of them hit almost simultaneously, impossible to dodge, impossible to counter at this range.
Kaiser staggered backward, his body shaking violently as his HP bar drained completely.
[Kaiser, Spirit Devourer: 0/8,000,000]
For a moment, time seemed to stop.
Then Kaiser froze in place, the crimson light around his figure fading out.
’I win,’ Stark thought, lowering his staff, a grin forming on his face.

chapters.title: Chapter 124: Tier-3 Mage of Oblivion, New Passive and Blood Staff
chapters.content:
Chapter 124: Chapter 124: Tier-3 Mage of Oblivion, New Passive and Blood Staff
Kaiser stayed still for a few seconds before his massive body finally lost balance and fell to the ground, lifeless.
His mouth remained open, the jagged teeth glinting faintly in the dark, but the hunger behind them was gone.
The devouring had stopped. No spirit, no power, nothing left to take.
The fight was truly over.
Since [Bloodline Bosses] were unique in [Eternal Soul], death was the end for them.
They didn’t respawn, didn’t reappear. Once they were gone, they were gone for good.
And now, Kaiser was truly dead.
As his corpse crashed to the cracked stone floor, a heavy shockwave burst outward.
The impact sent waves of air through the misted clearing, shaking the ruins around them.
A heartbeat later, all of the [Blood Mist] that had covered the entire zone vanished.
It was gone in an instant.
The crimson haze that had filled every corner, every crack, every breath of this place — wiped away as if it had never existed.
Meaning, of course, that Kaiser had been the one maintaining it all along.
And not just that.
The whispers, the eerie, quiet murmurs of ancient gods that had echoed faintly through the fog, disappeared too.
The moment Kaiser’s life ended, so did every trace of the presence he had summoned.
Silence filled the area.
Stark glanced around. The emptiness of the zone made the victory feel heavier somehow.
He didn’t receive any experience from killing Kaiser, which honestly annoyed him.
A boss like that? The experience points would have been massive.
But still...
Ding!
---
[You have gained 30 Evolution Points!]
[You have gained 3,500 Lives!]
Hand of Avarice!
[You have gained 29 Evolution Points!]
[You have gained 3,250 Lives!]
---
The notifications stacked up one after another, the white text flashing across his vision.
No items dropped when Kaiser fell, but after using [Hand of Avarice], something shimmered faintly beside the corpse.
’Nice,’ Stark thought, eyes narrowing in anticipation as he stepped closer.
But before he could take another step, more notifications appeared.
Ding!
[Global Announcement: Congratulations to player "Oblivion" for being the first player to defeat a bloodline boss.]
[You have gained 25 Prestige Points!]
’Damn,’ Stark sighed.
Another global announcement.
Another moment where every single player in the game saw his name flash across their screens.
The reaction was predictable, surprise at first, then the usual disbelief, then acceptance.
By now, everyone knew "Oblivion."
They were used to it. Used to seeing his name at the top.
Used to him doing things that no one else even tried to attempt.
And the funniest part? His reputation wasn’t even bad.
He didn’t kill for fun. He killed those who hunted other players.
He sold high-tier gear instead of hoarding it.
Even those who wanted to hate him couldn’t find a reason beyond "he’s too strong."
Still, Stark didn’t care much for fame.
He ignored the flashing announcement and focused on the panels that actually mattered.
Ding!
---
[You have completed your Tier-3 Advancement Task: Clear the "Blood Mist" zone by defeating its boss, "Kaiser, The Spirit Devourer."]
[Rating: SSS]
---
’Heh,’ Stark smirked.
He hadn’t completely dominated the fight like he expected, but a win was a win.
And an SSS rating meant the system agreed. Maybe it counted the difficulty.
Maybe it just recognized that he managed to do something few could.
Either way, it was enough.
Ding!
[Your level has been unlocked and you may now gain experience points.]
[Level: 50 (0 / 700,000)]
’Nice.’
The experience curve was getting ridiculous.
Seven hundred thousand points just for one level.
But Stark was used to it. Grinding was part of the game.
Numbers didn’t scare him. And there was something else.
Ding!
[You have fulfilled the condition for your "Class Advancement."]
"Here we go," Stark grinned.
"Guess I’ll check this out before anything else."
The next panels would show the reward from Kaiser, something entirely new, but before that, checking his class felt more fitting.
After all, this was the moment he’d been working toward.
Ding!
[Your "Mage of Oblivion" class has evolved!]
[Tier: 2 → 3]
He opened the new class panel immediately.
---
[Mage of Oblivion (Unique Hidden Class)]
[Tier: 3]
[Class Passive #1: All your magic damage is multiplied by 20 → 25.]
[Class Passive #2: Your MP recovery is multiplied by 20 → 25.]
[Class Passive #3: All your spells’ cooldowns are reduced by half.]
[Class Passive #4 (New): Your magic cannot be silenced or disrupted by anything, no matter what.]
---
’Damn.’
That last passive wasn’t flashy, but it was powerful in its own way.
Stark knew how often battles turned because a mage’s spell got interrupted.
When focus broke, when pain hit, when an enemy’s skill disrupted concentration, casting became impossible.
He’d experienced it many times before.
It was one of the most frustrating things for any mage.
But now? That weakness was gone.
Even if he was surrounded. Even if monsters tore through him from every direction.
Even if he was bleeding, burning or blinded, his magic would still fire.
His spells would never stop.
It wasn’t the kind of passive that screamed strength, but in the right fight, it was game-changing.
And with that, he was stronger.
His damage had gone up, his mana recovery too, even if the second one didn’t matter much right now.
Every improvement counted. He closed the panel, the faint smirk still on his lips.
Also, the advancement fully healed him, removing the [Strong Bleeding] effect. He was back to full strength.
Now there was just one thing left to do, check the item Kaiser had dropped.
Stark crouched beside the corpse. Something long and sleek glimmered faintly in the fading light.
When he picked it up and inspected it, his eyes widened slightly.
’No way.’
---
[Blood Staff (Mythical): +2,700 Spirit. Requirement: Level 50.]
[Blood Resistance (Passive): Prevents your skin from bleeding via "Status Effects."]
---
’Damn.’
The passive would’ve been a lifesaver earlier in the fight, but it was still an incredible bonus to have now.
More importantly, the spirit stat boost was massive.
’+2,700 Spirit.’
That kind of power increase wasn’t common, not even close.
It pushed his damage far beyond his old numbers.
At first, Stark thought he’d have trouble choosing between this new staff and his [Divine Staff].
The divine one had a solid 20% damage increase, hard to give up.
But with that much spirit added directly, the choice was obvious.
And later, when he could use [Heart of Sanctuary], the weapon would grow even stronger.
"Thanks for everything," Stark said quietly to the [Divine Staff] before storing it in his inventory.
"I’ll find you a new owner."
Grace wouldn’t need it.
She didn’t rely on raw attack damage, and this kind of weapon would be wasted on her.
Someone else could make better use of it.
He didn’t think too hard about it though.
There’d be time for that later.
The moment he equipped the [Blood Staff], the difference was immediate.
